IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p19/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p19/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p19/r3.claim: In discussing the reading “وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها,” Ibn Jinnī addresses stylistic ordering and its relation to the speaker’s intent.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p19/r3.anchor: وفي الاحتجاج لقراءة: "وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها"4

DAMGHANI:v1p320/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p320/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p320/r11.claim: ʿArḍ can mean presenting something to someone; Ṣād is parallel.
DAMGHANI:v1p320/r11.anchor: العرض من قولك عرضته على فلان قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r1.claim: The angels trusted their many acts of obedience and presumed sinlessness, so they magnified themselves and belittled Adam when questioning his appointment as vicegerent.
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r1.anchor: لما نظروا إلى كثرة طاعتهم واستعداد عصمتهم ونظروا إلى نتائج الصفات النفسانية استعظموا أنفسهم واستصغروا آدم وذريته

BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r2.claim: Israelites made the same entitlement argument against Talut; God answered that kingship rests on divine choice and superiority in knowledge and physique, not wealth.
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r2.anchor: قالوا أنى يكون له الملك علينا ونحن أحق بالملك منه

BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r3.claim: God's answer to the angels is expanded by Adam's election, teaching him the names, and creating him with His hands: succession is bestowed by God, not earned through abundant worship.
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r3.anchor: ليعلموا أن استعداد ملك الخلافة واستحقاقها ليس بكثرة الطاعات

BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r4.claim: After the angels boasted, God favored Adam with knowledge of the names; their prostration showed that God needs no service and that grace belongs to Him.
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r4.anchor: فبتفاخرهم على آدم صاروا ساجدين له ليعلموا أن الحق تعالى مستغن عن طاعتهم

BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r5.claim: God's knowledge of Adam also includes hidden faults unknown to angels: bodily dispositions shared with animals and vices produced by the commanding self when the spirit follows it without the discipline of sacred law.
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r5.anchor: له رذائل وأوصاف مذمومة لا يعلمها الملائكة لأنهم لا يعلمون منه أوصافا مذمومة هي من نتائج قالبه

BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r6.claim: Those soul-born faults include vanity, ostentation, seeking reputation, envy, preferring worldly life, innovation, deviation, and holding evil opinions.
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r6.anchor: من العجب والرياء والسمعة والحسد واشتراء الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة والابتداع

BURSEVI:v1p77/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p77/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
BURSEVI:v1p77/r1.claim: Wahb reports that God told the earth He would make a vicegerent from it; some descendants would enter Paradise and others Hell, prompting the earth to protest that it would produce someone destined for the Fire.
BURSEVI:v1p77/r1.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه : لما أراد الله أن يخلق آدم

BURSEVI:v1p77/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p77/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
BURSEVI:v1p77/r2.claim: The earth wept at this prospect, and springs burst from it and continued to flow until the Day of Resurrection.
BURSEVI:v1p77/r2.anchor: فبكت فانفجرت منها العيون إلى يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v1p77/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p77/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p77/r3.claim: Gabriel was sent to gather soil from the earth's four corners and varieties, but withdrew after it appealed to God; a Persian couplet notes that approaching a ruler brings many benefits but also danger.
BURSEVI:v1p77/r3.anchor: فرجع جبريل عليه السلام إلى مكانه ولم يأخذ منها شيئا

BURSEVI:v1p77/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p77/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p77/r4.claim: Michael and then Israfil received the same plea from the earth and each returned without taking soil.
BURSEVI:v1p77/r4.anchor: فأرسل الله ميكائيل عليه السلام فلما انتهى إليها قالت الأرض له كما قالت لجبريل

BURSEVI:v1p77/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p77/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p77/r5.claim: The Persian couplet says there are abundant benefits in approaching a ruler, but safety lies in staying away from him.
BURSEVI:v1p77/r5.anchor: بدريا در منافع بيشمارست اكرخوا هي سلامت در كنارست

BURSEVI:v1p77/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p77/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p77/r6.claim: The Angel of Death invoked God's authority, took a handful from the earth's four corners, and gathered about forty cubits of soil; the soil's differing colors and qualities account for human diversity.
BURSEVI:v1p77/r6.anchor: فقبض قبضة من وجه الأرض مقدار أربعين ذراعا من زواياها الأربع

BURSEVI:v1p77/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p77/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p77/r7.claim: Each particle in the gathered handful became the origin of a human body, and after death a person is buried where that soil was taken.
BURSEVI:v1p77/r7.anchor: فصار كل ذرة من تلك القبضة أصل بدن للإنسان فإذا مات يدفن في الموضع الذي أخذت منه

BURSEVI:v1p77/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p77/r8.speaker: روضة العلماء
BURSEVI:v1p77/r8.claim: A report says the earth complained that soil had been taken from it; God promised to return something better and purer, which the author links to embalming the dead with musk and ghaliya.
BURSEVI:v1p77/r8.anchor: قال في "روضة العلماء" : فشكت الأرض إلى الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r1.speaker: كشف الكنوز
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r1.claim: Kashf al-kunuz reports broad scholarly agreement that all names were divinely taught: God created in Adam necessary knowledge of words and the meanings they denote.
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r1.anchor: قال في "كشف الكنوز" اتفق جم غفير من أهل العلم

BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r2.speaker: خبر
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r2.claim: A report says God placed the secrets of letters in Adam alone; letters emerged on his tongue in many languages and were formed into images and shapes for him.
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r2.anchor: وفي الخبر لما خلق الله آدم بث فيه أسرار الأحرف ولم يبث في أحد من الملائكة

BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r3.speaker: خبر
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r3.claim: A report says Adam learned seven hundred thousand languages, lost all but Arabic after eating from the tree, then recovered them when chosen as a prophet; speaking his descendants' languages was among his miracles.
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r3.anchor: وفي الخبر علمه سبعمائة ألف لغة فلما وقع في أكل الشجرة سلب اللغات إلا العربية

BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r4.claim: Some exegetes say Adam learned a thousand trades and taught his children to seek worldly livelihood through crafts rather than religion; they list Adam as farmer, Noah as carpenter, Idris as tailor, Salih as merchant, David as armorer, Solomon as basket maker, and several prophets as shepherds.
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r4.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين : علم الله آدم ألف حرفة

BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r5.speaker: حديث
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r5.claim: A report says the best men's work is tailoring and the best women's work is spinning; the text also says Muhammad did much of the household tailoring.
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث "عمل الأبرار من الرجال الخياطة وعمل الأبرار من النساء الغزل"

BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r6.claim: The comprehensive wording includes names of creatures and names of God; if knowledge of creaturely names warrants the angels' prostration, knowledge of God's names warrants it even more.
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r6.anchor: فكما علمه أسماء المخلوقات علمه أسماء الحق تعالى

BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r7.claim: The masculine plural pronoun in the account of displaying the names is used because rational beings occur among the named things and take grammatical precedence.
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r7.anchor: وإنما ذكر الضمير لأن في المسميات العقلاء فغلبهم

BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r8.claim: To display something is to show it to another so that the viewer can recognize its condition.
BURSEVI:v1p78#2/r8.anchor: والعرض إظهار الشيء للغير ليعرف العارض منه حاله

BURSEVI:v1p79/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79/r1.speaker: حديث
BURSEVI:v1p79/r1.claim: A report says God displayed the named beings in forms as small as particles of dust.

BURSEVI:v1p79/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79/r2.claim: Possibly God displayed one representative from each kind so the angels could learn the states and rules of the rest from it.
BURSEVI:v1p79/r2.anchor: ولعله عز وجل عرض عليهم من أفراد كل نوع ما يصلح أن يكون أنموذجا

BURSEVI:v1p79/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79/r3.claim: Teaching and displaying the names honored and elected Adam, disclosed hidden knowledge through a chosen servant, prevented angels and others from claiming superior knowledge, and manifested God's encompassing mercy.
BURSEVI:v1p79/r3.anchor: والحكمة في التعليم والعرض تشريف آدم واصطفاؤه وإظهاره الأسرار والعلوم المكنونة

BURSEVI:v1p79/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79/r4.claim: The command to inform God was meant to rebuke and disable the angels, not to obtain an answer; such an impossible command can expose incapacity, as with image makers told to revive their creations on Judgment Day.
BURSEVI:v1p79/r4.anchor: تبكيتا وتعجيزا للملائكة وخطاب التعجيز جائز وهو الأمر بإتيان الشيء ولم يكن إتيانه مرادا

BURSEVI:v1p79/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79/r5.claim: The challenge asks for the names of the existing beings and tests the angels' claim that they deserved vicegerency more than God's chosen appointee.
BURSEVI:v1p79/r5.anchor: في زعمكم أنكم أحقاء بالخلافة ممن استخلفته كما ينبىء عنه مقالكم

BURSEVI:v1p79/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79/r6.claim: The verse shows that, after knowledge of divine unity, learning language is among the most valuable sciences, since God demonstrated Adam's superiority through it.
BURSEVI:v1p79/r6.anchor: هذه الآية دليل على أن أولى الأشياء بعد علم التوحيد تعلم علم اللغة

BURSEVI:v1p79/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79/r7.claim: Anyone claiming superiority must supply evidence: the angels were asked for proof, and their speculation about unseen corruption was answered by their ignorance of names of what they could actually see.
BURSEVI:v1p79/r7.anchor: دلت أيضا على أن المدعي يطالب بالحجة فإن الملائكة ادعوا الفضل فطولبوا بالبرهان

BURSEVI:v1p79/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79/r8.claim: The passage rebukes claimants and knowers alike: if people cannot name what they see, they should not presume to judge what they cannot see; knowledge should lead to love, and love to obedience.
BURSEVI:v1p79/r8.anchor: لا تعلمون أسماء ما تعاينون فكيف تتكلمون في فساد من لا تعاينون

BURSEVI:v1p79/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79/r9.speaker: أبو بكر الواسطي
BURSEVI:v1p79/r9.claim: Al-Wasiti says knowing God necessarily leads to loving Him, love to remembering Him, remembrance to tasting its sweetness, and that sweetness makes one turn away from other things.
BURSEVI:v1p79/r9.anchor: قال أبو بكر الواسطي : من المحال أن يعرفه العبد ثم لا يحبه

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r14.claim: The apparent view is that God coined the names and inscribed or inspired them in Adam; another possibility is that Adam received a special capacity to coin and use names as needed.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r14.anchor: bir taraftan da Âdem’e bütün o isimleri tâlim etti. Ya o esmâyı Allah kendi vaz‘edip Âdem’in rûhuna nakş u ilham etti

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r15.claim: Adam did not learn every primordial word instantaneously; he learned language gradually through an endowed capacity under nurture.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r15.anchor: Hazret-i Âdem’in asl-ı lisân olan isimleri birdenbire bir i‘lâm

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r16.claim: Adam’s attributes represent humanity’s original nature: as the first human, he transmitted the species’ essential faculties to humankind.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r16.anchor: nev‘-i beşerin mâhiyet ve fıtrat-ı ûlâsı demektir. Zira Âdem nev‘in ilk ferdidir

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r17.claim: The exegetical question is whether ‘all’ means every name or a defined set, and whether the article marks exhaustive generality or a known set.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r17.anchor: Bu isimler nedir ve كُلَّهَا istiğrâkının derece-i şümûlü ne kadardır?

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r18.speaker: ضحاك عن ابن عباس
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r18.claim: One universal-names view says Adam learned names used for human understanding, including people, animals, earth, sea, mountains, and donkeys.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r18.anchor:
cebel, himar vesâire hepsi (İbn Ab-
bas’tan Dahhâk)

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r19.speaker: Mücâhid
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r19.claim: Mujahid says Adam learned the names of the crow, dove, and everything.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r19.anchor: gurab, hamame ve her şeyin ismi (Mücâhid)

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r20.speaker: Saîd b. Cübeyr
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r20.claim: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr says Adam learned every name, down to camel, cow, and sheep.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r20.anchor: her şeyin ismi, ba‘îr, bakara, şâte varıncaya kadar (Saîd b. Cübeyr)

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r21.speaker: İbn Abbas’tan Saîd b. Ma‘bed
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r21.claim: Sa‘id ibn Ma‘bad’s report from Ibn Abbas extends the names to demonstratives such as ‘this’ and ‘that’ and even ‘hadath.’
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r21.anchor:
“şu”, “bu”, “hades” bile (İbn Abbas’tan Saîd b. Ma‘-
bed)

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r22.speaker: Katâde
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r22.claim: Qatada says Adam learned names and classes of created kinds, identifying things as ‘this mountain’ or ‘this sea’ and describing their properties.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r22.anchor: her sınıf halkın ismi ve cinsine ircâ‘ı, “şu cebel”, “bu deniz”, “şu şöyle” diye her şeyin ismi (Katâde)

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r23.claim: The universal view amounts to the vocabularies underlying all languages; some extend it to names of everything that would exist through the Resurrection.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r23.anchor: Bunların hâsılı, bütün elsinenin aslı olan lügātın hepsi oluyor

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r24.speaker: Rebî‘ ve daha diğerleri
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r24.claim: Another interpretation restricts the names to those of the angels.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r1.speaker: İbn Zeyd
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r1.claim: A third interpretation says the names are those of Adam’s descendants; Ibn Wahb, Yunus ibn Abd al-A‘la, and others also transmit this view.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r2.claim: The pronoun ‘them’ points to rational beings and favors descendants’ names; some exegetes combine descendants and angels, while the pronoun also rules out God’s names.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r2.anchor: bu kârineye nazaran bazı müfessirîn hem esmâ-i melâikeye ve hem esmâ-i zürriyete şümûlünü

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes the names as properties of things or mental forms assembled from them, which would be knowledge or inner speech rather than ordinary language.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r3.anchor: Esmâdan murad lisan değil, havâss-ı eşyâ, ta‘bîr-i âharla o havâstan müteşekkil suver-i ilmiyedir

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r4.claim: What is certain is that Adam received language teaching and was endowed with knowledge and speech; language matters to the caliphate.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r4.anchor: burada kat‘î olan nokta Hazret-i Âdem’e az veya çok ta’lîm-i lisân edilmiş

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r5.claim: Human linguistic diversity and development owe their foundation to Adam’s innate naming capacity, while knowledge and logic belong essentially to human nature.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r5.anchor: İlim ve mantık hâssası bu suretle nev‘-i insânînin fıtrat-ı asliyesinde dâhil zâtiyyâttan bulunmuş

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r6.claim: Speech is part of the human spirit’s essence; Adam became fully human through knowledge and speech, and language is not merely incidental.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r6.anchor: Bu suretle kuvve-i kelâmiye rûh-i insânînin mâhiyetinden bir cüz teşkil etmiştir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r7.claim: He rejects those who define human essence by sin while treating knowledge and speech as accidents, saying they misunderstand humanity.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r7.anchor: Masiyeti insanın zâtîsi sayıp da sıfat-ı ilmi ve sıfat-ı kelâmı araziyyâttan saymak isteyenler insanı bilememişlerdir

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r8.claim: If teaching preceded the breathing of spirit, Adam received speech and naming capacity and coined names gradually by divine enablement; if concurrent or later, God taught names gradually by inspiration or necessary knowledge.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r8.anchor: veya sonra ise vâzı‘-ı esmâ, Allah teâlâ’dır.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r9.claim: These alternatives correspond to the legal-theoretical dispute about the origin of language; the apparent reading is actual teaching and its prior determination.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r9.anchor: Müfessirînce tâlim böyle iki suretle de tevil edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r10.claim: Language is the cause of Adam’s appointment as caliph, not its result.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r10.anchor: Yani lisan, Âdem’in eser-i hilâfeti değil, sebeb-i hilâfetidir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r11.claim: The pronoun ‘them’ is grammatically marked for rational beings, favoring descendants as referents; all names may have been taught while only these referents were presented.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r11.anchor: arz olunan şeylerin zevi’l-‘ukūl olduğunu göstermekte zâhirdir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r12.claim: The most apparent referents are descendants who would succeed Adam, though this seems difficult because Eve and the descendants were not yet created in the narrative.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r12.anchor: en zâhir mâna bu müsemmeyâtın Hazret-i Âdem’e halef olacak olan zürriyetleri olmasıdır.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r13.claim: A well-known hadith explains that descendants were shown to angels as tiny particles, fine ants, or microbes; ‘descendants’ derives from ‘particles.’

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r14.claim: The hadith implies all future humanity existed in Adam as seedlike particles representing his descendants.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r14.anchor: Bu hadis bunların o zaman Âdem’de henüz tohum hâlinde, yani istikbalde bütün Benî Âdem’i temsil eden ilk

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r15.claim: Alternatively, before earthly descent Adam’s rational soul or subtle ethereal body could contain successive descendant forms; their presentation would then be intellectual, not sensory.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r15.anchor: Bu surette melâikeye arz, arz-ı hissî değil, arz-ı ilmî ve hakīkī olur.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r16.claim: The true referents of names are cognitive forms; Adam received knowledge especially of descendants as well as their names and linguistic forms, which angels lacked.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r16.anchor: Fi’l-vâki‘isimlerin asıl medlûlâtı eşyânın suver-i ilmiyesidir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r17.claim: This discussion raises whether knowledge is innate or acquired, a question he will explain elsewhere.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r17.anchor: Burada bilfiil ilmin fıtriyeti veya ‘adem-i fıtriyeti meselesi vardır

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r18.claim: God’s challenge tests angels’ implied claim to succession by asking them to identify the beings and their names if they are correct.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r18.anchor: haydi siz bi’l-işâre ifade etmek istediğiniz hilâfete liyâkatiniz îmasında sâdık yani musîb iseniz

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r19.claim: Administration and justice require knowing subjects, their capacities and rights, and identifying them by name even when absent.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r19.anchor: tasarruf, tedbir, ikāme-i ma‘delet bunların müte‘allaklarını, isti‘dadlarının mertebelerini

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r20.claim: Speech and truthful articulation have distinctive intrinsic value beyond knowledge, and legal rulings cannot be carried out without them.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r20.anchor: sıfat-ı ilimden daha fazla bir hususiyet ve meziyet ifade eden sıfat-ı kelâmın, kuvve-i lisâniyenin

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r3.claim: If the names mean all names, angels lack speech; if they mean descendants’ names, that need not prevent speech, so another wisdom must explain their lack of fitness.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r3.anchor: eğer esmâ-i zürriyet ise, diğer esmâyı men‘etmeyeceğinden sıfat-ı kelâma mâni‘olmaz

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r5.claim: Angels learn names through Adam’s report; knowledge is direct disclosure of reality, while speech conveys it indirectly through signs or deputies.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r6.claim: Knowledge is a direct manifestation of reality; speech is its derivative manifestation through an indicator or sign.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r6.anchor: asıl ilim hakikatin bizzat bir tecellîsi ve bir inkişâf-ı mahsûsudur. Kelâm da ilmin bir tecellîsi

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r7.claim: A name is a thing, but is a name by serving as a sign or proof that brings something else to mind.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r7.anchor: İsimde kelâmda ise o vechin ancak bir nâibi vardır.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r8.claim: Caliphate suits the representative role of names and speech, first bestowed on Adam; human sciences depend on derivative verbal forms and therefore contain shadowlike concepts.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r8.anchor: hilâfete liyâkat, esmâ ve kelâmdaki bu ma‘nâ-yı niyâbet ile mütenâsib olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r12.claim: Human susceptibility to error and compounded ignorance is tied to speech’s representative nature, through which Satan can mislead.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r12.anchor: Beşeriyetin hata ve cehl-i mürekkeb kabiliyeti de kendilerindeki kelâm sıfatı

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r13.claim: Speech is essentially ordered to truth, yet incidental effects can make it false; people may identify words with knowledge and truth and mistake concepts for reality.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r13.anchor: Gerçi kelâm esasen ilm-i hakka ve sıdka mevzû‘dur ve onun nâibidir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r14.claim: When representation is treated as original and people stop seeking truth beyond it, human evil begins.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r14.anchor: Haslet-i niyâbet, bir asalet telakkī edilir. Ve o zaman insanlığın bütün şerr ü fesâdı başlar.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r15.claim: God gave Adam both knowledge and speech, taught him the names, and tested his fitness before the angels.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r15.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak fıtrat-ı Âdem’i kendi sıfâtından

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r17.claim: Arabic derivations from ‘udma’ or ‘earth’s surface’ are reported, but the preferred view of Zamakhshari, Baydawi, and Abu al-Su‘ud is a non-Arabic origin on the fa‘al pattern.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r17.anchor: Zemahşerî, Beyzâvî, Ebussuud vesâire gibi muhakkikīnin muhtârı budur.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r18.speaker: İmam Şa‘bî
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r18.claim: Imam Sha‘bi holds that Adam is Hebrew, like Azer or A‘zar, and says Syriac ‘adam’ means soil.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r19.claim: Some derive Adam from Syriac ‘hatam,’ which would make the Turkish pronunciation ‘adam’ more original.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r19.anchor: Bazıları da bunun aslı “hâtam” vezninde Süryânî olduğuna zâhib olmuşlardır

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r20.claim: Whether Arabic or foreign, Adam is certainly a proper name rather than a generic noun and is indeclinable for its grammatical reasons.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r20.anchor: Ve her iki takdirde bir ism-i cins olmayıp ism-i ‘alem olduğu muhakkaktır.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r21.claim: Used generically like ‘human’ or ‘person,’ Adam has plural ‘avadim’ and a declinable singular meaning one Adamite; generic nouns begin by generalizing a proper name, and singularity precedes multitude.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r21.anchor: “Âdem”; “beşer”, “insan” gibi ism-i cins makamında kullanılacak olursa

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r22.claim: Hebrew and Syriac have variant forms; Sabaean ‘Aadhimun’ seems related, and Adam is said to have different names among peoples.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r22.anchor: Her hâlde Arabîden mâ‘adâ İbrânî ve Süryânîde bu ismin muhtelif lehçeleri mevcut olduğu anlaşılıyor.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r23.speaker: Şehristânî
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r23.claim: Shahrastani says a Magian Kuyumers tradition identifies Kayumers as Adam; Indian and Persian histories also report this, though other historians disagree.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r23.anchor: Şehristânî’nin Milel ü Nihâl’de beyânına göre Mecûstan Küyumresiye taifesi “Keyûmers Âdem’dir” derler.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r24.speaker: İbnü’l-Esîr
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r24.claim: Ibn al-Athir records in al-Kamil that the Magians call Jeyumers Adam.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r24.anchor: İbnü’l-Esîr dahi Kâmil’inde “Mecûsun Ceyumers dediği Hazret-i Âdem’dir” diye zikreder.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r25.claim: The most apparent view is that Adam is a word belonging to humanity’s first language.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r25.anchor: En zâhiri, Âdem ismi beşerin ilk lisânına ait bir kelime olmak üzere ahz edilmek iktizâ edecektir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r5.claim: The immediate purpose is specifically to establish and manifest the wisdom and causes of Adam's fitness for vicegerency, which the angels had not grasped.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r5.anchor: bilhassa [317] Âdem aleyhisselâm’da tahakkuk eden devâ‘î-i hilâfeti takrir ve izhâr-ı hikmet ü kudrettir

ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r7.claim: God announced Adam's vicegerency to the angels summarily, as if consulting them, then trained Adam through teaching the names.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r7.anchor: melâikesine istişare eder gibi icmâlen tebliğ etmiş

ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r8.claim: God tested Adam and the angels together, exposed the angels' inability, proved Adam's fitness in practice, and prepared them to submit to him.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r8.anchor: geçirip melaikeye izhâr-ı acz ve ona bilfiil isbât-ı ehliyet ettirmiş

ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r9.claim: The story clearly and subtly reveals how divine lordship manifests, recalls inward blessings embedded in human nature, and leads into the later direct-address warning.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r9.anchor: rubûbiyyet-i ilâhiyenin tarz-ı tecellîsi büyük bir vuzuh ve pek ince bir üslup ile ifham edilerek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r1.claim: God's implicit explanation of why Adam was created rested on faith and was already enough to convince the angels.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r1.anchor: üstü kapalı ve doğrulanması inanca dayalı olan açıklama melekleri ikna için yeterli idi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r2.claim: God rejected knowledge and faith acquired only by trusting another's report (taqlid) as sufficient, and staged a test to direct humanity toward observation, experience, and thought.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r2.anchor: yüce Allah bilginin ve imanın yalnızca kendisine güvenilen kimselerin haber ve bilgi vermesi yoluyla elde edilmesini (taklid) yeterli bulmadığı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r3.claim: Adam learned the names and properties of material and spiritual beings and concepts, or the capacity to name things and invent language.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r3.anchor: Âdem’e bütün isimleri, yani maddî ve mânevî varlıkların, kavramların isimleriyle bunların özelliklerini veya isim verme, dil icat etme kabiliyetini öğretti;

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r4.claim: God showed the angels the things because everything's origin exists in the unseen realm and the divine plan.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r4.anchor: her şeyin aslı gayb âleminde, ilâhî planda mevcut olduğu için bunları meleklerine gösterdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r5.claim: God asked the angels to name the things if they were right that Adam's positive qualities and capacities were present in them to an even greater degree.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r5.anchor: Âdem’in müsbet vasıflarının ve kabiliyetlerinin fazlasıyla kendilerinde mevcut bulunduğu kanaatlerinde haklı ve isabetli iseler bunların isimlerini bilip söylemelerini istedi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r6.claim: The angels recognized that their capacities for knowing and producing knowledge differed from Adam's, and admitted that he was fit to be God's vicegerent.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r6.anchor: kendilerine verilen bilme ve bilgi üretme kabiliyetinin Âdem’e verilenden farklı olduğunu ve bu sebeple halife olmaya onun ehil bulunduğunu anlayıp itiraf ettiler;

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r7.claim: By seeing God's work directly, the angels affirmed His knowledge and wisdom at a higher level of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:31/r7.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın ilim ve hikmetini, eserini görerek (ayne’l-yakîn olarak) daha üst dereceden tasdik ettiler.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p64/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p64/r3.speaker: يزيد البربري
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p64/r3.claim: Yazid al-Barbari transmits the reading وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p64/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة يزيد البربري: "وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها"

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p64/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p64/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p64/r4.claim: Arabic speakers can promote an object from a postverbal complement to a fronted object, then to the clause topic, and even omit its pronoun or the agent to foreground it.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p64/r4.anchor: فإن ازدادت عنايتهم به قدموه على الفعل الناصبه، فقالوا: عمرا ضرب زيد، فإن تظاهرت العناية به عقدوه على أنه رب الجملة

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r1.claim: Preposed complements can steer a clause’s meaning: رغبت في زيد expresses preference for him, while رغبت عن زيد expresses turning away, despite the same verb.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r1.anchor: ألا ترى أنك إذا قلت: رغبت في زيد، أفيد منه إيثارك له، وعنايتك به، وإذا قلت: رغبت عن زيد، أفيد منه اطراحك له

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r2.claim: The fronted object زيدا remains emphatic even when accusative and resumed by a pronoun; its position signals care, and an implied verb licenses it.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r2.anchor: فإن فيه غرضا من موضع آخر؛ وذلك أنه إذا نصب على ما ذكرت فإنه لا يعدم دليل العناية به، وهو تقديمه في اللفظ منصوبا

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r3.claim: He applies object prominence to the reading about Adam: its aim is to say Adam learned the names while making clear to the audience that God taught him.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r3.anchor: لما كان الغرض فيه أنه قد عرفها وعلمها، وآنس أيضا علم المخاطبين بأن الله سبحانه هو الذي علمه إياها بقراءة من قرأ

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r4.claim: The fronting of له in the verse demonstrates how an adjunct can be moved forward for emphasis; Sībawayh reports an alternative order from those unfamiliar with the written text.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p65/r4.anchor: وهذا الذي دعاهم إلى تقديم الفضلات في نحو قول الله سبحانه: {ولم يكن له كفوا أحد}

IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r1.speaker: عباس بن الفضل
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r1.claim: He reports lengthening the first hamza and softening the second in several forms with two hamzas in one word.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r1.anchor: وروى عباس بن الفضل عنه / أاءلقى / و / أاءنزل / و / قل أأونبئكم / المد في ذلك كله ويلين الثانية

IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r2.speaker: ابن سعدان وابن اليزيدي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r2.claim: They transmit the same lengthened first hamza and softened second hamza from Abu Amr.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r2.anchor: وكذلك روى ابن سعدان وابن اليزيدي عن أبيه عن أبي عمرو

IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r10.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r10.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r10.claim: When two hamzas meet across words, Nafi changes the first to a homorganic glide and keeps the second hamza; the first glide differs by vowel context.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r10.anchor: فكان نافع إذا التقتا في كلمتين مرفوعتين مثل ﴿ أولياء أولئك ﴾ الأحقاف 32 حول الأولى إلى الواو وهمز الثانية

IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r11.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r11.speaker: رواية خلف وابن المسيبي عن نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r11.claim: Some reports give a kasra on the yāʾ after the first hamza in هؤلاء إن كنتم; another report from Qalun gives a damma on the wāw in أولياء أولئك.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r11.anchor: ورأيت بعض من يروى عن خلف وابن المسيبي عن أبيه عن نافع بكسر الياء التي خلف الهمزة الأولى فيقول / هؤلآى إن كنتم /

IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r12.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r12.speaker: أحمد بن يزيد عن قالون عن نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r12.claim: Ahmad ibn Yazid likewise reports a damma on the wāw in أولياء أولئك.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r12.anchor: وكذلك زعم أحمد بن يزيد عن قالون عن نافع

IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r13.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r13.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r13.claim: Mujahid prefers the softened, intermediate pronunciation of the first hamza, since one hamza can be omitted for ease.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p136/r13.anchor: وهذا أجود الوجهين لأن الهمزتين إنما يكتفي بإحداهما عن الأخرى طلبا للتخفيف

QIRAAT-ER:2:31:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:31:12#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:31:12#1/r1.claim: The anbūnī form elides the imperative hamza as a dialectal or phonological variant, with no change in meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:2:31:12#1/r1.anchor: Hamza elision: anbiʾūnī → anbūnī — drops the hamza in the imperative, dialectal/phonological variant.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42#2/r1.claim: Adam was taught the name of every thing, exemplified by identifying a sea, a mountain, and other things, before the names were presented to the angels.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها ﴾ قال علمه اسم كل شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r9.speaker: أبو علي الشلوبين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Shalawbīn says ʿallama is transferred from the one-object verb ʿalima, distinguished from the two-object verb by doubling versus hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r9.anchor: فرقوا بينها وبين علم التي تتعدى لاثنين في النقل، فعدوا تلك بالتضعيف، وهذه بالهمزة، قاله الأستاذ أبو علي الشلوبين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r10.claim: Ādam is a foreign proper name like Āzar and ʿĀbir, indeclinable for properness and foreignness; deriving it from Arabic words is morphologically unsound.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r10.anchor: آدم: اسم أعجمي كآزر وعابر، ممنوع الصرف للعلمية والعجمة، ومن زعم أنه أفعل مشتق من الأدمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r11.claim: The claim that Ādam is Hebrew for earth or a quadriliteral verb is also rejected; deriving a foreign noun from Arabic or calling it fāʿil conflicts with its declension.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r11.anchor: وقيل: هو عبري من الإدام، وهو التراب، ومن زعم أنه فاعل من أديم الأرض فخطؤه ظاهر لعدم صرفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r12.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r12.claim: Al-Ṭabarī's claim that Ādam is a quadriliteral verb used as a name is especially far-fetched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r12.anchor: وأبعد الطبري في زعمه أنه فعل رباعي سمي به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r13.claim: ʿArḍ means displaying something so that its aspect becomes known.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r13.anchor: العرض: إظهار الشيء حتى تعرف جهته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r14.claim: Inbāʾ means informing; its verb takes the first object directly and the second with a preposition, which can be omitted, or it can take three objects by implying aʿlama.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r14.anchor: الإنباء: الإخبار، ويتعدى فعله الواحد بنفسه والثاني بحرف جر، ويجوز حذف ذلك الحرف، ويضمن معنى أعلم فيتعدى إلى ثلاثة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r15.claim: Hāʾulāʾ points to something near; hāʾ is an alerting particle and ulāʾ is built on kasra, with attested hamza and vowel variants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r15.anchor: هؤلاء: اسم إشارة للقريب، وها: للتنبيه، والاسم أولاء: مبني على الكسر، وقد تبدل همزته هاء فيقال: هلاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r16.speaker: قطرب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r16.claim: Quṭrub records a variant pronunciation with a lengthened ḍamma before the lām in ulāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r16.anchor: وقد تشبع الضمة قبل اللام فيقال: أولاء، قاله قطرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r17.speaker: أبو علي الشلوبين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r17.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Shalawbīn transmits hāʾulāʾ with the alif of hāʾ and hamza of ulāʾ deleted, retaining the following wāw.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r17.anchor: وقد يقال: هؤلاء بحذف ألف ها وهمزة أولاء وإقرار الواو التي بعد تلك الهمزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r1.claim: An unnamed poem witnesses the variant hūlāʾ for hāʾulāʾ with the alif and hamza deleted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r1.anchor: تجلد لا تقل هولاء هذا ... بكى لما بكى أسفا عليكا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r2.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ assigns the long vowel in ulāʾ to the Hijaz and the shortened form to Tamim; others add some Qays and Asad speakers to the shortened form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r2.anchor: وذكر الفراء: أن المد في أولاء لغة الحجاز، والقصر لغة تميم، وزاد غيره أنها لغة بعض قيس وأسد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r3.speaker: الأعشى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r3.claim: Al-Aʿshā's verse supplies an example of the lengthened hāʾulāʾ form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r3.anchor: وأنشد للأعشى: هؤلاء ثم هؤلاء كلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r4.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī analyzes the final hamza of hāʾulāʾ as the final radical, so both its first and final radicals are hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r4.anchor: والهمزة عند أبي علي لام الفعل، ففاؤه ولامه همزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r5.speaker: أبو العباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r5.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās says the hamza replaces a yāʾ that followed an alif.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r5.anchor: وعند أبي العباس بدل من الياء وقعت بعد ألف فقلبت همزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r8.claim: After giving the angels the general wisdom for creating Adam and his descendants, God specifies Adam’s superiority by teaching him the names, completing the general answer with detail.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r8.anchor: أراد أن يفصل، فبين لهم من فضل آدم ما لم يكن معلوما لهم، وذلك بأن علمه الأسماء ليظهر فضله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r9.claim: A clause meaning He made a vicegerent on earth must be supplied before and taught Adam, completing the sense and coordination; the wording then names Adam explicitly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r9.anchor: ولا بد من تقدير جملة محذوفة قبل هذا، لأنه بها يتم المعنى ويصح هذا العطف، وهي: فجعل في الأرض خليفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r10.claim: He rejects coordinating and taught Adam directly with the earlier God said from the opening of the passage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r10.anchor: وأبعد من زعم أن: وعلم آدم معطوف على قوله، قال من قوله تعالى:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r11.claim: Although teaching could be direct speech, through an angel, or inspiration, the most apparent view is that God taught Adam directly, without intermediary or inspiration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r11.anchor: أظهرها أن الباري تعالى هو المعلم، لا بواسطة ولا إلهام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r12.speaker: اليماني ويزيد اليزيدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r12.claim: Al-Yamānī and Yazīd al-Yazīdī read the verb in the passive, with its agent omitted because it is understood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r12.anchor: وقرأ اليماني ويزيد اليزيدي: وعلم آدم مبنيا للمفعول، وحذف الفاعل للعلم به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r13.claim: The doubled form of علم makes the verb take two objects, but such causative extension is licensed by attestation rather than freely by analogy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r13.anchor: والتضعيف في علم للتعدية، إذ كان قبل التضعيف يتعدى لواحد، فعدى به إلى اثنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r14.speaker: القاسم بن علي الحريري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r14.claim: Al-Ḥarīrī wrongly claims that doubling a verb already taking two objects can make it take three; Abu Hayyan says Arabic supplies no such construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r14.anchor: وقد وهم القاسم بن علي الحريري في زعمه في شرح الملحة له أن علم تكون منقولة من علم التي تتعدى إلى اثنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r1.speaker: بعض النحويين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r1.claim: Some grammarians treat causative doubling as productive, whereas the cited account of Sibawayh’s view limits it to attested usage for both transitive and intransitive verbs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r1.anchor: وقد ذهب بعض النحويين إلى اقتياس التعدية بالتضعيف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r2.speaker: أبو الحسين بن أبي الربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abī al-Rabīʿ says the apparent position of Sibawayh is that causative doubling is attested for both transitive and intransitive verbs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r2.anchor: الظاهر من مذهب سيبويه أن النقل بالتضعيف سماع في المتعدي واللازم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, and Qatāda say Adam was taught the names of all created beings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r3.anchor: أسماء جميع المخلوقات، قاله ابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r4.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās says Adam was taught the names of everything that had existed or would exist until Judgment Day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r4.anchor: أو اسم ما كان وما يكون إلى يوم القيامة، وعزي إلى ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r5.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r5.claim: Another view says Adam learned all languages, then taught each son a language and the peoples dispersed speaking different languages.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r5.anchor: أو جميع اللغات، ثم كلم كل واحد من بنيه بلغة فتفرقوا في البلاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Qatāda are also reported to say the names taught were only the stars.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r6.anchor: أو أسماء النجوم فقط، قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r7.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym says Adam was taught only the names of the angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r7.anchor: أو أسماء الملائكة فقط، قاله الربيع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r8.speaker: الربيع بن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r8.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Zayd says the names taught were Adam’s descendants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r8.anchor: أو أسماء ذريته، قاله الربيع بن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r9.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Adam was taught the names of both his descendants and the angels, and selects this view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r9.anchor: أو أسماء ذريته والملائكة، قاله الطبري واختاره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī selects the names of created kinds, such as horses and camels, together with their religious and worldly uses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r10.anchor: أو أسماء الأجناس التي خلقها، علما أن هذا اسمه فرس، وهذا اسمه بعير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r11.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r11.claim: Ibn Qutayba says Adam was taught the names of what God created on earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r11.anchor: أو أسماء ما خلق في الأرض، قاله ابن قتيبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r12.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r12.claim: Another view says Adam learned names in one language, and his descendants later coined the names in other languages.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r12.anchor: أو الأسماء بلغة ثم وقع الاصطلاح من ذريته في سواها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r13.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r13.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī says Adam learned everything, even things like the word Sībawayh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r13.anchor: أو علمه كل شيء حتى نحو سيبويه، قاله أبو علي الفارسي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r14.speaker: الحكيم الترمذي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r14.claim: Al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī says Adam learned the names of God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r14.anchor: أو أسماء الله عز وجل، قاله الحكيم الترمذي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r15.speaker: الجريري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r15.claim: Al-Jurayrī says Adam learned God’s hidden names, through which he learned all names.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r15.anchor: أو أسماء من أسمائه المخزونة، فعلم بها جميع الأسماء، قاله الجريري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r16.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r16.claim: The majority interpret the teaching as Adam’s learning how to name things, distinguishing the act of naming from the names themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r16.anchor: أو التسميات. ومعنى هذا علمه أن يسمي الأشياء، وليس المعنى علمه الأسماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r17.speaker: بعض من عاصرناه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r17.claim: Two views differ on whether Adam was shown the entities or only described them; a contemporary Abu Hayyan knew prefers names of descendants, including the obedient and sinful, to answer the angels’ concern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r17.anchor: وحالة تعليمه تعالى آدم، هل عرض عليه المسميات أو وصفها له ولم يعرضها عليه قولان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r18.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r18.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the names as names of their referents, with the genitive elided and the article serving in its place, citing the head blazing gray as a parallel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234#2/r18.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وعوض منه اللام كقوله: واشتعل الرأس شيبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r1.claim: He says treating the article as a replacement for a genitive construction is not the Basran grammarians’ position.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r1.anchor: وقد تقدم لنا أن اللام عوض من الإضافة ليس مذهب البصريين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r2.claim: He also allows an analysis with the genitive construction names of the referents, but prefers teaching the names themselves because the command and later report attach to names.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r2.anchor: ويترجح الأول، وهو تعليق التعليم بالأسماء تعلق الإنباء به في قوله: أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r3.claim: If then He presented them is read literally, its animate plural pronoun points to the referents, since names themselves are not treated as animate plurals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r3.anchor: ويترجح الثاني بقوله، ثم عرضهم إذا حمل على ظاهره، لأن الأسماء لا تجمع كذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r4.claim: The wording says God taught Adam all names without specifying a subset; the wisdom is achieved by teaching names even if their referents are unknown to us.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r4.anchor: أن الله علم آدم الأسماء ولم يبين لنا أسماء مخصوصة، بل دل قوله تعالى: كلها على الشمول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r5.claim: The word names may instead stand for the things named, using the expression for its referents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد بالأسماء المسميات، فيكون من إطلاق اللفظ ويراد به مدلوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r6.claim: The word then marks a delay: Adam was taught, given time for the knowledge to settle, and only afterward told to report what he had learned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r6.anchor: ثم عرضهم: ثم: حرف تراخ، ومهلة علم آدم ثم أمهله من ذلك الوقت إلى أن قال: أنبئهم بأسمائهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r7.claim: The angels received the command immediately without earlier instruction, so they could not answer; Adam, having first been taught, responded and showed God’s prior care for him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r7.anchor: وأما الملائكة فقال لهم على وجه التعقيب دون مهلة أنبئوني، فلما لم يتقدم لهم تعريف لم يخبروا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says God created the referents and presented them to the angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r8.anchor: عرضهم خلقهم وعرضهم عليهم، قاله ابن مسعود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r9.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r9.claim: Other explanations say God showed their images to the angels’ hearts or displayed them as tiny particles.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r9.anchor: أو صورهم لقلوب الملائكة، أو عرضهم وهم كالذر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the things displayed were the names.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r10.anchor: أو عرض الأسماء، قاله ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r11.claim: The apparent pronoun in presented them returns to the referents and is grammatically animate; it may mean rational beings, or a mixed set where rational beings control agreement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r11.anchor: والظاهر أن ضمير النصب في عرضهم يعود على المسميات، وظاهره أنه للعقلاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r12.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r12.claim: Ubayy reads the pronoun as feminine singular, which returns to the names and makes the names themselves the displayed items.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r13.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r13.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads a feminine plural pronoun returning to the names; alternatively, what was displayed was the named referents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r13.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ثم عرضهن، والضمير عائد على الأسماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r14.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r14.claim: On the phrase upon the angels, one view takes the reference to include all angels; another limits it to the angels who were with Iblis on earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r14.anchor: على الملائكة: ظاهره العموم، فقيل: هو مراد، وقيل: الملائكة الذين كانوا مع إبليس في الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r15.claim: The conjunction fa marks immediate succession, with no pause for reflection between the display and the command; Abu Hayyan says this better supports the absence of any addition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r15.anchor: فقال: الفاء: للتعقيب، ولم يتخلل بين العرض والأمر مهلة بحيث يقع فيها ترو أو فكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p235/r16.claim: Anbiuni is an incapacitating challenge rather than a legally binding command.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r2.claim: Using the challenge as proof that God may command the impossible is weak: the wording is a rebuke, as confirmed by if you are truthful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r2.anchor: وقد استدل بقوله: أنبئوني على جواز تكليف ما لا يطاق، وهو استدلال ضعيف، لأنه على سبيل التبكيت، ويدل عليه: إن كنتم صادقين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r3.claim: These appears to refer to entities present when the angels were addressed; making it refer to absent people through their names is strained and unsupported.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r3.anchor: ظاهره حضور أشخاص حالة العرض على الملائكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r4.speaker: سيبويه وجمهور البصريين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r4.claim: Sibawayh and most Basrans say the conditional جواب is omitted and supplied by the earlier command anbiuni, rather than the command itself being the answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r4.anchor: شرط جوابه محذوف تقديره فأنبئوني يدل عليه أنبئوني السابق، ولا يكون أنبئوني السابق هو الجواب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r5.speaker: الكوفيون وأبو زيد وأبو العباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r5.claim: The Kufans, Abū Zayd, and Abū al-ʿAbbās instead take the earlier command as the answer to the conditional.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r5.anchor: وخالف الكوفيون وأبو زيد وأبو العباس، فزعموا أن جواب الشرط هو المتقدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r6.speaker: المهدوي وابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r6.claim: Al-Mahdawī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya wrongly attribute the omitted-answer parse to al-Mubarrad; Abu Hayyan allows that they may have seen an obscure contrary report.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r6.anchor: وقد وهم المهدوي، وتبعه ابن عطية، فزعما أن جواب الشرط محذوف عند المبرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r7.speaker: ابن عطية وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others also misstate Sibawayh as placing the answer before the condition and taking the earlier command as the answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r7.anchor: وكذلك وهم ابن عطية وغيره، فزعما أن مذهب سيبويه تقديم الجواب على الشرط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r8.claim: Here truthful means correct, as false can mean mistaken; the angels’ supposed claim may concern their knowledge, the vicegerent’s corruption, their superiority, or their own fitness for worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r8.anchor: والصدق هنا هو الصواب، أي إن كنتم مصيبين، كما يطلق الكذب على الخطأ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r9.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r9.claim: One interpretation takes the angels’ claim to be that no created being would be more knowledgeable than they were.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r9.anchor: إني لا أخلق خلقا، لا كنتم أعلم منه، لأنه هجس في أنفسهم أنهم أعلم من غيرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r10.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r10.claim: Another interpretation takes their claim to concern the prediction that God’s vicegerents would corrupt the earth and shed blood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r10.anchor: أو فيما زعمتم أن خلفائي يفسدون في الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r11.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r11.claim: Another interpretation says they assumed God would create no beings better than themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r11.anchor: أو فيما وقع في نفوسكم أني لا أخلق خلقا إلا كنتم أفضل منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r12.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r12.claim: Another interpretation takes the claim to concern the future beings God would appoint after the angels.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r13.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r13.claim: Another interpretation says the angels thought they would glorify God if appointed, while others would disobey if appointed instead.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r13.anchor: أو إني إن استخلفتكم فيها سبحتموني وقدستموني، وإن استخلفت غيركم فيها عصاني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r14.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās take their claim to mean that they alone were fit for every form of worship required of creatures.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r14.anchor: في قولكم: إنه لا شيء مما يتعبد به الخلق إلا وأنتم تصلحون له وتقومون به، قاله ابن مسعود وابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r15.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r15.claim: Another reading takes the challenge itself as their supposed truth: they should report the names and answer the question.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p236/r15.anchor: أو في ذلك إنباء، وجواب السؤال بالأسماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r1.speaker: القشيري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r1.claim: Al-Qushayrī says awe of the address silenced the angels when asked for knowledge they lacked; Adam, previously taught, reported the names, revealing his superiority and God’s knowledge of their outward worship and concealed self-regard.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r1.anchor: داخلهم من هيبة الخطاب ما أخذهم عنهم، لا سيما حين طالبهم بإنبائهم إياه ما لم تحط بهم علومهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r2.claim: In Arabic, successive quoted statements normally need no conjunction marking sequence because their semantic order is clear; he cites the dialogue about the angels and Adam and many Quranic examples.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r2.anchor: والجملة المفتتحة بالقول إذا كانت مرتبا بعضها على بعض في المعنى، فالأصح في لسان العرب أنها لا يؤتى فيها بحرف ترتب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r3.claim: The command to tell the angels and the report that Adam told them show God taught Adam about beings whose states the angels did not know; they had seen his form before the spirit was breathed into him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r3.anchor: وفي قوله: أنبئوني، فلما أنبأهم تنبيه على إعلام الله أنه قد أعلم الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r4.claim: God raised Adam’s rank by teaching him what the angels did not know and placed him as their teacher, with the angels as learners.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r4.anchor: وعلى أنه رفع درجة آدم عندهم، لكونه قد علم لآدم ما لم يعلمهم، وعلى إقامته مقام المفيد المعلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r5.claim: The angels’ questioning lacked the pure submission appropriate to them; obedience without understanding the wisdom or asking in surprise would better suit their purity and complete qualities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r5.anchor: وكان الامتثال والتسليم، بغير تعجب ولا استفهام، أليق بمقامهم لطهارة ذواتهم وكمال صفاتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r6.speaker: المعتزلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r6.claim: The Muʿtazilites say Adam’s knowledge of the names was a miracle proving his prophethood at that time; they suggest he was sent to Eve and perhaps also to the challenged angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r6.anchor: قالت المعتزلة: ظهر من آدم عليه السلام في علمه بالأسماء معجزة دالة على نبوته في ذلك الوقت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan counters that learning language through God’s teaching is no breach of ordinary custom, and asks how angels could know Adam’s answers were correct if they had not known the names.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r7.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول: حصول العلم باللغة لمن علمه الله وعدم حصوله لمن لم يعلم ليس بناقض للعادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r8.claim: They argue that if the angels knew the names and their referents, Adam had no advantage; if not, they could not recognize his accuracy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r8.anchor: فالملائكة أما أن علموا وضع تلك الأسماء للمسميات فلا مزية أو لا، فكيف علموا إصابته في ذلك؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan introduces a two-part answer to how the angels could recognize Adam’s answers as correct.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r9.anchor: فكيف علموا إصابته في ذلك؟ والجواب من وجهين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p241/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p241/r1.speaker: من قال لم يكن نبيا
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p241/r1.claim: Those denying Adam’s prophethood cite his later sin, the lack of a suitable recipient for a message, and the statement that God chose him only after his lapse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p241/r1.anchor: واحتج من قال: لم يكن نبيا، بوجوه: أحدها: صدور المعصية عنه بعد، وذلك غير جائز على النبي

QASHANI:2:31-32/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:31-32/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:31-32/r1.claim: God placed in Adam’s heart the properties of things by which they are recognized, along with their benefits and harms.
QASHANI:2:31-32/r1.anchor: ألقى في قلبه خواص الأشياء التي تعرف بها هي ومنافعها ومضارها

QASHANI:2:31-32/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:31-32/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:31-32/r2.claim: Presenting the angels with the named things means showing them the referents of the names; they witnessed the human constitution and accompanied Adam in the descent.
QASHANI:2:31-32/r2.anchor: بشهودهم البنية الإنسانية ومرافقتهم لآدم في التنزيل

QASHANI:2:31-32/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:31-32/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:31-32/r3.claim: God intended the angels to be enlivened by some of humanity’s knowledge, which the human constitution and its varied, newly arising perceptions bring to them; their knowledge depends on God’s.
QASHANI:2:31-32/r3.anchor: إرادته لانتعاشهم ببعض معلومات الإنسان باقتضاء التركيب الإنساني

QASHANI:2:31-32/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:31-32/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:31-32/r4.claim: Adam’s announcement lets the human faculties and attending angels receive knowledge they could not receive elsewhere.
QASHANI:2:31-32/r4.anchor: إذ جميع القوى الإنسانية والملائكة التي بحضرته تنتعش بما لا تنتعش هي في غير ذلك المحل

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r1.claim: The generic plural ‘the names’ implies all names, and ‘all of them’ reinforces their comprehensiveness and certainty.

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and other exegetes say Adam was taught the names of all created things.
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r2.anchor: على ما نطق به تفسير ابن عباس وغيره

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r3.claim: Adam was also taught God’s names, but God demonstrated his advantage to the angels through the created names.

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r4.claim: God’s exclusive knowledge of His own names is a secret disclosed to no angel, even one brought near.
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r4.anchor: فذلك سر لم يطلع عليه ملك مقرب

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r5.claim: One unable to equal Adam in knowing created names has no hope of approaching his knowledge of God’s names or the unseen.
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r5.anchor: ومن ليس له رتبة مساواة آدم في معرفة أسماء المخلوقات فأي طمع في مداناته في أسماء الحق

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r6.claim: If knowledge of created names warrants the angels’ prostration, the distinction in divine names warrants an even greater honor.
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r6.anchor: فما الظن بالتخصيص بمعرفة أسماء الحق سبحانه

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r7.claim: Angels’ specialty is glorification and purification, creaturely acts of worship; knowledge is a greater praiseworthy attribute associated with God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r7.anchor: خصوصية الملائكة بالتسبيح والتقديس وهذه طاعات تليق بالمخلوقين

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r8.claim: God honored Adam secretly by teaching him, then publicly by demonstrating his distinction and giving him precedence.
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r8.anchor: أكرمه في السر بما علمه ثم بين تخصيصه يوم الجهر وقدمه

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r9.claim: The delay in ‘then He presented them’ may mean Adam was given time to settle and verify the knowledge in his heart before being questioned.
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r9.anchor: فإنه أمهله من الوقت ما تقررذلك

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r10.claim: Alternatively, the delay concerns the angels: they were asked abruptly without prior teaching, while Adam answered because he had already been taught.

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r11.claim: The challenge ‘if you are truthful’ alludes to the angels’ claim of special standing and superiority over Adam; merit comes from prior divine choice, not earlier glorification.
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r11.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى أنهم تعرضوا لدعوى الخصوصية

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r12.claim: By asking the angels to name what He knew they could not, God demonstrated His sovereign right to command and rule.
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r12.anchor: ولما علم الحق سبحانه تقاصر علومهم عن معرفة أسماء المخلوقات ثم كلفهم الإنباء عنها صار فيه أوضح دلالة على أن الأمر أمره

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r13.claim: Divine rulings are not governed by human claims about rationally attractive outcomes; God may obligate whom He wills, and good or bad is what He judges so.
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r13.anchor: ردا على من توهم أن أحكام الحق سبحانه معللة باستحسان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r1.claim: The teaching clause coordinates with God’s prior speech and confirms its content; the opening of the teaching account suggests the dialogue followed Adam’s creation and occurred in his presence after the spirit was breathed into him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r1.anchor: عطف على ( قال ) وفيه تحقيق لمضمون ما تقدم وظاهر الابتداء بحكاية التعليم يدل على أن ما مر من المقاولة إنما جرت بعد خلقه عليه السلام بمحضر منه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r2.claim: An alternative parses the teaching as coordinated with an omitted verb: God created Adam and taught him, created, fashioned and breathed into him before teaching him, or appointed him a vicegerent and taught him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r2.anchor: وقيل : إنه معطوف على محذوف اي فخلق وعلم أو فخلقه وسواه ونفخ فيه الروح وعلم أو فجعل في الأرض خليفة وعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r3.claim: Naming Adam explicitly specifies him and honors him by mentioning his name.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r3.anchor: وإبراز أسمه عليه السلام للتنصيص عليه والتنويه بذكره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r4.speaker: الجواليقي وكثيرون
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r4.claim: They treat Ādam as an Arabic name on the afʿal pattern, deriving it from complexion; some explain the complexion as swarthiness and others as whiteness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r4.anchor: صرح الجواليقي وكثيرون أنه عربي ووزنه أفعل من الأدمة بضم فسكون السمرة وياما أحيلاها في بعض وفسرها أناس بالبياض

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r5.claim: Other proposed Arabic derivations connect Ādam with a model or exemplar, the visible surface of the earth, or affinity and harmony.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r5.anchor: أو الأدمة بفتحتين الأسوة والقدوة أو من أديم الأرض ما ظهر منها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r6.speaker: أحمد والترمذي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r6.claim: A report they transmit, authenticated by several scholars, says God took a handful from all parts of the earth, smooth and rugged, and made Adam from it; this explains the diversity of his descendants.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r6.anchor: أخرج أحمد والترمذي وصححه غير واحد أنه تعالى قبض قبضة من جميع الأرض سهلها وحزنها فخلق منها آدم فلذلك تأتي بنوه أخيافا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r7.claim: On the affinity derivation, the original form has two hamzas and the second became an alif after a fatḥa; the name is diptote because it is a proper name on a verb pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r7.anchor: وأصله اادم بهمزتين فأبدلت الثانية ألفا لسكونها بعد فتحة ومنع صرفه للعلمية ووزن الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r8.speaker: some scholars
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r8.claim: A competing account says Ādam is foreign and follows the faʿil pattern with a fatḥa, as in names such as Shalikh and Āzar.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r8.anchor: وقيل : أعجمي ووزنه فاعل بفتح العين ويكثر هذا في الأسماء كشالخ وآزر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r9.claim: The foreign-name account cites the plural awdām and diminutive uwaydim, which use wāw rather than the forms expected if the name were Arabic Ādam.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r9.anchor: ويشهد له جمعه على أودام بالواو لا اآدم بالهمزة وكذا تصغيره على أويدم لاأؤيدم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r10.speaker: الجوهري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r10.claim: Al-Jawhari argues that hamza has no known original position in this pattern, so the name’s plural and diminutive instead favor wāw; others do not accept his argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r10.anchor: واعت عنه الجوهري بأنه ليس للهمزة أصل في البناء معروف فجعل الغالب عليها الواو ولم يسلموه له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r11.claim: A foreign name cannot be securely etymologized from its source language, which is unknown, or from another language, since cross-language coincidence is remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r11.anchor: وحينئذ لا يجري الاشتقاق فيه لأنه من تلك اللغة لا نعلمه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r12.claim: Any Arabic derivation is best understood as an analogical derivation after Arabization, used to identify the name’s form and added letters; a truly original derivation would be like joining unrelated words.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r12.anchor: وإن ذكر فيه فذاك للإشارة إلى أنه بعد التعريب ملحق بكلامهم وهو اشتقاق تقديري اعتبروه لمعرفة الوزن والزائد فيه من غيره ومن أجراه فيه حقيقة كمن جمع بين الضب والنون ولعل هذا أقرب إلى الصواب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r13.claim: The plural asmāʾ is etymologically a sign for a thing, raising it into the mind through words assigned in any language, along with qualities and actions.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r13.anchor: جمع أسم وهو باعتبار الاشتقاق ما يكون علامة للشيء ودليلا يرفعه إلى الذهن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r14.claim: In customary usage, ism can mean an expression assigned to a meaning, whether simple or compound and whether functioning as subject, predicate, or relation; either lexical sense can fit here.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r14.anchor: واستعمل عرفا في الموضوع لمعنى مفردا كان أو مركبا مخبرا عنه أو خبرا أو رابطة بينهما وكلا المعنيين محتمل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r15.speaker: author
