ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r15.claim: Knowledge of simple and compound expressions, declarative or performative, entails knowledge of conceptual and propositional meanings; the later technical sense of ism cannot be intended in this passage.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p223/r15.anchor: والعلم بالألفاظ المفردة والمركبة تركيبا خبريا أو إنشائيا يستلزم العلم بالمعاني التصويرية والتصديقية وإرادة المعنى المصطلح مما لا يصلح لحدوثه بعد القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r1.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r1.claim: The Imam explains the names as attributes, qualities, and properties because they signify the essences of things.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r1.anchor: وقال الإمام : المراد بالأسماء صفات الأشياء ونعوتها وخواصها لأنها علامات دالة على ماهياتها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r2.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r2.claim: Al-Shihāb objects that attributes and properties are not attested as being called names, so this cannot explain the wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r2.anchor: كما قال الشهاب نظر إذ لم يعهد إطلاق الاسم على مثله حتى يفسر به النظم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r3.claim: One view attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās says the names comprise everything that existed and will exist until the Day of Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r3.anchor: وقيل : المراد بها أسماء ما كان وما يكون إلى يوم القيامة وعزى إلى ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r4.claim: Other reported interpretations take the names to mean languages, the names of angels, or the names of stars.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r4.anchor: وقيل : اللغات وقيل : أسماء الملائكة وقيل : أسماء النجوم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r5.speaker: الحكيم الترمذي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r5.claim: Al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī interprets the taught names as God’s names.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r6.claim: The author prefers the position of the people of spiritual realization: the names are all things, celestial and terrestrial, substances and accidents, as required by Adam’s comprehensive vicegerency.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r6.anchor: والحق عندي ما عليه أهل الله تعالى وهو الذي يقتضيه منصب الخلافة الذي علمت

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r7.speaker: أهل الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r7.claim: They call things God’s names because each thing points to Him and manifests Him without limiting Him; every existent thing is one of His names and an aspect of His activity, so His names are without limit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r7.anchor: ويقال لها أسماء الله تعالى عندهم باعتبار دلالتها عليه وظهوره فيها غير متقيد بها ولهذا قالوا : إن أسماء الله تعالى غير متناهية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r8.claim: The names express divine realities appearing in multiplicity while retaining a distinction between the levels of unity and differentiation; without levels, the names and attributes would have no expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r8.anchor: إن الوجود وإن تعدد ظاهرا وحياتكم ما فيه إلا أنتم لكن للفرق مقام وللجمع مقام ولكل مقام مقال ولولا المراتب لتعطلت الأسماء والصفات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r9.speaker: أهل الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r9.claim: Adam’s teaching means the Real manifested in him through all the mutually contrasting names and attributes suited to his comprehensive capacity, without incarnation, union, or likeness; he thereby knew the realities and secrets of things.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r9.anchor: تعليمها له عليه السلام على هذا ظهور الحق جل وعلا فيه منزها عن الحلول والاتحاد والتشبيه بجميع أسمائه وصفاته المتقابلة حسب استعداده الجامع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r10.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r10.claim: One account says God created in Adam, according to his capacity, necessary and detailed knowledge of the names, their referents, their indications, and how they indicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r10.anchor: فقيل : بأن خلق فيه عليه السلام بموجب استعداده علما ضروريا تفصيليا بتلك الأسماء وبمدلولاتها وبدلالتها ووجه دلالتها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r11.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r11.claim: Another account says Adam was made from diverse elements and powers ready to perceive, then inspired with knowledge of things, names, properties, scientific principles, crafts, tools, and their use; this puts the dialogue before his creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r11.anchor: وقيل : بأن خلقه من أجزاء مختلفة وقوى متباينة مستعدا لإدراك أنواع المدركات وألهمه معرفة ذوات الأشياء وأسمائها وخواصها ومعارفها وأصول العلم وقوانين الصناعات وتفاصيل آلاتها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r12.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r12.claim: A further view takes the teaching literally but says it came through an angel excluded from the address tell Me; the author rejects it unless a sound report supports it, and even then allows a less obvious interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r12.anchor: بأن التعليم على ظاهره وكان بواسطة ملك غير داخل في عموم الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r13.speaker: أبو هاشم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r13.claim: Abū Hāshim claims the teaching presupposes an already established conventional language.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r13.anchor: هذا التعليم لا يقتضي تقدم لغة اصطلاحية كما زعمه أبو هاشم واحتج عليه بوجوه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r14.claim: The author rejects the requirement of a prior conventional language: it would entail circularity or an infinite regress.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r14.anchor: لا يقتضي تقدم لغة اصطلاحية كما زعمه أبو هاشم واحتج عليه بوجوه ردت في التفسير الكبير إذ لو افتقر لتسلسل الأمر أودار

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r15.speaker: الإمام الأشعري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r15.claim: Al-Ashʿarī uses this verse to argue that God initially established all languages, while allowing people to create some later names, such as a father naming his son’s standard.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r15.anchor: والإمام الأشعري يستدل بهذه الآية على أن الواضع للغات كلها هو الله تعالى ابتداء ويجوز حدوث بعض الأوضاع من البشر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r16.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r16.claim: The Muʿtazila hold that human beings, whether Adam or someone else, established language by convention.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r16.anchor: والمعتزلة يقولون : الواضع من البشر آدم أو غيره ويسمى مذهب الاصطلاح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r17.speaker: الأستاذ
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r17.claim: A distribution position assigns some linguistic conventions to God and the rest to human beings; al-Ustādh holds this view.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r17.anchor: وقيل : وضع الله تعالى بعضها ووضع الباقي البشر وهو مذهب التوزيع وبه قال الأستاذ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r18.speaker: اليماني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r18.claim: The Yemeni reader reads ʿullima in the passive, and al-Baḥr says the doubled form is causative by attested usage, though another view treats this as regular.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r18.anchor: وقرأ اليماني ( وعلم ) مبنيا للمفعول وفي البحر أن التضعيف للتعدية وهي به سماعية وقيل : قياسية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r19.speaker: الحريري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r19.claim: Al-Ḥarīrī mistakenly claims in his commentary that a verb taking two objects can, by doubling, take a third.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r19.anchor: والحريريفي شرح لمحته يزعم أنعلم المتعدي لإثنين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r20.claim: The object pronoun in ʿaraḍahum refers to the things named, understood from the context; masculine agreement is explained either by the inclusion of rational beings or by honoring the referents as rational.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r20.anchor: ثم عرضهم على الملائكة أي المسميات المفهومة من الكلام وتذكير الضمير على بعض الوجوه لتغليب ما اشتملت عليه من العقلاء وللتعظيم بتنزيلها منزلتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r21.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r21.claim: Others take the pronoun to refer to the names by way of metonymy for their referents, or because names and named things are identical; Makkī and al-Mahdawī adopt the latter view.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r21.anchor: وقيل : الضمير للأسماء باعتبار أنها المسميات مجازا على طريق الاستخدام ومن قال : الاسم عين المسمى قال : الأسماء هي المسميات والضمير لها بلا تكلف وإليه ذهب مكي والمهدوي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r22.claim: The author rejects identifying the displayed items with the names themselves: the angels are asked for the names of those items, whereas asking about the items themselves would have said tell Me these.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r22.anchor: ويرد عليه أن ( أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء ) يدل على أن العرض للسؤال عن أسماء المعروضات لا عن نفسها وإلا لقيل : أنبئوني بهؤلاء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r23.claim: Displaying the referents may mean picturing them to the angels, showing them like particles, or informing them in outline about future beings and the knowledge and crafts needed for life and the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r23.anchor: ومعنى عرض المسميات تصويرها لقلوب الملائكة أو إظهارها لهم كالذر أو إخبارهم بما سيوجده من العقلاء وغيرهم إجمالا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r24.claim: The display is only general because detailed knowledge of what is owed and due belongs to the Subtle and All-Knowing; the scene is like presenting a matter for another to advise on.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r24.anchor: وسؤالهم عما لا بد لهم منه من العلوم والصنائع التي بها نظام معاشهم ومعادهم إجمالا أيضا وإلا فالتفضيل لا يمكن علمه لغير اللطيف الخبير

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r25.claim: Abstract referents can be shown as intellectual forms or immutable entities, or made visible in a realm where meanings take shape; God can do this, and the imaginal realm already gives meanings forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r25.anchor: وعندي أن عرض المسميات عليهم يحتمل أن يكون عبارة عن إطلاعهم على الصور العلمية والأعيان الثابتة التي قد يطلع عليها في هذه النشأة بعض عباد الله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r26.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r26.claim: Another view says the angels witnessed those named things within Adam himself, as expressed by the saying that the greater world is contained in the seemingly small human body.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r26.anchor: وقيل : إنهم شهدوا تلك المسميات في آدم عليه السلام وهو المراد بعرضها وتزعم أنك جرم صغير وفيك انطوى العالم الأكبر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r27.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r27.claim: Ubayy reads ʿaraḍahā, referring either to the named things or their feminine names.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r27.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( ثم عرضها ) وعبدالله ( عرضهن ) والمعنى عرض مسمياتها أو مسمياتهن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r28.speaker: عبدالله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r28.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads ʿaraḍahunna; the feminine pronoun can likewise refer to the named items or their names.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p224/r28.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( ثم عرضها ) وعبدالله ( عرضهن ) والمعنى عرض مسمياتها أو مسمياتهن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r1.claim: The command to name the displayed things exposes the angels’ inability and is not an impossible obligation; sound management and justice in vicegerency require knowledge of aptitudes and rights.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r1.anchor: فقال أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء تعجيز لهم وليس من التكليف بما لا يطاق على ما وهم وفيه إشارة إلى أن أمر الخلافة والتصرف والتدبير وإقامة المعدلة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r2.claim: The author’s preferred reading is that the task reveals the angels’ lack of capacity for the comprehensive outer and inner vicegerency; inability to report the names signals inability to attain its required qualities.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r2.anchor: وعندي أن المراد إظهار عجزهم وقصور استعدادهم عن رتبة الخلافة الجامعة للظاهر والباطن بأمرهم بالأنباء بتلك الأسماء على الوجه الذي أريد منها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r3.claim: Nabaʾ generally means report; here it may mean a report conveying substantial benefit and knowledge or probable knowledge, and this elevated sense suits the high rank of the names.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r3.anchor: والأنباء في الأصل مطلق الأخبار وهو الظاهر هنا ويطلق على الأخبار بما فيه فائدة عظيمة ويحصل به علم أو غلبة ظن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r4.speaker: some scholars
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r4.claim: Some define informing as a report that conveys information, so it functions like either reporting or informing; this is selected here to signal the names’ importance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إنه إخبار فيه إعلام ولذلك يجري مجرى كل منهما وأختاره هنا على ما قيل للإيذان برفعة شأن الأسماء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r5.claim: The use of thumma in the preceding account and fa here marks special attention to Adam while withholding it from the angels.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r5.anchor: وفي استعمال ثم فيما تقدم والفاء هنا ما لا يخفى من الاعتناء بشأن آدم عليه السلام وعدمه في شأنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r6.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r6.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ( أنبئوني ) بغير همز إن كنتم صادقين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r7.claim: The transmitted explanation is that the angels thought God would create no one more honored or knowledgeable than them; al-Ṭabarī transmits this from Ibn ʿAbbās.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r7.anchor: وهذا هو التفسير المأثور فقد أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن الملائكة قالوا : لن يخلق الله تعالى خلقا أكرم عليه منا ولا أعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r8.claim: The preceding angels’ claim that they glorify God suggests they thought themselves superior, while their praise and sanctification imply knowledge, supporting this interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r8.anchor: وفي الكلام دلالة عليه فإن ( ونحن نسبح ) إلخ يدل على أفضليتهم وتنزيه الله تعالى وتقديسه أو تقديسهم أنفسهم يدل على كمال العلم أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r9.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r9.claim: Another interpretation makes the condition ask the angels to prove their claim that they deserve vicegerency or that appointing Adam would be inappropriate; their doubt is a question seeking clarification, not disobedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r9.anchor: وقيل : إن المعنى ( إن كنتم صادقين ) في زعمكم أنكم أحق بالاستخلاف أو في استخلافهم لا يليق فأثبتوه ببيان ما فيكم من الشرائط السابقة وليس هذا من المعصية في شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r10.claim: Although the angels asked rather than asserted, truth and falsity can apply secondarily to performatives through what their meanings entail, even though they do not apply to their primary wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r10.anchor: الصدق والكذب إنما يتعلق بالخبروهم إستخبروا ولم يخبروا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r11.speaker: سيبويه وجمهور البصريين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r11.claim: Sibawayh and most Basrans say the conditional’s omitted answer is indicated by the preceding command, anbiʾūnī.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r11.anchor: وجواب ( إن ) في مثل هذا الموضع محذوف عند سيبويه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r12.speaker: الكوفيون وأبو زيد والمبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r12.claim: The Kufans, Abū Zayd, and al-Mubarrad take the preceding command itself as the answer; al-Ālūsī says this is the correctly transmitted attribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r12.anchor: وعند الكوفيين وأبي زيد والمبرد أن الجواب هو المتقدم وهذا هو النقل الصحيح عمن ذكر في المسألة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r13.claim: The author rejects reading in here as temporal idhā with no conditional answer, and rejects resorting to that reading merely to avoid an implication thought to compromise angelic innocence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r13.anchor: ومن زعم أن ( إن ) هنا بمعنى إذا الظرفية فلا تحتاج إلى جواب فقد وهم وكأنه لما رأى عصمة الملائكة وظن من الآية ما يخل بها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r14.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r14.claim: The Imam’s alternative makes the condition emphatic: tell Me, speaking only truth, as a way of stressing their inability; al-Ālūsī says he is grateful not to need this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p225/r14.anchor: إلى القول بأن الغرض من الشرطية التوكيد لما نبههم عليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r1.claim: Adam is named because he was created from the surface soil of the earth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r1.anchor: سمي آدم لأنه خلق من أديم الأرض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that Adam was named for his dark complexion.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r3.claim: Adam's kunya was Abu Muhammad and Abu al-Bashar.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r4.speaker: الملائكة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r4.claim: When God announced a successor on earth, the angels thought no creation would be dearer to God than they were, and that they knew more because they preceded Adam and had seen what he had not.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r4.anchor: لما قال الله تعالى: {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة} ليخلق ربنا ما شاء فلن يخلق خلقا أكرم عليه منا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r5.claim: God demonstrated Adam's superiority through knowledge; this supports the Sunni view that prophets are superior to angels, even though angels are messengers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r5.anchor: فأظهر الله تعالى فضله عليهم بالعلم وفيه دليل على أن الأنبياء أفضل من الملائكة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r6.claim: Adam was taught the name of every thing, down to a large and small bowl.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة: علمه اسم كل شيء حتى القصعة والقصيعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r7.claim: Another view is that Adam was taught the names of everything that existed or would exist until the Resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: اسم ما كان وما يكون إلى يوم القيامة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r8.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r8.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas says the names taught were the angels' names.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r8.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: أسماء الملائكة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r9.claim: Another view is that the names were those of Adam's descendants.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r10.claim: Another view is that Adam was taught how to make every thing.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r11.speaker: أهل التأويل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r11.claim: Exegetes say God taught Adam all languages; his children then spoke different languages, dispersed across lands, and each group retained one language.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r11.anchor: قال أهل التأويل: إن الله عز وجل علم آدم جميع اللغات ثم تكلم كل واحد من أولاده بلغة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r12.claim: The pronoun in “displayed them” is masculine because a mixed group of rational and non-rational named things is referred to with the rational masculine plural.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r12.anchor: لأن المسميات إذا جمعت من يعقل وما لا يعقل يكنى عنها بلفظ من يعقل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r13.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r13.claim: Muqatil says God created all animals and inanimate things and displayed their forms; the pronoun therefore refers to those forms.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r13.anchor: وقال مقاتل: خلق الله كل شيء الحيوان والجماد ثم عرض تلك الشخوص على الملائكة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r14.anchor: {فقال أنبئوني} أخبروني {بأسماء هؤلاء إن كنتم صادقين}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r15.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r15.claim: The challenge asks whether the angels are truthful in claiming that no creation would be better or more knowledgeable than them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r15.anchor: {بأسماء هؤلاء إن كنتم صادقين} في أني لا أخلق خلقا إلا وكنتم أفضل وأعلم منه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r16.speaker: الملائكة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79#2/r16.claim: The angels answered by acknowledging their inability.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r1.claim: Adam may have received necessary knowledge created in him directly or cast into his awareness; prior linguistic convention was unnecessary.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r1.anchor: إما بخلق علم ضروري بها فيه، أو إلقاء في روعه، ولا يفتقر إلى سابقة اصطلاح ليتسلسل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r2.claim: Teaching generally leads to knowledge, which explains why one can say that someone was taught but did not learn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r2.anchor: والتعليم فعل يترتب عليه العلم غالبا، ولذلك يقال علمته فلم يتعلم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r3.claim: Adam is a non-Arabic name, like Azar and Shalakh.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r3.anchor: اسم أعجمي كآزر وشالخ، واشتقاقه من الأدمة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r4.claim: Reported derivations connect Adam with complexion or example, and with the earth's surface.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r4.anchor: واشتقاقه من الأدمة أو الأدمة بالفتح بمعنى الأسوة، أو من أديم الأرض

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r5.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r5.claim: A prophetic report says Adam was formed from a handful taken from all the earth, its soft and rough regions, explaining the diversity of his descendants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r5.anchor: أنه تعالى قبض قبضة من جميع الأرض سهلها وحزنها فخلق منها آدم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r6.claim: Deriving Adam from words for affinity is strained, like deriving Idris, Jacob, and Iblis from related Arabic roots.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r6.anchor: أو من الأدم أو الأدمة بمعنى الألفة، تعسف كاشتقاق إدريس من الدرس، ويعقوب من العقب، وإبليس من الإبلاس.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r7.claim: By derivation, a name is a sign and proof that brings its referent to mind.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r7.anchor: والاسم باعتبار الاشتقاق ما يكون علامة للشيء ودليلا يرفعه إلى الذهن

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r8.claim: In customary usage, a name is an expression assigned to a meaning, whether compound or simple and whether subject, predicate, or connective.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r8.anchor: واستعماله عرفا في اللفظ الموضوع لمعنى سواء كان مركبا أو مفردا مخبرا عنه أو خبرا أو رابطة بينهما.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r9.claim: In technical grammar, a name is a simple expression signifying a meaning in itself without reference to one of the three tenses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r9.anchor: واصطلاحا: في المفرد الدال على معنى في نفسه غير مقترن بأحد الأزمنة الثلاثة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r10.claim: The verse means either the lexical or customary sense of names; the customary sense entails the lexical one because understanding signifying words requires knowing meanings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r10.anchor: والمراد في الآية إما الأول أو الثاني وهو يستلزم الأول، لأن العلم بألفاظ من حيث الدلالة متوقف على العلم بالمعاني

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r11.claim: God created Adam from varied components and powers, prepared to perceive intelligible, sensory, imagined, and conjectured things.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r11.anchor: أنه تعالى خلقه من أجزاء مختلفة وقوى متباينة، مستعدا لإدراك أنواع المدركات من المعقولات والمحسوسات، والمتخيلات والموهومات.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r12.claim: God inspired Adam with knowledge of things, their properties and names, the foundations of sciences, craft principles, and tools.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31/r12.anchor: وألهمه معرفة ذوات الأشياء وخواصها وأسمائها وأصول العلوم وقوانين الصناعات وكيفية آلاتها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r1.claim: The pronoun in ‘displayed them’ refers implicitly to the named objects: the construction means the names of the things named, with the genitive complement omitted.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r1.anchor: الضمير فيه للمسميات المدلول عليها ضمنا إذ التقدير أسماء المسميات، فحذف المضاف إليه لدلالة المضاف عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r2.claim: The omitted genitive is replaced by a lām, as in Maryam 19:4.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r3.claim: The objects displayed are the things themselves or their referents, not the words, since the point is to ask for the displayed things' names.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r3.anchor: لأن العرض للسؤال عن أسماء المعروضات فلا يكون المعروض نفس الأشياء سيما إن أريد به الألفاظ

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r4.claim: The masculine plural pronoun is used because the group includes rational beings, who predominate.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r4.anchor: وتذكيره ليغلب ما اشتمل عليه من العقلاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r5.claim: Two feminine readings, ʿaraḍahunna and ʿaraḍahā, refer to the named entities or their referents.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r5.anchor: وقرىء عرضهن وعرضها على معنى عرض مسمياتهن أو مسمياتها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r6.claim: The demand that the angels name the objects rebukes them and exposes their inability to carry out the caliphate.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r6.anchor: تبكيت لهم وتنبيه على عجزهم عن أمر الخلافة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r7.claim: Governance and establishing justice require prior knowledge of capacities and rights, which they lack.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r7.anchor: فإن التصرف والتدبير إقامة المعدلة قبل تحقق المعرفة، والوقوف على مراتب الاستعدادات وقدر الحقوق محال

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r8.claim: This is not an impossible assignment, since the question is not a binding command.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r8.anchor: وليس بتكليف ليكون من باب التكليف بالمحال

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r9.claim: Inbāʾ means informing in a way that conveys knowledge, so it functions like either informing or making known.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#2/r9.anchor: والإنباء: إخبار فيه إعلام، ولذلك يجري مجرى كل واحد منهما.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#3/r1.claim: The challenge presumes the angels claimed they were more entitled to the caliphate because of their impeccability.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#3/r1.anchor: في زعمكم أنكم أحقاء بالخلافة لعصمتكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, they implied that creating such beings and appointing them as successors would be unfitting for divine wisdom.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#3/r2.anchor: أو أن خلقهم واستخلافهم وهذه صفتهم لا يليق بالحكيم، وهو وإن لم يصرحوا به لكنه لازم مقالهم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#3/r3.claim: A statement can be judged truthful or false by what its implication entails, even when that implication was not explicitly stated; this also applies to performative speech.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:31#3/r3.anchor: والتصديق كما يتطرق إلى الكلام باعتبار منطوقه قد يتطرق إليه بفرض ما يلزم مدلوله من الأخبار، وبهذا الاعتبار يعتري الإنشاءات.

SULAMI:v1p56#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p56#2/r1.speaker: الجريري
SULAMI:v1p56#2/r1.claim: Al-Jurayri says God taught Adam one of His hidden names, through which Adam learned all names.
SULAMI:v1p56#2/r1.anchor: قال الجريري : علمه اسما من أسمائه المخزونة فعلم به جميع الأسامي .

SULAMI:v1p56#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p56#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p56#2/r2.claim: One view says God taught Adam all names and preserved them in him, but Adam forgot the entrusted covenant, as in the report about his forgetting.
SULAMI:v1p56#2/r2.anchor: فقال بعضهم علم آدم الأسماء كلها قال : علمها بتعليم الحق إياه وحفظها بحفظه عليه

SULAMI:v1p56#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p56#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p56#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ata says Adam's knowledge surpassed the angels because direct witnessing of God's address gave him knowledge they could not report.
SULAMI:v1p56#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : لو لم يكشف لآدم عليه السلام علم تلك الأسامي لكان لعجز من الملائكة في الإخبار عنها

SULAMI:v1p56#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p56#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p56#2/r4.claim: A respondent says Adam's knowledge exceeded his capacity and total learning because it contained the governance of creation.
SULAMI:v1p56#2/r4.anchor: وقيل لبعضهم : أليس علم آدم على قدره ؟ فقال : بل علمه أكثر من قدرة وجملة تعلمه إذ فيه تدابير الخلق .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r1.claim: God begins proving the angels’ mistaken assumption by teaching Adam, demonstrating the superiority that had been announced to them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r1.anchor: ولما أعلم سبحانه الملائكة أن الأمر على خلاف ما ظنوا شرع في إقامة الدليل عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r2.claim: Teaching is repeated instruction that makes knowledge settle, compensating for the teacher’s innate forgetfulness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r2.anchor: والتعليم تكرار العلم ليثبت لما في جبلة المعلم من النسيان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r3.claim: Adam’s name derives from adīm, the earth’s skin, from which his body was made; the earth-derived portion of him is reflected in his name.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r3.anchor: من الأدم من الأديم وهو جلدة الأرض التي منها جسمه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r4.claim: Al-Harali says “names” joins derivations from marking and elevation: as a word it marks, and as a share of a thing’s essence it is elevated.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r4.anchor: وهو جمع اسم وهو ما يجمع اشتقاقين من السمة والسمو

BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r5.claim: Al-Harali distinguishes the spoken naming from a name as a portion of an object’s reality; the displayed objects are the latter, while the label corresponds to them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r5.anchor: قاله الحرالي , وقال في كتاب له في أصول الفقه : الاسم يقال على لفظ التسمية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r6.claim: Al-Harali explains that the displayed objects are shown from a side or aspect, which is the sense of ʿarḍ.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r6.anchor: قال الحرالي : أظهرهم عن جانب وهو العرض والناحية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r7.claim: Adam was taught the realities of all witnessed beings; angels saw their forms and the divine dominion but not the realities conveyed by their names, while Adam knew the relation between essences and their spoken labels.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r7.anchor: إحاطة علم آدم بما شهدوا صورة ولم يشهدوا حقيقة مدلول تسميتها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r8.claim: Al-Harali says Adam’s knowledge joined each created thing’s image with its divine command-word, completing what his heart apprehended through hearing and sight and preparing him to judge the created order.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p88/r8.anchor: فيكمل علمه في قبله على سبيل سمعه وبصره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r1.claim: God displayed a form of intellectual and practical vicegerency through Adam’s naming, thereby exalting him before the angels.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r1.anchor: فأبدى الله عز وجل لهم بذلك وجه خلافة علمية وعملية في التسمية إعلاء له عندهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r2.claim: The angels immediately yielded to Adam’s superiority over all creation and learned that God raises whom He wills through His vicegerency of command and creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r2.anchor: فانقادوا للوقت بفضل آدم على جميع الخلق وبدا لهم علم أن الله يعلي من يشاء بما يشاء من خلافة أمره وخلقه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r3.claim: The masculine plural pronoun in “displayed them” encompasses the names as shares of the forms of all existing things; “these” points to them once the display is complete.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى { ثم عرضهم } وأشار إليه ( هؤلاء ) عند كمال عرضهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r4.claim: The masculine plural pronoun applies because the displayed creatures include both rational and non-rational beings.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r4.anchor: وأجرى على الجميع ضمير ( هم ) لاشتمال تلك الكائنات على العاقلين وغيرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r5.claim: Biqaʿi adds that every creature can speak when God makes it speak, as in the verse about bodily testimony on the Last Day.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90/r5.anchor: وبالتحقيق فكل خلق ناطق حين يستنطقه الحق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r1.speaker: أبو حاتم أحمد بن حمدان الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r1.claim: Abu Hatim reports the grammarians’ derivation of “name” from elevation, then offers a wordplay: sīn suggests radiance and mīm the core, so a name illuminates an object’s essence; divine marks make names encompass knowledge of things.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r1.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم أحمد بن حمدان الرازي في كتاب الزينة : ويقال إن الاسم مأخوذ من السمو

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r2.claim: God challenges the angels to report the names of the beings they had discerned, testing their earlier claim; the names and their referents have a wise correspondence established by the All-Knowing, All-Wise.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r2.anchor: بأسماء هؤلاء } أي الموجودات بتفرسكم فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r3.claim: The angels’ “Glory be to You” absolves God of deficiency in knowledge or action and disclaims the implication that anyone else possesses independent knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r3.anchor: أي ننزهك تنزيها يجل عن الوصف عن أن ننسب إليك نقصا في علم أو صنع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r4.claim: Al-Harali reads the angels’ admission as displaying their virtue, submission, and acquiescence, preparing for the ensuing mention of Iblis’s refusal.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r4.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفي هذا المعنى إظهار لفضلهم وانقيادهم وإذعانهم توطئة لما يتصل به من إباء أبليس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r5.claim: The angels’ statement that they know only what God taught them establishes that there is no way to know anything except through His teaching.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r5.anchor: فهو دليل على أنه لا سبيل إلى علم شيء من الأشياء إلا بتعليم الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r6.claim: Al-Harali says this returns the beginning of the matter to its source; an unnamed transmitted maxim says one has not truly known unless one ends knowledge by recognizing ignorance apart from what God teaches.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r6.anchor: قال الحرالي : ردا لبدء الأمر لمن له البدء , ولذلك ورد في أثارة من علم : من لم يختم علمه بالجهل لم يعلم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r7.claim: The angels reserve all knowledge and wisdom to God: He knows every object of knowledge and His wise acts cannot be corrupted, leaving no ground for objection.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r7.anchor: أي العالم بكل المعلومات { الحكيم } أي فلا يتطرق إلى صنعك فساد بوجه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r8.claim: Al-Harali calls this an exclusive affirmation of divine knowledge and wisdom, a high form of surrender in which God adorns and gives life to hearts.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r8.anchor: قال الحرالي : توكيد وتخليص وإخلاص للعلم والحكمة لله وحده , وذلك من أرفع الإسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r9.claim: Al-Harali compares knowledge and wisdom to light that gives life to hearts as water gives life to bodies, and defines wisdom as causal relation between two matters.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r9.anchor: فإن العلم والحكمة نور القلوب الذي تحيا به كما أن الماء رزق الأبدان الذي تحيا به

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r10.claim: Al-Harali defines wisdom as a causal connection between two matters, with the prior one calling for and supporting the later one.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r10.anchor: والحكمة جعل تسبيب بين أمرين يبدو بينهما تقاض من السابق واستناد من اللاحق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r11.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r11.claim: Al-Harali says Adam is told to inform the angels so they gain insight that knowledge and felicity depend on what God teaches and grants.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r11.anchor: أي ليزدادوا بصيرة في أن العالم من علمته والسعيد من أسعدته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r12.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r12.claim: Adam is described as informing rather than teaching: he already knew the names, while the angels received information and could not learn from him without Adam’s comprehensive created capacity.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r12.anchor: قال الحرالي : ولم يقل : علمهم , فكان آدم عليما بالأسماء وكانوا هم مخبرين بها لا معلميها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r13.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r13.claim: Al-Harali says every thing has two comprehensive names: one makes its existence perceptible and the other expresses its meaning toward its full reality; its many aspects yield distinct names and languages.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r13.anchor: والشيء اسمان جامعان : اسم بيصره من موجود الشيء واسم يذكره لإبداء معنى ذلك الشيء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r14.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r14.claim: Al-Harali says names reflect the many aspects of things, producing diverse languages; Arabic is most eloquent and comprehensive, the language of the final revelation and of Paradise.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r14.anchor: ولكل اسم جامع عنده وجوه متعددة يحاذي كل وجه منها بتسمية تخصه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r15.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r15.claim: Al-Harali calls Arabic the most eloquent and comprehensive language, the language of the final scripture and messengers and of Paradise, matching the ending to the beginning’s comprehensiveness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p90#2/r15.anchor: فأفصحها وأعربها الاسم الجامع وذلك الاسم هو العربي الذي به أنزل خاتم الكتب على خاتم المرسلين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p95/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95/r1.claim: Al-Harali says divine lordship explains each rank according to the sign shown by its recipient; he links this to several verses about the Lord and His signs.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95/r1.anchor: فللربوبية بيان في كل رتبة بحسب ما أظهرته آية مربوبه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p95/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95/r2.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur’an’s address to the Prophet carries the greatest degree of understanding; forms of address vary with their hearers and divine attributes disclose different ranks of explanation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95/r2.anchor: وقال في الباب الذي بعده : فخطاب الإقبال على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أعظم إفهام في القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p95/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95/r3.claim: Al-Harali describes disclosure as unseen in signs to believers, direct vision for the fully certain, and comprehensive realization for the perfected knower; attention to these ranks opens further understanding.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95/r3.anchor: غيبا في متجلى الآيات للمؤمن , وعينا للكامل الموقن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r1.claim: Biqaʿi says the Qur’an presents the beginning of creation in the order God brought it into being.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r1.anchor: وقد أوقع سبحانه ذكر ابتداء الخلق على ترتيب إيجاده له

BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet’s chronology: soil on Saturday, mountains Sunday, trees Monday, harmful things Tuesday, light Wednesday, animals Thursday, and Adam after Friday afternoon, last among creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيدي فقال : ( خلق الله التربة يوم السبت

BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r3.speaker: المزي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r3.claim: Al-Mizzi cites al-Bukhari’s historical note that some authorities consider Abu Hurayra’s report from Kaʿb the more accurate attribution.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r3.anchor: وقال المزي في الأطراف قال البخاري في التاريخ : وقال بعضهم : أبو هريرة عن كعب وهو أصح .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r4.claim: Biqaʿi rejects as baseless the claim that earlier disobedient beings lived on earth and that the angels analogized Adam to them; the cited Muslim report makes Adam earth’s first inhabitant.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r4.anchor: وما يقال من أنه كان قبل آدم عليه السلام في الأرض خلق يعصون قاس عليهم الملائكة عليهم السلام حال آدم عليه السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r5.claim: Biqaʿi says Adam’s name begins with the alphabet’s first letter and ends with its last, hinting that he was the first inhabitant while his descendants would be the last inhabitants before the Hour.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r5.anchor: والذي يلوح من اسمه في بدئه بالهمزة التي هي أول الحروف وختمه بالميم التي هي آخرها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r6.claim: Biqaʿi quotes a Torah translation’s creation account: God made heaven, earth, light, waters, dry land, vegetation, celestial lights, sea and sky creatures, then land animals and humanity.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p95#2/r6.anchor: ورأيت في ترجمة للتوراة وهو أولها : خلق الله ذات السماء وذات الأرض وكانت الظلمة فقال الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r1.claim: The quoted Torah account continues with humanity’s dominion, food, the completion of creation, and the claim that rain and cultivation awaited Adam’s creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r1.anchor: فخلق آدم بصورته ذكرا وأنثى وبارك عليهما وقال لهما : انميا وأكثرا وتسلطا على حيتان البحر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r2.claim: The Torah passage says God formed Adam from earth, placed him in Eden, planted its trees, named its rivers, and prohibited eating from the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r2.anchor: فجبل الله الرب آدم من تربة الأرض ونفخ في وجهه نسمة الحياة فصار آدم ذا نفس حية وغرس الله الرب فردوسا بعدن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r3.claim: In the Torah account Adam names every living creature brought before him; God then makes a woman from his rib, and the pair become one flesh.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r3.anchor: وأقبل بها إلى آدم ليرى ما يسميها وكل نفس حية سماها آدم فذلك اسمها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r4.claim: The quoted Torah story recounts the serpent’s deception, the couple’s eating and shame, divine curses, expulsion from Eden, and a cherub guarding the tree of life; Adam lives 930 years.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r4.anchor: فأخرجه الله ربنا وأحاط من مشرق عدن ملكا من الكروبيين بيده حربة يطوف بها ليحرس طريق شجرة الحياة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r5.claim: Biqaʿi explains “cherub” as a Hebrew word for a small person; cherubim are angels associated with people through revelation, named after the two figures between whom God’s speech was heard in the tabernacle.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p96/r5.anchor: والكروب بوزن زبور بلغة العبرانيين الشخص الصغير , فكان الكروبيون الملائكة المنسوبين إلى مخالطة الناس بالوحي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r1.claim: Biqaʿi defends citing the Torah by arguing that an interlocutor should be answered from beliefs he accepts; he invokes Qur’anic commands to bring the Torah and its confirmation by the Qur’an, and recalls the Prophet’s use of Torah in an adultery case.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r1.anchor: قل فأتوا بالتوراة فاتلوها إن كنتم صادقين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r2.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that the earth will be served as a single loaf to the people of Paradise on the Resurrection Day; the Prophet smiles as a Jewish man confirms the report.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r3.claim: Biqaʿi says the report of the Beast of the Earth is similar and groups such reports among matters confirmed by the Qur’an.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r3.anchor: وقريب من ذلك حديث الجساسة في أشباهه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr reports the Prophet’s permission to narrate from the Children of Israel without blame.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما

BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet instructed Muslims not to affirm or deny People of the Book, but to say that they believe what was revealed to both communities.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : كان أهل الكتاب يقرؤون التوراة بالعبرانية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r6.claim: Biqaʿi reads these traditions as supporting the permissibility of transmitting such material, rather than prohibiting it; many Companions therefore took reports from People of the Book.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r6.anchor: فإن دلالة هذا على سنية ذكر مثل ذلك أقرب من الدلالة على غيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r7.speaker: الرافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r7.claim: Al-Rafiʿi and other Shafiʿi authorities are cited as saying that Torah and Gospel books may not be used because they were altered.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r7.anchor: قول الإمام أبي القاسم الرافعي في شرحه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r8.claim: Biqaʿi limits that prohibition to material known to have been altered, since alteration is the stated rationale and al-Shafiʿi’s own texts allow other material to be used.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r8.anchor: هذا مخصوص بما علم تبديله , بدليل أن كل من قال ذلك علل بالتبديل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r9.speaker: المزني
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r9.claim: Al-Muzani says non-disliked medical or other useful books taken from unbelievers may be sold, while books containing shirk are destroyed and their containers retained for use.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r9.anchor: قال المزني في مختصره في باب جامع السير : وما كان من كتبهم أي الكفار فيه طب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r10.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r10.claim: Al-Shafiʿi says captured books should be translated; useful material without objection may be sold, while books of shirk are split and their materials retained, with no destruction before their contents are examined.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p98/r10.anchor: قال الشافعي : وما وجد من كتبهم فهو مغنم كله , وينبغي للإمام أن يدعو من يترجمه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r1.claim: Biqaʿi reads al-Shafiʿi’s phrase “book of shirk” as suggesting the whole book is shirk, whereas al-Muzani’s wording allows that only some chapters contain it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r1.anchor: فقوله في الأم : كتاب شرك , مفهم لأنه كله شرك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r2.speaker: النواوي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r2.claim: Al-Nawawi records a preferred Shafiʿi position that touching Torah or Gospel while in minor ritual impurity has the same rule as touching a Qur’anic passage whose recitation was abrogated.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r2.anchor: محرر المذهب الشيخ محيي الدين النواوي رحمه الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r3.claim: Biqaʿi infers from calling this the preferred of two positions that the alternative view forbidding an impure person to touch or carry such books is also substantial.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r3.anchor: حكم ما نسخت تلاوته من القرآن في أصح الوجهين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r4.speaker: المتولي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r4.claim: Al-Mutawalli says touching a passage thought to be unaltered is disliked; Biqaʿi treats the dislike as respect, implying that preservation and reading are permitted.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r4.anchor: أن المتولي قال : فإن ظن أن فيها شيئا غير مبدل كره مسه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r5.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r5.claim: Al-Shafiʿi’s statement that books without objection may be sold supports the permissibility of retaining and using them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r5.anchor: وأصرح من ذلك كله قول الشافعي رحمه الله : إن ما لا مكروه فيه يباع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r6.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r6.claim: Al-Baghawi says a person in major ritual impurity may utter words coinciding with Qur’anic wording, abrogated verses, Torah or Gospel, remembrance of God, or blessings on the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r6.anchor: قول البغوي في تهذيبه في آخر باب الوضوء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r7.speaker: عائشة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r7.claim: ʿAʾisha reports that the Prophet remembered God in every state, which al-Baghawi uses as evidence for the permissibility of such utterances.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r7.anchor: قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها : ( كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يذكر الله على كل أحيانه )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r8.claim: Biqaʿi argues that whatever may be read by a person in major impurity without necessity may be read by one in minor impurity, but not vice versa; this does not make every passage lawful, and the relevant words count as remembrance of God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r8.anchor: فإنه لا يتخيل أنه يجوز للجنب ما لا يجوز للمحدث

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r9.speaker: القاضي الحسين
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r9.claim: Al-Qadi al-Husayn says one may clean oneself with the Torah and Gospel, based on the position that all of both books have been altered.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r9.anchor: قول القاضي الحسين : إنه يجوز الاستنجاء بهما

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r10.claim: Biqaʿi calls that position weak or restricts it to altered text, since no Muslim would use the Ten Commandments as a means of cleaning himself.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r10.anchor: وهو ضعيف أو محمول على المبدل منهما , لأنه لا يخفى على أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r11.speaker: ابن حجر
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r11.claim: Ibn Hajar’s conclusion permits learned scholars grounded in religious sciences to consult these books and extract benefits for the guided, while others may not; Biqaʿi endorses the distinction.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r11.anchor: شيخنا حافظ عصره أبو الفضل بن حجر في آخر شرحه للبخاري

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r12.claim: Biqaʿi says he composed a separate work on the ruling of transmitting from ancient scriptures, titled “Al-Aqwal al-Qawima fi Hukm al-Naql min al-Kutub al-Qadima.”
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r12.anchor: ثم صنفت في ذلك تصنيفا حسنا سميته ( الأقوال القويمة في حكم النقل من الكتب القديمة )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r13.claim: Biqaʿi distinguishes three Torah versions—the Septuagint, the Rabbinic and Karaite text, and the Samaritan text—which differ in wording but are close in meaning; he recounts the Septuagint’s translation by 72 Jewish scholars.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r13.anchor: اعلم أن التوراة ثلاث نسخ مختلفة اللفظ متقاربة المعنى إلا يسيرا : إحداها تسمى توراة السبعين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r14.claim: Biqaʿi says the Septuagint was translated into Syriac and Arabic and was held by Christians; he notes that al-Samarqandi, al-Taftazani, and Qadi ʿIyad cited Torah passages on theology.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r14.anchor: وهذه النسخة ترجمت بعد بالسرياني ثم بالعربي وهي في أيدي النصارى ؛ والنسخة الثانية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r15.claim: Biqaʿi describes his own old Torah copy as probably Jewish, with damaged lines restored from a Septuagint copy and its wording compared against Saʿadia al-Fayyumi’s translation with a Jewish reader; he judges his copy closer to Hebrew and its translator more skilled in Arabic.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p100/r15.anchor: ثم اعلم أن أكثر ما ذكرته في كتابي هذا من نسخة وقعت لي لم أدر اسم مترجمها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r1.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r1.claim: Al-Baghawi says the angels were ordered to prostrate before Adam's creation was completed, immediately after the spirit was breathed into him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r1.anchor: أن الأمر بالسجود له كان قبل إتمام خلقه وأن السجود كان عقب النفخ , وبه صرح البغوي في تفسيره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r2.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r2.claim: To reconcile 7:11, he says creation and fashioning concern Adam alone, expressed plurally because he is mankind's father; alternatively, ثم can mean و without sequence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r2.anchor: وبه صرح البغوي في تفسيره , وأجاب عن قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r3.speaker: يمان
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r3.claim: Yaman defines fashioning as opening the ears, eyes, and fingers.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r3.anchor: والتصوير شق السمع والبصر والأصابع - قاله يمان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r4.claim: Making Adam even means adjusting and completing his form and preparing it to receive the spirit.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r4.anchor: والتسوية تعديل الخلق وإتمامه وتهيئته لنفخ الروح

BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r5.claim: The plural creation and fashioning may mean a near and deliberate ordering for emergence from nonexistence; the Torah's two creation statements can thus mean existence and prior preparation for intended ends.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r5.anchor: فهذا خلق بمعنى الإيجاد , وذلك بمعنى التقدير القريب منه - والتهيئة لقبول الغايات

BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r6.speaker: البيضاوي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r6.claim: Al-Baydawi places the command to prostrate after the angels are informed of the names.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r6.anchor: ومشى البيضاوي على أن الأمر بالسجود كان بعد الإنباء بالأسماء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r7.claim: The author prefers placing prostration after the announcement: before it, the angels' prostration would be faith in the unseen; afterward, Adam's learned superiority was evident with certainty.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r7.anchor: على أن المشي عليه أولى من جهة المعنى , لأن سجود الملائكة عليهم السلام قبل يكون إيمانا بالغيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r8.claim: The narrative order first establishes Adam's knowledge as the proof of his merit, then records the angels' submission and the favor of prostration for his descendants, preserving a clear sequence of argument and favors.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r8.anchor: فذكر ما آتاه من العلم , فلما فرغ من محاجتهم بما أوجب إذعانهم ذكر بنيه بنعمة السجود له

BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r9.claim: After displaying Adam's knowledge, vicegerency, and prostration, God shows Adam's capacity to err and return in repentance, contrasting his return with Iblis's refusal and the angels' submission.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r9.anchor: ليظهر فضل آدم في حال مخالفته على إبليس في حال إبائه مما يبدو على آدم من الرجوع بالتوبة كحال رجوع الملائكة بالتسليم

DURR-FULL:v1p120/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r1.claim: Adam learned the names of all things, down to ordinary vessels and even the smallest bodily terms.
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال: علمه اسم الصحفة والقدر وكل شيء حتى الفسوة والفسية

DURR-FULL:v1p120/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r2.claim: A second report says Adam learned every thing's name, including a dish and the camel, cow, sheep, and tiny terms.
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال: علمه اسم كل شيء حتى علمه القصعة والقصيعة والفسوة والفسية

DURR-FULL:v1p120/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r3.claim: Adam learned every thing's name, including the camel, cow, and sheep.
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال: علمه اسم كل شيء

DURR-FULL:v1p120/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r4.claim: One concise gloss takes all the names to mean everything God created.
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال: ما خلق الله

DURR-FULL:v1p120/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r5.speaker: أبو رافع
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r5.claim: The Prophet says his community was shown to him in water and clay and that he was taught the names as Adam was.
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r5.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: مثلت لي أمتي في الماء والطين وعلمت الأسماء كما علم آدم الأسماء كلها

DURR-FULL:v1p120/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r6.speaker: عطية بن يسر
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r6.claim: A raised report says the names included a thousand crafts; Adam was told to direct descendants seeking worldly livelihood to crafts, not religion, which belongs purely to God, and warns against seeking it through religion.
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r6.anchor: عن عطية بن يسر مرفوعا في قوله {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال علم الله في تلك الأسماء ألف حرفة من الحرف

DURR-FULL:v1p120/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r7.claim: The names were the names of all Adam's descendants, whom God took from his back when He displayed them.
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r7.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال: أسماء ذريته أجمعين {ثم عرضهم} قال: أخذهم من ظهره

DURR-FULL:v1p120/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r8.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r8.claim: Al-Rabiʿ b. Anas interprets the names as the names of the angels.
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r8.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس في قوله {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال: أسماء الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v1p120/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r9.claim: Adam was taught the names of his creatures, named each thing, and assigned everything to its kind.
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r9.anchor: عن قتادة {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال: علم آدم من الأسماء أسماء خلقه ثم قال ما لم تعلم الملائكة فسمى كل شيء باسمه وألجأ كل شيء إلى جنسه

DURR-FULL:v1p120/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r10.claim: The names were the familiar names by which people identify humans, animals, land, sea, plains, donkeys, and other created kinds.
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال: علم الله آدم الأسماء كلها وهي هذه الأسماء التي يتعارف بها الناس انسان دابة وأرض وبحر وسهل وحمار

DURR-FULL:v1p120/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r11.claim: God displayed the names of all the kinds of creatures Adam had been taught and challenged the angels to identify them if their claim was true.
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r11.anchor: {ثم عرضهم على الملائكة} يعني عرض أسماء جميع الأشياء التي علمها آدم من أصناف الخلق

DURR-FULL:v1p121/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r1.claim: Mujahid says the bearers of the names were presented to the angels.
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {ثم عرضهم} قال: عرض أصحاب الأسماء على الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v1p121/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r2.claim: As God began creating Adam, the angels thought no creature would be more honored by God or more knowledgeable than they; Adam's creation tested that assumption.
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال: إن الله لما أخذ في خلق آدم قالت الملائكة: ما الله خالق خلقا أكرم عليه منا ولا أعلم منا

DURR-FULL:v1p121/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r3.speaker: قتادة والحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r3.claim: The angels privately claimed superiority in knowledge and honor; after Adam was created, God commanded them to prostrate, demonstrated his precedence by teaching him the names, and they repented when unable to answer.
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r3.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن قالا: لما أخذ الله في خلق آدم همست الملائكة فيما بينها فقالوا: لن يخلق الله خلقا إلا كنا أعلم منه وأكرم عليه منه

DURR-FULL:v1p121/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r5.claim: They explain the angels' challenge as referring to their claim that Adam's descendants would corrupt the earth and shed blood.
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة في قوله {إن كنتم صادقين} قال: إن بني آدم يفسدون في الأرض ويسفكون الدماء

DURR-FULL:v1p121/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r6.claim: The angels' disclosed speech was their question about placing someone in the earth who would cause corruption there.
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r6.anchor: وفي قوله {وأعلم ما تبدون} قال: قولهم {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها}

AKHFASH:v1p63/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p63/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p63/r1.claim: The masculine object pronoun in “then He presented them” refers to the people who bear the names, as “these” confirms.
AKHFASH:v1p63/r1.anchor: قوله {الأسمآء كلها ثم عرضهم} فيريد عرض عليهم أصحاب الأسماء

AKHFASH:v1p63/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p63/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p63/r2.claim: The challenge did not answer a claim by the angels; it exposed their ignorance of the unseen, like asking someone to tell what he plainly does not know.
AKHFASH:v1p63/r2.anchor: فلم يكن ذلك لان الملائكة ادعوا شيئا، انما أخبر عن جهلهم بعلم الغيب

IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r1.claim: Adam was taught the names of his children one by one and of animals, including the donkey, camel, and horse.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : وعلم ادم الاسماء كلها قال : عرض عليه اسماء ولده انسانا انسانا ، والدواب . فقيل : هذا الحمار ، هذا الجمل ، هذا الفرس .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also says Adam learned names such as the platter and pot, down to coarse bodily terms.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : وعلم ادم الاسماء كلها قال : علمه اسم الصفحة والقدر ، قال : نعم حتى الفسوة والفسية .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r3.claim: Mujahid says Adam was taught the name of every animal, bird, and thing.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد : وعلم ادم الاسماء كلها قال : علمه كل دابة وكل طير وكل شئ .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r4.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r4.claim: The author says similar accounts from Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Qatada agree with Ibn Abbas's view.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r4.anchor: وروى عن مجاهد ، وسعيد بن جبير ، وقتادة نحو قول ابن عباس .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r5.speaker: حميد الشامي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r5.claim: Hamid al-Shami says Adam was taught the stars; the author clarifies that this means their names.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r5.anchor: عن حميد الشامي قال : علم ادم النجوم . قال أبو محمد : يعني اسماء النجوم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r6.claim: Qatada says God presented those names to the angels and challenged them to name them if they were truthful.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r6.anchor: عن قتادة قال : ثم عرض تلك الاسماء على الملائكة فقال : انبؤني باسماء هؤلاء ان كنتم صادقين .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says God presented the creatures to the angels.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r7.anchor: عن السدى : وعلم ادم الاسماء كلها ثم عرض الخلق على الملائكة .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r8.claim: Mujahid identifies the things the angels were asked to name as those Adam had been taught.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p80/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد : فقال : انبئوني باسماء هؤلاء ان كنتم صادقين باسماء هذه التي حدث بها ادم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r1.claim: Adam first learned words for concrete entities humans need to name, recall, or describe, including proper names and classes of animals, plants, stones, and stars.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r1.anchor: أسماء الذوات من الموجودات مثل الأعلام الشخصية وأسماء الأجناس من الحيوان والنبات والحجر والكواكب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur thinks these first words belonged to humanity's first language and included things such as a garden, angel, Adam, Eve, Iblis, tree, and fruit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r2.anchor: ونجد ذلك بحسب اللغة البشرية الأولى ولذلك نرجح أن لا يكون فيما علمه آدم ابتداء شيء من أسماء المعاني والأحداث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r3.claim: He rejects the idea that Adam initially learned abstract and event nouns; these arose later, first expressed by joining an entity name with an event name, as in 'water cold.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r3.anchor: أن لا يكون فيما علمه آدم ابتداء شيء من أسماء المعاني والأحداث ثم طرأت بعد ذلك فكان إذا أراد أن يخبر عن حصول حدث أو أمر معنوي لذات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r4.claim: The later emergence of verbs and adjectives from such noun pairings supports the view that verbal nouns, rather than verbs, are the root of derivation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r4.anchor: وهذا يرجح أن أصل الاشتقاق هو المصادر لا الأفعال لأن المصادر صنف دقيق من نوع الأسماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r5.claim: The definite article in 'the names' marks the whole customary set of things known in that world, the amount that displays Adam's merit and fits divine wisdom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r5.anchor: والتعريف في ( الأسماء ) تعريف الجنس أريد منه الاستغراق للدلالة على أنه علمه جميع أسماء الأشياء المعروفة يومئذ في ذلك العالم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r6.claim: The plural means God taught Adam each name together with its referent; a plural is necessary here, and the popular claim that a definite singular is more inclusive is imprecise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p409/r6.anchor: وتعريف الأسماء يفيد أن الله علم آدم كل اسم ما هو مسماه ومدلوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r1.claim: This verse neither proves nor disproves that languages were divinely fixed and taught to humanity through Adam, since the manner of teaching is left open.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r1.anchor: وليس في هذه الآية دليل على أن اللغات توقيفية أي لقنها الله تعالى البشر على لسان آدم ولا على عدمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r2.claim: All agree that the human capacity for language is divinely inspired, whether God taught Adam one language or all languages and names, inspired them, or created speech in him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r2.anchor: والناس متفقون على أن القدرة عليها إلهام من الله وذلك تعليم منه سواء لقن آدم لغة واحدة أو جميع لغات البشر وأسماء كل شيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r3.speaker: المازري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r3.claim: Al-Maziri says the dispute matters only for whether language may be changed: revealed legal wording may not be altered, while ordinary language may.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r3.anchor: إلا في جواز قلب اللغة والحق أن قلب الألفاظ الشرعية حرام وغيره جائز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur endorses al-Maziri and rejects attempts to give the disagreement any other practical consequence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411/r4.anchor: ولقد أصاب المازري وأخطأ كل من رام أن يجعل لهذا الخلاف ثمرة غير ما ذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r1.claim: Some take then as a temporal sequence, allowing time for Adam to be taught or to devise names before the display.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r1.anchor: قيل عطفه بثم لأن بين ابتداء التعليم وبين العرض مهلة وهي مدة تلقين الأسماء لآدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur prefers then as indicating rank: the display and the demonstration of Adam's merit and God's wisdom outweigh the mere learning of names.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r2.anchor: والأظهر أن ( ثم ) هنا للتراخي الرتبي كشأنها في عطفها الجمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r3.claim: Because a name is relational and entails something named, mentioning names can concisely omit the referents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r3.anchor: كان مفهوم لفظ ( اسم ) من المفهومات الإضافية التي يتوقف تعقلها على تعقل غيرها إذ الاسم لا يكون إلا لمسمى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r4.claim: The pronoun 'them' refers to the named entities, not to the names, since display makes a hidden object manifest and the following question asks for the names of these entities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r4.anchor: وضمير { عرضهم } للمسميات لأنها التي تعرض بقرينة قوله : { أنيئوني بأسماء هؤلاء }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r5.claim: The displayed referents may have been visible images whose names or properties were requested, or symbolic forms that made abstract qualities recognizable, as in allegorical and dream images; the scene exceeds the material world.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p411#2/r5.anchor: والحاصل أن الحال المذكورة في الآية حالة عالم أوسع من عالم المحسوسات والمادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r1.claim: The masculine rational pronoun for the referents uses the Arabic convention of treating a group by its most noble members; 17:36 similarly uses 'all those' of hearing, sight, and heart.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r1.anchor: وإعادة ضمير المذكر العاقل على المسميات في قوله : { عرضهم } للتغليب لأن أشرف المعروضات ذوات العقلاء وصفاتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r2.claim: The following question is coordinated as a consequence of the display.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { فقال أنبئوني } تفريع على العرض وقرن بالفاء لذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r3.claim: The command to inform is a challenge meant to expose inability, not an impossible task as some commentators thought; this figurative command presupposes that the challenger knows the asked matter and the angels' inability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r3.anchor: أمر نعجيز بقرينة كون المأمور يعلم أن الآمر عالم بذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r4.claim: Inbāʾ is telling a significant, eagerly sought report, so it entails imparting knowledge and is more specific than ordinary reporting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412/r4.anchor: والإنباء الإخبار بالنبأ وهو الخبر ذو الفائدة العظيمة والأهمية بحيث يحرص السامعون على اكتسابه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r1.claim: The condition may challenge an implied claim that the angels were superior to Adam, if their statement about glorifying God implied that they deserved the vicegerency.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r1.anchor: إن كنتم صادقين في أنكم أفضل من هذا المخلوق إن كان قولهم : { ونحن نسبح } الخ تعريضا بأنهم أحقاء بذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, it asks whether their objection that Adam was unfit for vicegerency was true; on Ibn Ashur's chosen reading, their praise was submission or a public declaration that they did not object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r2.anchor: أو أراد إن كنتم صادقين في عدم جدارة آدم بالخلافة كما دل عليه قولهم : { أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r3.claim: The ability to name things entails rational and practical knowledge suited to stewardship: humans can govern, guide, analyze, and place things rightly, whereas angels perform fixed tasks under divine direction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r3.anchor: وكل ذلك يستلزم ثبوت العالمية بالفعل أو بالقوة ، وصاحب هذا الوصف هو الجدير بالاستخلاف في العالم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r4.claim: The angels' inability to name things does not by itself refute their claim about human unfitness, but it prepares for Adam's answer; God's statement that He knows what they do not supports this setup.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p412#2/r4.anchor: فإن كان محل الصدق هو دعواهم أنهم أجدر فقد ثبت عدمها ، وإن كان محل التصديق هو دعواهم أن البشر غير صالح للاستخلاف فانتفاء الإنباء لا يدل على انتفاء دعواهم

FARRA:v1p26/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p26/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p26/r1.claim: The masculine plural عرضهم treats the displayed items as embodied persons; if the names alone were intended, feminine forms would also work, and عرضها could refer to names or embodied figures.
FARRA:v1p26/r1.anchor: على مذهب شخوص العالمين وسائر العالم

FARRA:v1p26/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p26/r2.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v1p26/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud’s reading has the feminine plural عرضهن, consistent with referring to names without their embodied referents.

FARRA:v1p26/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p26/r3.speaker: أبي
FARRA:v1p26/r3.claim: Ubayy’s reading has عرضها, which can refer either to the names or to the displayed figures.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r11.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r11.claim: Some say God taught Adam the names by immediate inspiration, giving him necessary knowledge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r11.anchor: تعليم آدم هنا عند قوم إلهام علمه ضرورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r12.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r12.claim: Others say Adam was taught through speech, either by an angel or by divine speech before he descended to earth, preserving Moses’s unique distinction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r12.anchor: بل تعليم بقول، فإما بواسطة ملك، أو بتكليم قبل هبوطه الأرض، فلا يشارك موسى- عليه السلام- في خاصته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r13.speaker: اليماني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r13.claim: The Yamānī reading has the verb in the passive, wa-ʿullima, with Ādam as its nominative subject.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r13.anchor: وقرأ اليماني: «وعلم» بضم العين على بناء الفعل للمفعول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r14.speaker: أبو الفتح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r14.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ identifies this passive reading as the reading of Yazīd al-Barbarī.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r15.claim: One etymology derives Ādam from adama, reddishness tending toward black; its plurals are udm and awādim, and it is indeclinable.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r15.anchor: وآدم أفعل مشتق من الأدمة وهي حمرة تميل إلى السواد، وجمعه أدم وأوادم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r16.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r16.claim: Another etymology derives Ādam from the surface of the earth, as if an angel formed it; this account gives plurals Ādamūn and awādim and requires declension.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r16.anchor: وقيل آدم وزنه فاعل مشتق من أديم الأرض، كأن الملك آدمها وجمعه آدمون وأوادم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r1.speaker: الطبري
