IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Ādam is a quadriliteral verb used as a name.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet says Ādam was created from all the earth’s soil, so his descendants vary in color, temperament, and moral character.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r2.anchor: خلق الله آدم من أديم الأرض كلها فخرجت ذريته على نحو ذلك منهم الأبيض والأسود والأسمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r3.speaker: جمهور الأمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r3.claim: The majority of the community understand the names as labels for things; another group takes them to mean the persons themselves, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the first view because the verb “taught him” supports it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r3.anchor: فقال جمهور الأمة: «علمه التسميات» وقال قوم: «عرض عليه الأشخاص»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and Mujāhid say Adam learned the names of every created thing, small and great.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r4.anchor: علمه اسم كل شيء من جميع المخلوقات دقيقها وجليلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r5.speaker: حميد الشامي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r5.claim: Ḥumayd al-Shāmī restricts the names to the stars.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r6.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r6.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym restricts the names to the angels.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r7.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd says Adam learned only the names of his descendants.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r8.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Adam learned the names of his descendants and the angels, preferring this because the next clause says God displayed “them” to the angels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r8.anchor: وقال الطبري: «علمه أسماء ذريته والملائكة» ، واختار هذا ورجحه بقوله تعالى: ثم عرضهم على الملائكة.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r9.speaker: النقاش عن ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r9.claim: Al-Naqqāsh transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that God taught Adam one word from which he recognized all names.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r9.anchor: حكى النقاش عن ابن عباس أنه تعالى علمه كلمة واحدة عرف منها جميع الأسماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r10.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r10.claim: Some say Adam learned generic names such as mountains, horses, and valleys, without assigning the names his descendants later used.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r10.anchor: علمه أسماء الأجناس، كالجبال والخيل والأودية ونحو ذلك، دون أن يعين ما سمته ذريته منها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r11.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r11.claim: Ibn Qutayba says Adam learned the names of everything God created on earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r11.anchor: علمه أسماء ما خلق في الأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r12.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r12.claim: Some say Adam learned names in one language, while his descendants later agreed on names for other things.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r12.anchor: علمه الأسماء بلغة واحدة، ثم وقع الاصطلاح من ذريته فيما سواها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r13.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r13.claim: Others say Adam learned names in every language spoken by his descendants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r13.anchor: بل علمه الأسماء بكل لغة تكلمت بها ذريته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r14.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r14.claim: Ibn Jinnī reports Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī’s extreme claim that Adam knew everything, even grammar as advanced as Sībawayh’s; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this wrong on several grounds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p119/r14.anchor: حكى ابن جني عن أبي علي الفارسي أنه قال: «علم الله تعالى آدم كل شيء، حتى إنه كان يحسن من النحو مثل ما أحسن سيبويه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r1.speaker: أكثر العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r1.claim: Most scholars say God taught Adam the uses of every thing and what is beneficial for it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r1.anchor: علمه تعالى منافع كل شيء ولما يصلح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r2.claim: Some say God displayed the objects to Adam during the teaching; others say He described them without displaying their physical forms.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya regards both object-display and verbal-description accounts as possibilities people have held.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r3.anchor: وهذه كلها احتمالات، قال الناس بها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r4.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reads the feminine singular “then He displayed them.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads the feminine plural “then He displayed them.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and others say God displayed the objects themselves to the angels; Ibn ʿAbbās and others say He displayed the names.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r6.anchor: فقال ابن مسعود وغيره: عرض الأشخاص. وقال ابن عباس وغيره: عرض الأسماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r7.claim: If the names meant all things, “displayed them” can mean presenting each community or kind; if they meant labels, Ubayy’s feminine reading fits.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r7.anchor: عرضهم أمة أمة ونوعا نوعا، ومن قال في الأسماء إنها التسميات استقام على قراءة أبي: «عرضها»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r8.claim: The masculine plural “them” can refer to the objects because the word “names” can signify the objects named.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r8.anchor: إن لفظ الأسماء يدل على الأشخاص، فلذلك ساغ أن يقول للأسماء عرضهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r9.claim: Anbiʾūnī means “inform me”; nabaʾ means news, and the word nabīʾ derives from it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r9.anchor: وأنبئوني معناه: أخبروني، والنبأ الخبر، ومنه النبيء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r10.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r10.claim: Some infer that the command to inform the angels charges them with what they cannot do, showing that such a charge is permissible because God knew they lacked the knowledge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r10.anchor: يخرج من هذا الأمر بالإنباء تكليف ما لا يطاق، ويتقرر جوازه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r11.speaker: المحققون من أهل التأويل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r11.claim: More discerning exegetes reject the impossible-charge reading: the command only elicits an acknowledgment and confirmation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r11.anchor: ليس هذا على جهة التكليف وإنما هو على جهة التقرير والتوقيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r12.claim: The demonstrative “these” naturally indicates that visible persons were present when God displayed them to the angels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r12.anchor: هؤلاء ظاهره حضور أشخاص، وذلك عند العرض على الملائكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r13.claim: The verse does not require “name” to mean its referent, despite Makki and al-Mahdawī’s view; the demonstrative can point to absent referents through their names or to displayed bodies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r13.anchor: وليس في هذه الآية ما يوجب أن الاسم أريد به المسمى كما ذهب إليه مكي والمهدوي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s own reading is that God taught Adam names, displayed concrete kinds first to Adam and then to the angels, and asked the angels to name them before Adam did so.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r14.anchor: والذي يظهر أن الله تعالى علم آدم الأسماء وعرض مع ذلك عليه الأجناس أشخاصا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r15.claim: Hāʾulāʾ is built on kasra; shortening it is a dialect of Tamīm, some Qays, and Asad, and al-Aʿshā supplies a poetic example.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r15.anchor: وهؤلاء لفظ مبني على الكسر والقصر فيه لغة تميم وبعض قيس وأسد، قال الأعشى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya cites al-Aʿshā in the khafīf meter as evidence for the shortened form of hāʾulā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p120/r16.anchor: وهؤلاء لفظ مبني على الكسر والقصر فيه لغة تميم وبعض قيس وأسد، قال الأعشى: [الخفيف] .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r1.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r1.claim: Sībawayh says kuntum is jussive under the conditional, with the answer supplied by the preceding clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r1.anchor: وكنتم في موضع الجزم بالشرط، والجواب عند سيبويه فيما قبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r2.speaker: المبرد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad instead treats the answer as omitted: “if you are truthful, then inform Me.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r2.anchor: وعند المبرد محذوف، والتقدير: إن كنتم صادقين فأنبئوني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وناس من أصحاب النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and some Companions take “if you are truthful” to refer to the angels’ claim that the human successor would corrupt and shed blood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r3.anchor: معنى الآية: إن كنتم صادقين في أن الخليفة يفسد ويسفك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r4.claim: Others understand it as referring to the angels’ claim that, if appointed, they would glorify God and sanctify Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r4.anchor: صادقين في أني إن استخلفتكم سبحتم بحمدي وقدستم لي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r5.claim: A report from al-Ḥasan and Qatāda says the angels expected no creation to know more or be more honored than they; God showed Adam’s knowledge and honor to correct their assumption.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r5.anchor: روي أن الملائكة قالت حين خلق الله آدم: ليخلق ربنا ما شاء فلن يخلق خلقا أعلم منا ولا أكرم عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r6.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r6.claim: Some say the angels are challenged to be truthful in their claim to knowledge; others say they must answer accurately because they know the names, a view al-Naqqāsh records.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r6.anchor: إن كنتم صادقين في جواب السؤال عالمين بالأسماء. قالوا: ولذلك لم يسغ للملائكة الاجتهاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r7.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r7.claim: Al-Naqqāsh argues that without the accuracy condition, the angels could have reasoned as did the man whom God caused to die for a hundred years, who guessed how long he had stayed and was not rebuked.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r7.anchor: ولو لم يشترط عليهم الصدق في الإنباء لجاز لهم الاجتهاد كما جاز للذي أماته الله مائة عام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says all these explanations of the angels’ truthfulness are possible.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r9.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects an interpretation reported from some exegetes that in kuntum means “when you were.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r9.anchor: معنى إن كنتم «إذ كنتم» . قال الطبري: وهذا خطأ.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#3/r1.claim: The names taught to Adam were the names of the things created on earth.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#3/r1.anchor: يريد أسماء ما خلق في الأرض

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#3/r2.claim: God displayed the actual created beings to the angels and asked them to name them.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#3/r2.anchor: أي عرض أعيان الخلق عليهم {فقال أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء}

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جبير، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r1.claim: Adam was named because he was created from the surface soil of the earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r1.anchor: لأنه خلق من أديم الأرض قاله ابن عباس وابن جبير و الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r2.speaker: الضحاك، النضر بن شميل، قطرب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r2.claim: A second etymology derives Adam from the color called adama.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r2.anchor: انه من الأدمة في اللون قاله الضحاك والنضر بن شميل وقطرب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير، مجاهد، قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r3.claim: One view is that God taught Adam every name.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r3.anchor: أنه علمه كل الاسماء وهذا قول ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير و مجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r4.speaker: أبو القالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r4.claim: Among views limiting the lesson to particular referents, Adam learned the angels’ names.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r4.anchor: أنه علمه أسماء الملائكة قاله أبو القالية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r5.claim: Another view says Adam learned category names, such as human, angel, jinn, and bird, without their subtypes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r5.anchor: أسماء الاجناس دون أنواعها كقولك إنسان وملك وجني وطائر قاله عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r6.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل، ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r6.claim: Another view identifies the lesson as names of earthly creatures, including animals, vermin, and birds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r6.anchor: أسماء ما خلق من الأرض من الدواب والهوام والطير قال الكلبي و مقاتل وابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r7.claim: A fourth restricted interpretation says Adam learned the names of his descendants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p62/r7.anchor: أنه علمه أسماء ذريه قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r1.claim: The beings displayed before the angels were the actual individual creatures.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r1.anchor: يريد أعيان الخلق على الملائكة قال ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r2.claim: The angels addressed here were specifically those who had been with Iblis.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r2.anchor: الملائكة هاهنا هم الذين كانوا مع إبليس خاصة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r3.claim: Anbiʾūnī means tell me or inform me.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r4.claim: The challenge means: if you claim no creature I create will surpass you in virtue and knowledge, name these beings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r4.anchor: إن كنتم صادقين أني لا أخلق خلقا هو أفضل منكم وأعلم قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r5.speaker: السدي عن أشياخه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r5.claim: Alternatively, the challenge concerns their claim about God placing a corrupting creature on earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63/r5.anchor: أني أجعل فيها من يفسد فيها قاله السدي عن أشياخه

MAJAZ:v1p36/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p36/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p36/r1.claim: The names taught to Adam were the names of created beings.

MAJAZ:v1p36/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p36/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p36/r2.claim: The pronoun in “then He displayed them” refers to the created beings.
MAJAZ:v1p36/r2.anchor: «ثم عرضهم على الملائكة» (31) أي عرض الخلق.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r1.claim: The passage shows Adam's superiority over the angels through knowledge of all names; it follows their prostration in chronology but is placed first to answer their question about the vicegerent's creation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r1.anchor: هذا مقام ذكر الله تعالى فيه شرف آدم على الملائكة، بما اختصه به من علم أسماء كل شيء دونهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r2.claim: From Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi says Adam was shown the names of his children one by one and of animals such as donkey, camel, and horse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r2.anchor: وقال السدي، عمن حدثه، عن ابن عباس: {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال: عرض عليه أسماء ولده إنسانا إنسانا، والدواب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r3.claim: From Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak identifies the names as familiar terms for people, animals, sky, earth, plain, sea, camel, donkey, and other kinds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس: {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال: هي هذه الأسماء التي يتعارف بها الناس: إنسان، ودابة، وسماء، وأرض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Adam was taught names of ordinary objects, including a serving dish and cooking pot, down to coarse and delicate bodily terms.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن معبد، عن ابن عباس: {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال: علمه اسم الصحفة والقدر، قال: نعم حتى الفسوة والفسية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says Adam learned the name of every animal, bird, and thing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} قال: علمه اسم كل دابة، وكل طير، وكل شيء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة وغيرهم من السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada, and other early authorities likewise say Adam learned names of everything.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r6.anchor: وكذلك روي عن سعيد بن جبير وقتادة وغيرهم من السلف: أنه علمه أسماء كل شيء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r7.speaker: الربيع
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r7.claim: Al-Rabi reports that the names taught to Adam were the angels' names.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r7.anchor: وقال الربيع في رواية عنه: أسماء الملائكة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r8.speaker: حميد الشامي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r8.claim: Humayd al-Shami says the names were the names of the stars.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r9.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r9.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says Adam learned the names of all his descendants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r9.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: علمه أسماء ذريته كلهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r10.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r10.claim: Ibn Jarir selects the view that Adam learned angels' and descendants' names, reasoning that the masculine rational plural in عرضهم points to rational beings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r10.anchor: واختار ابن جرير أنه علمه أسماء الملائكة وأسماء الذرية؛ لأنه قال: {ثم عرضهم} وهذا عبارة عما يعقل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects Ibn Jarir's grammatical inference as necessary: other kinds may also be included, with the rational plural used by predominance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r11.anchor: وهذا الذي رجح به ليس بلازم، فإنه لا ينفي أن يدخل معهم غيرهم، ويعبر عن الجميع بصيغة من يعقل للتغليب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r12.claim: As an analogy for using a rational plural for a mixed group, Ibn Kathir cites the verse saying every animal was created from water, though they move in different ways.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222#2/r12.anchor: كما قال: {والله خلق كل دابة من ماء فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين ومنهم من يمشي على أربع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r1.claim: Ibn Masud's reading uses the feminine plural عرضهن for what was displayed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r1.anchor: وقد قرأ عبد الله بن مسعود: "ثم عرضهن"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r2.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b reads عرضها, which is explained as referring to the heavens.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب: "ثم عرضها" أي: السماوات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir considers it correct that Adam was taught the names of all things, both their entities and their actions, including large and diminutive forms.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r3.anchor: والصحيح أنه علمه أسماء الأشياء كلها: ذواتها وأفعالها؛ كما قال ابن عباس حتى الفسوة والفسية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r4.claim: In the intercession report transmitted from Anas, people ask Adam to intercede because God created him by His hand, angels prostrated to him, and he was taught every name; Adam declines and directs them to other prophets.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p223/r4.anchor: وعلمك أسماء كل شيء، فاشفع لنا عند ربك حتى يريحنا من مكاننا هذا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r1.claim: The intercession hadith shows Adam was taught the names of every created thing; عرضهم refers to the named entities themselves.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r1.anchor: فدل هذا على أنه علمه أسماء جميع المخلوقات؛ ولهذا قال: {ثم عرضهم على الملائكة} يعني: المسميات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r2.claim: Qatada says God displayed those names to the angels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r2.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة قال: ثم عرض تلك الأسماء على الملائكة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r3.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, and other Companions says God displayed the creatures to the angels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس -وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس من الصحابة: {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} ثم عرض الخلق على الملائكة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r4.claim: Mujahid says the holders of the names were displayed to the angels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r4.anchor: وقال ابن جريج، عن مجاهد: {ثم عرضهم} عرض أصحاب الأسماء على الملائكة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r5.claim: Hasan and Qatada say Adam learned each thing's name, named everything, and was shown each community in turn.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r5.anchor: عن الحسن -وأبي بكر، عن الحسن وقتادة -قالا علمه اسم كل شيء، وجعل يسمي كل شيء باسمه، وعرضت عليه أمة أمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r6.claim: Hasan and Qatada interpret the challenge as asking angels to name what they had been shown, given their claim to greater knowledge of created beings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r6.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة في قوله: {إن كنتم صادقين} إني لم أخلق خلقا إلا كنتم أعلم منه، فأخبروني بأسماء هؤلاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r7.claim: From Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak explains if you are truthful as meaning: if you know that God would not place a vicegerent on earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r7.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس: {إن كنتم صادقين} إن كنتم تعلمون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r8.claim: Al-Suddi, reporting Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, and other Companions, says the challenge addresses their claim that Adam's descendants would corrupt the earth and shed blood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس -وعن مرة عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس من الصحابة: إن كنتم صادقين أن بني آدم يفسدون في الأرض ويسفكون الدماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r9.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r9.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers Ibn Abbas's interpretation: God challenges the angels who questioned the vicegerent to name the beings, exposing that they cannot know unseen future events or uncreated matters.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p224/r9.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك تأويل ابن عباس ومن قال بقوله، ومعنى ذلك فقال: أنبئوني بأسماء من عرضته عليكم أيها الملائكة القائلون

NAHHAS:v1p208/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p208/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p208/r3.claim: Adam and the names are the two objects of علم; grammarians unanimously treat proper-name Adam as diptote, and Basrans require two causes to prevent declension.
NAHHAS:v1p208/r3.anchor: آدم و الأسماء مفعولان لعلم وآدم لا ينصرف في المعرفة بإجماع النحويين

NAHHAS:v1p208/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p208/r4.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p208/r4.claim: They keep Adam diptote even when indefinite and not adjectival; al-Akhfash Saʿid allows declension then because he attributes the restriction to adjectival use on an afʿal pattern.
NAHHAS:v1p208/r4.anchor: لم يصرفه الخليل وسيبويه وصرفه الأخفش سعيد لأنه إنما منعه من الصرف

NAHHAS:v1p208/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p208/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p208/r5.claim: He sides with Sibawayh: adjective versus non-adjective does not change the ruling, since the form is effectively the same.
NAHHAS:v1p208/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق القول قول سيبويه لا يفرق بين النعت وغيره لأنه هو ذاك بعينه

NAHHAS:v1p208/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p208/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p208/r6.claim: The plural of Adam as an adjective is أدم; as a non-adjective it is آدمون or أوادم.
NAHHAS:v1p208/r6.anchor: وجمع آدم إذا كان صفة أدم فإن لم يكن نعتا فجمعه آدمون وأوادم

NAHHAS:v1p208/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p208/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p208/r7.claim: أنبئوني has hamzat qaṭʿ because it derives from أنبأ ينبئ; the hamza can be softened or replaced, yielding أنبوني like أعطوني.
NAHHAS:v1p208/r7.anchor: ( فقال أنبئوني ) ألف قطع لأنها من أنبأ ينبىء فإن خففت الهمزة

NAHHAS:v1p208/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p208/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p208/r8.claim: In بأسماء هؤلاء, the preposition makes أسماء genitive and هؤلاء is genitive by annexation while remaining indeclinable on kasra.
NAHHAS:v1p208/r8.anchor: بأسماء مخفوض بالباء و هؤلاء في موضع مخفوض بالإضافة إلى أنه مبني

NAHHAS:v1p208/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p208/r9.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p208/r9.claim: For the two hamzas in هؤلاء إن, they prefer retaining the first and softening the second; this is Nāfiʿ's reading.
NAHHAS:v1p208/r9.anchor: خففت الهمزة الثانية وحققت الأولى وهو أجود الوجوه عند الخليل وسيبويه وهي قراءة نافع

NAHHAS:v1p208/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p208/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p208/r10.claim: Other pronunciations soften the first and retain the second, pronounce both fully, or soften both; the same-hamza approach is attributed to Abū ʿAmr.
NAHHAS:v1p208/r10.anchor: خففت الأولى وحققت الثانية فقلت هؤلاان كنتم وان شئت حققتهما جميعا

NAHHAS:v1p208/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p208/r11.speaker: تميم وبعض أسد وقيس
NAHHAS:v1p208/r11.claim: These tribes shorten هؤلاء; the resulting form before إن is هاؤلا.
NAHHAS:v1p208/r11.anchor: وتميم وبعض أسد وقيس يقصرون هؤلا فعلى لغتهم هاؤلا إن كنتم

JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r1.claim: These readers use one short measure for hāʾulāʾ and lengthen ūlāʾ; the other readers lengthen both equally throughout the Qur’an.
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: هؤلاء بمدة واحدة لا يمدونها إلا على قدر خروج الألف، ويمدون أولاء

JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r2.claim: The remaining readers give both parts of hāʾulāʾ two measures equally throughout the Qur’an, preserving the original form.
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r2.anchor: والباقون يمدون مدتين سواء في كل القرآن، فالأول للتخفيف من غير إخلال، والثاني على الأصل والتمام

JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع برواية ورش وابن كثير برواية القواس ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r3.claim: For two same-vowel hamzas across words, these readers pronounce the first and soften the second, indicating its vowel.
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r3.anchor: فأبو جعفر ونافع برواية ورش وابن كثير برواية القواس ويعقوب يهمزون الأولى ويخففون الثانية ويشيرون بالكسر إليها

JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير برواية البزي
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r4.claim: When two across-word hamzas have matching vowels, these readers pronounce one and omit the other.
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r4.anchor: وأبو عمرو وابن كثير برواية البزي يهمزون همزة واحدة، ويتركون إحداهما أصلا إذا كانا متفقتين

JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r5.speaker: نافع برواية إسماعيل وابن كثير برواية ابن فليح
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r5.claim: These readers soften the first hamza and fully pronounce the second when the two hamzas match.
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r5.anchor: ونافع برواية إسماعيل، وابن كثير برواية ابن فليح بتليين الأولى وتحقيق الثانية

JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r6.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة وعاصم والكسائي
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r6.claim: These readers pronounce both hamzas, whether the two across-word hamzas have matching vowels or differ.
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r6.anchor: ابن عامر وحمزة وعاصم والكسائي فيهمزون همزتين في جميع ذلك متفقتين كانتا أو مختلفتين

JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r7.claim: The softened or deleted hamza eases pronunciation, while retaining the hamza follows the original form.
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r7.anchor: أما الحذف والتليين فللتخفيف، والهمز على الأصل

JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r8.claim: Ādam can mean brownish hue in people, whiteness in gazelles and camels, and the earth’s face; adama also means duskiness.
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r8.anchor: الأدمة في الناس شربة بسواد، وفي الظباء والإبل بياض، والأدمة نحو السمرة، وأدمة الأرض وجهها

JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r9.claim: One etymology derives Ādam from the earth’s surface; on this derivation the name is declinable when indefinite.
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r9.anchor: قيل: مأخوذ من أديم الأرض، فإذا سميت به في هذا الوجه ثم نكرته صرفته

JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r10.claim: Another etymology derives Ādam from the color or quality of adama; on this derivation it is not declinable when indefinite.
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: أخذ من الأدمة على معنى اللون والصفة، فإذا سميت به ثم نكرته في هذا الوجه لم تصرفه

JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r11.claim: Asmāʾ is the plural of ism, as in the verse about God’s beautiful names.
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r11.anchor: والأسماء: جمع اسم، ومنه: (ولله الأسماء الحسنى)

JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r12.claim: Kull literally encompasses all parts, though it can also function as emphasis like ajmaʿīn; Arabic places kull first in such wording.
JISHUMI:v1p315#2/r12.anchor: حقيقته: الإحاطة بالأبعاض يقال: أبعض القوم أتاك أم كلهم، وقد يكون تأكيدا نحو أجمعين،

JISHUMI:v1p317/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r1.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v1p317/r1.claim: ʿArḍ originally means a side or region; width is named as the opposite of length, and presenting goods displays their sides.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: العرض أصله في اللغة الناحية من نواحي الشيء، فمن ذلك العرض خلاف الطول

JISHUMI:v1p317/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p317/r2.claim: To turn away is to withdraw; a person’s ʿarḍ was variously glossed as what earns praise or blame, good character, or lineage.

JISHUMI:v1p317/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r3.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v1p317/r3.claim: ʿArḍ is the aspect of a person that he protects from harm and disgrace.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r3.anchor: قال علي بن عيسى: والذي عندي أنه ناحية الرجل التي يصونها عن المكروه والشين

JISHUMI:v1p317/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p317/r4.claim: The root sense of ʿarḍ is appearance: width makes an object visible, presentation displays it, and an ʿaraḍ is an accident that alters a body’s quality.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r4.anchor: وقيل: أصل العرض الظهور، فالعرض خلاف الطول لأن به يظهر، وعرضته على البيع أي أظهرته

JISHUMI:v1p317/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p317/r5.claim: Inbāʾ means informing; nabaʾ is news, and some restrict the word to news of great importance.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r5.anchor: والإنباء الإخبار والإعلام، والنبأ بالهمز الخبر، وأنبأه أخبره

JISHUMI:v1p317/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p317/r6.claim: Some say nabaʾ is used only for news of momentous significance.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r6.anchor: وقيل: النبأ لا يستعمل إلا في شيء عظيم شأنه

JISHUMI:v1p317/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p317/r7.claim: The pronoun in ʿaraḍahum refers to created beings that God showed Adam; Ibn ʿAbbās summarizes this as displaying creation.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r7.anchor: وروي أنه خلق الأشخاص وعرضهم عليه، قال ابن عباس: عرض الخلق

JISHUMI:v1p317/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r8.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v1p317/r8.claim: Another grammatical account supplies “owners of the names”; nonrational beings take the plural masculine by predominance.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r8.anchor: وقيل: فيه إضمار أراد أصحاب الأسماء، وفيه ما لا يعقل، فجرى على التغليب، عن مجاهد

JISHUMI:v1p317/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p317/r9.claim: The suggestion that the pronoun refers to the names themselves is invalid because names as abstractions cannot be presented, and the wording does not fit presentation in heaven.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r9.anchor: وقيل: عرض الأسماء، وهذا لا يصح؛ لأن عرض نفس الأسماء لا يمكن، ولأنه لا يقال: عرضهم في السماء.

JISHUMI:v1p317/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r10.speaker: قتادة وغيره
JISHUMI:v1p317/r10.claim: God taught Adam the meanings of names, since names without meanings convey nothing.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r10.anchor: يعني معاني الأسماء؛ إذ الأسماء من غير معان لا تفيد، عن قتادة وغيره

JISHUMI:v1p317/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r11.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وأكثر المفسرين
JISHUMI:v1p317/r11.claim: The comprehensive teaching included crafts, tools, cultivation, foods, medicines, mining, trees, fruits and their uses, and what serves religion and worldly life.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r11.anchor: علمه الصناعات والآلات وعمارة الأرض والأطعمة والأدوية واستخراج المعادن وغرس الأشجار وأسماء الثمار ومنافعها

JISHUMI:v1p317/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r12.speaker: الربيع
JISHUMI:v1p317/r12.claim: An alternative says Adam was taught the names of the angels.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r12.anchor: وقيل: علمه أسماء الملائكة، عن الربيع

JISHUMI:v1p317/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r13.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v1p317/r13.claim: Another alternative says Adam was taught the names of his descendants.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r13.anchor: وقيل: أسماء ذريته، عن ابن زيد

JISHUMI:v1p317/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p317/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p317/r14.claim: The comprehensive interpretation is stronger because the wording says all names, and most scholars hold it.
JISHUMI:v1p317/r14.anchor: والأول: أوجه؛ لعموم الأسماء، وليس عليه أكثر أهل العلم

JISHUMI:v1p318/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p318/r1.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p318/r1.claim: Adam was taught every language; his children inherited them, later peoples adopted familiar tongues, and forgotten languages explain their diversity; crafts and the uses and harms of things were also taught.
JISHUMI:v1p318/r1.anchor: نعم، عن أبي علي، فإنه تعالى علمه جميع اللغات فأخذ منه ولده، فلما تفرقوا تكلم كل قوم بلسان ألفوه

JISHUMI:v1p318/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p318/r2.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p318/r2.claim: An alternative says Adam learned every language except the language in which God addressed him, which arose by convention.
JISHUMI:v1p318/r2.anchor: وقيل: علمه سائر اللغات إلا اللغة التي خوطب بها فإنها بمواضعة

JISHUMI:v1p318/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p318/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p318/r3.claim: One account says God made Adam know the names by necessity; another says He taught him the angels’ language, through which Adam learned all languages.
JISHUMI:v1p318/r3.anchor: فقيل: بأن اضطره إلى العلم بها، وقيل: علمه لغة الملائكة، ثم إن الله علمه بتلك اللغة سائر اللغات

JISHUMI:v1p318/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p318/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p318/r4.claim: God taught names of individual beings by bringing each thing before Adam and teaching its name in every language, purpose, benefit, and harm; Adam did likewise for the angels.
JISHUMI:v1p318/r4.anchor: بأن أحضر ذلك الشيء وعلمه اسمه بكل لغة، وأنه لأي شيء يصلح، وأي نفع، وأي ضرر

JISHUMI:v1p318/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p318/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p318/r5.claim: The angels knew some of the information because their commissioning preceded Adam’s.
JISHUMI:v1p318/r5.anchor: كانت تعرف بعض ذلك؛ لأن تكليفها كان متقدما

JISHUMI:v1p318/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p318/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p318/r6.claim: Another account distributes languages, useful knowledge, and crafts among angelic groups, who recognized Adam’s truth when he listed them all.
JISHUMI:v1p318/r6.anchor: كانت تلك اللغات ومعرفة المصالح متفرقة في الملائكة، كل فريق يتكلم بلغة، ويعلم بعض تلك الحرف

JISHUMI:v1p318/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p318/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p318/r7.claim: The angels may instead have known because God informed them before creating Adam.
JISHUMI:v1p318/r7.anchor: وقيل: كانت تعلم جميع ذلك بأن أخبرهم الله تعالى قبل خلق آدم

JISHUMI:v1p318/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p318/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p318/r8.claim: Another account says a miracle established Adam’s truthfulness to the angels.
JISHUMI:v1p318/r8.anchor: وقيل: بالمعجزة، وعلموا صدقه في ذلك

JISHUMI:v1p318/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p318/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p318/r9.claim: This was Adam’s miracle because it exceeded ordinary experience; God perfected his intellect, commissioned him as a prophet, and made this his miracle.
JISHUMI:v1p318/r9.anchor: نعم لأنه خارج عن العادة، فإنه تعالى كما خلقه أكمل عقله وبعثه نبيا، وجعل معجزته ذلك

JISHUMI:v1p318/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p318/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p318/r10.claim: God presented the beings after creating them; alternatively, He impressed their forms upon the angels’ hearts, and asked for the names and uses of the named things.
JISHUMI:v1p318/r10.anchor: قيل: عرضهم بعد أن خلقهم، وقيل: صورهم لقلوب الملائكة فقال أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء

JISHUMI:v1p318/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p318/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p318/r11.claim: One explanation says the angels had thought that a vicegerent from among themselves would avoid the corruption expected from Adam’s progeny and be better for them; the challenge exposed their ignorance of hidden realities.
JISHUMI:v1p318/r11.anchor: هجس في نفوسهم أنه لو كان الخليفة منهم بدلا من آدم وذريته لم يكن الفساد وأن ذلك أصلح لهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r1.claim: Adam was named from adīm, the visible face of the earth, from which he was created.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r1.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس , وقد روى أبو موسى الأشعري قال

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r2.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r2.claim: The Prophet said Adam was created from a handful gathered from all the earth, so his descendants reflect its colors, temperaments, and qualities.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r2.anchor: وقد روى أبو موسى الأشعري قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إن الله تعالى خلق آدم من قبضة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r3.claim: Another etymology derives Adam from adama, meaning complexion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r3.anchor: والثاني : أنه مأخوذ من الأدمة , وهي اللون

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r4.claim: The names taught to Adam have three reported referents: angels, his descendants, or all things.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r4.anchor: وفي الأسماء التي علمها الله تعالى آدم , ثلاثة أقوال : أحدها : أسماء الملائكة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Mujahid identify the taught names as the names of all things.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r5.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس , وقتادة , ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r6.claim: One view limits the teaching to names without meanings; another says Adam learned names and meanings, since names without meanings have no benefit and meanings are intended, with names as their signs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r6.anchor: ثم فيه وجهان : أحدهما : أن التعليم إنما كان مقصورا على الاسم دون المعنى . والثاني : أنه علمه الأسماء ومعانيها , إذ لا فائدة في علم الأسماء بلا معاني

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r7.claim: If only the words were taught, one view says Adam learned them in his own language.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r7.anchor: أنه علمه إياها باللغة , التي كان يتكلم بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r8.claim: If only the words were taught, another view says Adam learned every language and taught them to his children; dispersed peoples kept a familiar language and forgot the rest.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r8.anchor: أنه علمه بجميع اللغات , وعلمها آدم ولده , فلما تفرقوا تكلم كل قوم منهم بلسان

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r9.claim: Some claim all peoples awoke after one night speaking different languages and forgetting the others; the author calls this impossible by common custom.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r9.anchor: وزعم قوم أنهم أصبحوا وكل منهم يتكلمون بلغة قد نسوا غيرها في ليلة واحدة , ومثل هذا في العرف ممتنع

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r10.claim: The display may have shown the names without their referents, or the beings named by them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r10.anchor: وفيما عرضه عليهم قولان : أحدهما : أنه عرض عليهم الأسماء دون المسميات . والثاني : أنه عرض عليهم المسمين بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r11.claim: Ibn Masud's reading says “and displayed them” in the feminine plural.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r11.anchor: وفي حرف ابن مسعود : { وعرضهن } وفي حرف أبي : { وعرضها }

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r12.speaker: أبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r12.claim: Ubayy's reading has the feminine singular “and displayed it.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r12.anchor: وفي حرف أبي : { وعرضها } فكان الأصح توجه العرض إلى المسمين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r13.claim: The sounder interpretation takes the display as directed to the named beings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r13.anchor: فكان الأصح توجه العرض إلى المسمين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r14.claim: The display may have taken place after the beings were created, or their forms may have been shown to the angels' minds before creation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r14.anchor: ثم في زمان عرضهم قولان : أحدهما : أنه عرضهم بعد أن خلقهم . والثاني : أنه صورهم لقلوب الملائكة , ثم عرضهم قبل خلقهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r15.claim: Anbiʾūnī means “inform me”; inbaʾ can mean reporting, from which nabīʾ with hamza is derived, or informing, used figuratively for reporting.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r15.anchor: ومعنى أنبئوني خبروني مأخوذ من الإنباء , وفي الإنباء قولان : أظهرهما : أنه الإخبار

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r16.claim: The author prefers the sense of reporting: nabāʾ means report, and nabīʾ with hamza derives from it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r16.anchor: أظهرهما : أنه الإخبار , والنبأ الخبر , والنبيء بالهمز مشتق من هذا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r17.claim: A second view takes inbaʾ as making known, with its use for reporting being figurative.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r17.anchor: والثاني : أن الإنباء الإعلام , وإنما يستعمل في الإخبار مجازا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r18.claim: “These” refers to the names God taught Adam.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r18.anchor: وقوله : { بأسماء هؤلاء } يعني الأسماء التي علمها آدم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r19.claim: “If you are truthful” may challenge angels who felt they knew more than any creature God creates.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r19.anchor: إن كنتم صادقين أني لا أخلق خلقا إلا كنتم أعلم منه ؛ لأنه هجس في نفوسهم أنهم أعلم من غيرهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r20.claim: Another interpretation refers to their claim that God's earthly deputies would cause corruption.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r20.anchor: إن كنتم صادقين فيما زعمتم أن خلفائي يفسدون في الأرض

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r21.claim: Another interpretation refers to their thought that, if appointed, they would glorify God, whereas another appointed creation would disobey.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r21.anchor: إن كنتم صادقين أني إن استخلفتكم فيها سبحتموني وقدستموني , فإن استخلفت غيركم فيها عصاني

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r22.claim: Another interpretation refers to their feeling that God would create no creature better than them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r22.anchor: إن كنتم صادقين فيما وقع في نفوسكم , أني لا أخلق خلقا إلا كنتم أفضل منه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r23.claim: One interpretation takes ṣādiqīn to mean knowledgeable.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r23.anchor: والخامس : معنى قوله : { إن كنتم صادقين } أي عالمين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r24.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r24.claim: A final interpretation leaves the phrase with its ordinary meaning, “if you are truthful.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r24.anchor: والسادس : أن معناه إن كنتم صادقين

MUJAHID:v1p73#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p73#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p73#2/r1.claim: Adam was taught the names of everything God created; the angels were asked to identify the things shown to Adam.
MUJAHID:v1p73#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال ﴿ وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها ﴾ يعني ما خلق الله كله

MUQATIL:2:31/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:31/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:31/r1.claim: God taught Adam the names of every terrestrial animal and bird, naming creatures such as horses, mules, and donkeys individually.
MUQATIL:2:31/r1.anchor: فعلم آدم، عليه السلام، أسماءها، فقال: يا آدم، هذا فرس، وهذا بغل، وهذا حمار،

MUQATIL:2:31/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:31/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:31/r2.claim: God displayed the named creatures to the angels on earth and challenged them to identify them if truthful about the coming corruption and bloodshed.
MUQATIL:2:31/r2.anchor: ثم عرض أهل تلك الأسماء على الملائكة الذين هم فى الأرض،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r1.claim: Adam is a foreign name, probably on the pattern fāʿil; it may derive from earth's surface or complexion, as names of Jacob, Idris and Iblis have proposed derivations.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r1.anchor: هو اسم أعجمي وأقرب أمره أن يكون على فاعل كآزر واشتقاقهم آدم من أديم الأرض أو من الأدمة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r2.claim: The phrase means the names of the named things: the genitive complement is omitted because it is understood from the word names.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r2.anchor: فحذف المضاف إليه لكونه معلوما مدلولا عليه بذكر الأسماء إذ الاسم يدل على المسمى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r3.claim: The definite article compensates for the omitted complement, as in the Qur'anic phrase about the head flaring gray.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r4.claim: It is incorrect to construe the verse as teaching the objects rather than their names, since the command explicitly asks for their names.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r4.anchor: ولا يصح أن يقدر وعلم آدم مسميات الأسماء على حذف المضاف وإقامة المضاف إليه مقامه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r5.claim: God showed Adam the created kinds and taught him each object's name, such as horse and camel.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r5.anchor: أنه تعالى أراه الأجناس التى خلقها وعلمه أن هذا اسمه فرس وهذا اسمه بعير

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Adam was taught the name of every thing, even a bowl and small items.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما علمه اسم كل شيء حتى القصعة والمعرفة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r7.claim: The masculine plural pronoun refers to the displayed things because rational beings are included among them and take grammatical precedence.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r7.anchor: إنما ذكر لأن فى المسميات العقلاء فغلبهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r8.claim: God questioned the angels to expose and rebuke them, despite already knowing they could not name the things.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r8.anchor: استنبأهم وقد علم عجزهم عن الإنباء على سبيل التبكيت

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r9.claim: The challenge answers the angels' claim that a human successor would spread corruption and bloodshed by showing the knowledge-based benefits of that appointment.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36#2/r9.anchor: فى زعمكم أنى أستخلف فى الأرض مفسدين سفاكين للدماء وفيه رد عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r1.claim: ʿAllama means ‘made known’; Adam received the names by necessary inspiration, though Gabriel as intermediary is possible, and Qurtubi finds the first account stronger.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r1.anchor: «علم» معناه عرف. وتعليمه هنا إلهام علمه ضرورة. ويحتمل أن يكون بواسطة ملك وهو جبريل عليه السلام على ما يأتي. «وعلم» غير مسمى الفاعل. والأول أظهر على ما يأتي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r2.speaker: علماء الصوفية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r2.claim: The Sufis say God taught Adam the names and preserved them for him; he forgot the earlier charge after being left to himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r2.anchor: قال علماء الصوفية: علمها بتعليم الحق إياه وحفظها بحفظه عليه ونسى ما عهد إليه لأن وكله فيه إلى نفسه فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ argues that without disclosure of the names Adam would have been less able than the angels to report them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء: لو لم يكشف لآدم علم تلك الأسماء لكان أعجز من الملائكة في الإخبار عنها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r4.speaker: السهيلي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r4.claim: Al-Suhaylī says Adam was kunya-named Abū Muḥammad after the final Prophet; another report assigns him Abū Muḥammad in Paradise and Abū al-Bashar on earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r4.anchor: وقيل: أبا محمد كني بمحمد خاتم الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم، قاله السهيلي. وقيل: كنيته في الجنة أبو محمد، وفي الأرض أبو البشر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r5.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r5.claim: Adam has two original hamzas, with the second softened; because no yāʾ root is known, al-Akhfash makes the plural follow the dominant wāw pattern, awādim.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r5.anchor: وأصله بهمزتين لأنه أفعل إلا أنهم لينوا الثانية، فإذا احتجت إلى تحريكها جعلتها واوا فقلت: أوادم في الجمع لأنه ليس لها أصل في الياء معروف، فجعلت الغالب عليها الواو عن الأخفش.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās derives Adam from the earth’s surface, the material from which he was made.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r6.anchor: فقيل: هو مشتق من أدمة الأرض وأديمها وهو وجهها، فسمي بما خلق منه قاله ابن عباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r7.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes the complexion derivation to mean dark-brown coloring.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r7.anchor: إنه مشتق من الأدمة وهي السمرة. واختلفوا في الأدمة، فزعم الضحاك أنها السمرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r8.speaker: النضر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r8.claim: Al-Naḍr says Adam was white, deriving the complexion term from a white she-camel; this etymology gives the plural adum and awādim.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r8.anchor: وزعم النضر أنها البياض، وأن آدم عليه السلام كان أبيض مأخوذ من قولهم: ناقة أدماء، إذا كانت بيضاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r9.claim: Qurtubi prefers deriving Adam from the earth’s surface; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says he was named for that origin and insān for forgetting, as cited by Ibn Saʿd.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r9.anchor: قلت: الصحيح أنه مشتق من أديم الأرض. قال سعيد بن جبير: إنما سمي آدم لأنه خلق من أديم الأرض، وإنما سمي إنسانا لأنه نسي ذكره ابن سعد في الطبقات.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r10.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r10.claim: Al-Suddī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd that Earth refuses Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl, then the Angel of Death takes mixed soils; Adam and humanity’s diversity derive from them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31/r10.anchor: وروى السدي عن أبي مالك وعن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس وعن مرة الهمداني عن ابن مسعود في قصة خلق آدم عليه السلام قال: فبعث الله جبريل عليه السلام إلى الأرض ليأتيه بطين منها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r1.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r1.claim: The creation account continues: God formed Adam from foul, sticky clay, left it until it stank, and announced the coming creation and command to prostrate when the spirit entered.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r2.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r2.claim: The report says God formed Adam with His hand so Iblīs would not be too proud to prostrate; the body remained clay for forty years measured from Friday.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r2.anchor: فخلقه الله بيده لكيلا يتكبر إبليس عنه. يقول: أتتكبر عما خلقت بيدي ولم أتكبر أنا عنه! فخلقه بشرا فكان جسدا من طين أربعين سنة من مقدار يوم الجمعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r3.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r3.claim: The angels feared Adam’s clay body; Iblīs struck it and heard a pottery-like sound, called it hollow, and privately planned to destroy or disobey him if favored.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r3.anchor: وكان أشدهم منه فزعا إبليس فكان يمر به فيضربه فيصوت الجسد كما يصوت الفخار تكون له صلصة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r4.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r4.claim: When the spirit reached Adam’s head he sneezed, was taught to praise God, and received God’s mercy; on seeing fruit and craving food, he rushed before life reached his legs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r4.anchor: فلما نفخ فيه الروح فدخل الروح في رأسه عطس فقالت له الملائكة: قل الحمد لله فقال: الحمد لله، فقال الله له: رحمك ربك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r5.claim: The account closes by saying all the angels prostrated except Iblīs, who refused to join them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r5.anchor: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون. إلا إبليس أبى أن يكون مع الساجدين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r6.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet saying Adam was created from a handful gathered from all the earth, so his descendants vary in color, temperament, and goodness; al-Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#2/r6.anchor: إن الله عز وجل خلق آدم من قبضة قبضها من جميع الأرض فجاء بنو آدم على قدر الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r1.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r1.claim: A poet’s line uses al-adam for the earth’s surface, supporting derivation of Adam from al-adīm rather than al-adama; Qurtubi allows both roots as possible.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r2.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says Adam is indeclinable when definite by agreement because it is a proper noun on the afʿal pattern; Basrans require two grounds for non-declension.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r2.anchor: قال أبو جعفر النحاس: «آدم لا ينصرف في المعرفة بإجماع النحويين لأنه على أفعل وهو معرفة، ولا يمتنع شيء من الصرف عند البصريين إلا لعلتين.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r3.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r3.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh do not decline Adam when indefinite and not an adjective; al-Akhfash declines it as an adjective, while al-Zajjāj sides with Sībawayh.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r3.anchor: فإن نكرته ولم يكن نعتا لم يصرفه الخليل وسيبويه، وصرفه الأخفش سعيد لأنه كان نعتا وهو على وزن الفعل، فإذا لم يكن نعتا صرفه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r4.claim: Al-asmāʾ most commonly means the expressions themselves; depending on context, ism can instead denote the named thing or the act of naming.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r4.anchor: الأسماء» هنا بمعنى العبارات، فإن الاسم قد يطلق ويراد به المسمى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r5.claim: Qurtubi says the expressions reading is the most common usage, citing God’s ninety-nine names; other verses use ism for the divine essence or name, and for names people invent.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r5.anchor: وهو الأكثر من استعمالها ومنه قوله تعالى: { وعلم آدم الأسمآء كلها } على أشهر التأويلات

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وقتادة ومجاهد وابن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and Ibn Jubayr say Adam learned the names of every kind of thing, great and small.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r6.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وعكرمة وقتادة ومجاهد وابن جبير: علمه أسماء جميع الأشياء كلها جليلها وحقيرها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r7.claim: In a report from Saʿd, Ibn ʿAbbās cites the verse when asked about a bowl and a whip, showing that ordinary objects were included.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#3/r7.anchor: كنت جالسا عند ابن عباس فذكروا اسم الآنية واسم السوط قال ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet’s account of people seeking intercession on Judgment Day: they approach Adam, citing his creation by God’s hand, angelic prostration, and knowledge of every name.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r1.anchor: فيأتون آدم فيقولون أنت أبو الناس خلقك الله بيده وأسجد لك ملائكته وعلمك أسماء كل شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r2.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r2.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mindād takes the verse as proof that language was divinely instituted and taught to Adam all at once, in detail.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r2.anchor: قال ابن خويز منداد: في هذه الآية دليل على أن اللغة مأخوذة توقيفا، وأن الله تعالى علمها آدم عليه السلام جملة وتفصيلا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Adam learned the names of everything, including a bowl and a milking vessel.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r3.anchor: وكذلك قال ابن عباس: علمه أسماء كل شيء حتى الجفنة والمحلب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r4.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r4.claim: Qatāda says Adam learned names of created beings unknown to the angels, named each thing, and was taught its use; al-Naḥḥās calls this the best report.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r4.anchor: وروى شيبان عن قتادة قال: علم آدم من الأسماء أسماء خلقه ما لم يعلم الملائكة، وسمى كل شيء باسمه وأنحى منفعة كل شيء إلى جنسه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r5.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Adam learned the names of angels and his descendants, preferring that reading because the verse says God presented them to the angels.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r5.anchor: وقال الطبري: علمه أسماء الملائكة وذريته واختار هذا ورجحه بقوله: { ثم عرضهم على الملائكة }.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the names were those of all Adam’s descendants.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: علمه أسماء ذريته كلهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r7.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym restricts the names to angels.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r7.anchor: وقال الربيع بن خثيم: أسماء الملائكة خاصة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r8.speaker: القتبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r8.claim: Al-Qutaybī says Adam learned names of what had been created on earth; another view makes them names of species and kinds.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r8.anchor: وقال القتبي: أسماء ما خلق في الأرض. وقيل: أسماء الأجناس والأنواع.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r9.claim: Qurtubi prefers the broad view that Adam learned the names of all things, based on the word all and the evidence discussed above.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r9.anchor: قلت: القول الأول أصح، لما ذكرناه آنفا ولما نبينه إن شاء الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r10.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and others say God presented the named beings themselves, supported by pronouns them and these and Arabic usage for displaying an object.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r10.anchor: فقال ابن مسعود وغيره: عرض الأشخاص لقوله تعالى: «عرضهم» وقوله: { أنبئوني بأسمآء هؤلاء }.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say God presented the names rather than their referents; Ibn Masʿūd’s reading uses feminine plural, while Ubayy’s uses feminine singular.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: عرض الأسماء. وفي حرف ابن مسعود: «عرضهن» فأعاد على الأسماء دون الأشخاص

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r12.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r12.claim: Mujāhid interprets the displayed objects as the bearers of the names.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r12.anchor: مجاهد: أصحاب الأسماء. فمن قال في الأسماء إنها التسميات فاستقام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r13.claim: Qurtubi explains that the reading عرضهم can call names by their referents, while هؤلاء points to named beings present through their related names.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r13.anchor: وتقول في قراءة من قرأ «عرضهم»: إن لفظ الأسماء يدل على أشخاص فلذلك ساغ أن يقال للأسماء: «عرضهم». وقال في «هؤلاء» المراد بالإشارة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r14.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Adam learned names, saw the named beings, then named them for the angels after God showed the beings to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r14.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والذي يظهر أن الله تعالى علم آدم الأسماء وعرضهن عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r15.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r15.claim: Al-Māwardī says the display was most properly directed to the named beings; they may have been shown after creation or represented to the angels’ minds.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r15.anchor: وقال الماوردي: وكان الأصح توجه العرض إلى المسمين. ثم في زمن عرضهم قولان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r16.speaker: كعب الأحبار
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r16.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār and others say Adam first devised Arabic, Syriac, all writing, and spoke all languages.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r16.anchor: فروي عن كعب الأحبار: أن أول من وضع الكتاب العربي والسرياني والكتب كلها وتكلم بالألسنة كلها آدم عليه السلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r17.speaker: كعب الأحبار
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r17.claim: Another report from Kaʿb says Gabriel first spoke Arabic, taught it to Noah, and Noah passed it to his son Shem.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#4/r17.anchor: قد روي عن كعب الأحبار من وجه حسن قال: أول من تكلم بالعربية جبريل عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r1.claim: A Prophetic report says Ishmael was the first to speak clear Arabic, at age ten.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r1.anchor: أول من فتق لسانه بالعربية المبينة إسماعيل وهو ابن عشر سنين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r2.claim: Another report names Yaʿrub ibn Qaḥṭān as the first Arabic speaker.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r2.anchor: وقد روي أيضا: أن أول من تكلم بالعربية يعرب بن قحطان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r3.claim: Qurtubi prefers Adam as the first human speaker of all languages: all languages are names covered by this verse, and a Prophetic report says he learned even the platter and its small serving dish.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r3.anchor: قلنا: الصحيح أن أول من تكلم باللغات كلها من البشر آدم عليه السلام، والقرآن يشهد له

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r4.claim: Qurtubi reconciles reports naming later figures as first Arabic speakers by taking them as first among Abraham’s descendants or their own tribe; Gabriel first spoke Arabic among angels and passed it to Noah.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r4.anchor: وما ذكروه يحتمل أن يكون المراد به أول من تكلم بالعربية من ولد إبراهيم عليه إسماعيل عليه السلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r5.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r5.claim: Hāʾulāʾ is normally built on kasra; Tamīm and some Qays and Asad speakers shorten it, as in al-Aʿshā’s example, while another dialect deletes alif and hamza.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r5.anchor: ولغة تميم وبعض قيس وأسد فيه القصر قال الأعشى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r6.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad supplies the omitted apodosis: if the angels were right that Adam’s descendants would corrupt the earth, they should name the displayed beings.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r6.anchor: إن كنتم صادقين أن بني آدم يفسدون في الأرض فأنبئوني قاله المبرد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r7.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r7.claim: Al-Naqqāsh says ṣādiqīn means knowledgeable here, so the angels were not invited to reason by ijtihād; with mere accuracy in reporting, such reasoning would have been allowed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r7.anchor: ومعنى «صادقين» عالمين ولذلك لم يسغ للملائكة الاجتهاد وقالوا: «سبحانك» حكاه النقاش

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r8.speaker: الطبري وأبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and Abū ʿUbayd report a view that إن كنتم means إذ كنتم, but reject it as erroneous.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r8.anchor: وحكى الطبري وأبو عبيد: أن بعض المفسرين قال إن معنى «إن كنتم»: إذ كنتم، وقالا: هذا خطأ.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r9.claim: Anbiʾūnī means tell me, from nabaʾ meaning news; Qurtubi says he will explain the hamzated form nabīʾ later.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r9.anchor: و «أنبئوني» معناه أخبروني. والنبأ: الخبر ومنه النبيء بالهمز

QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r10.claim: Some infer that God commanded an impossible task because He knew the angels lacked the knowledge; the investigators say this was a declaration and demonstration, not a charge of obligation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:31#5/r10.anchor: قال بعض العلماء: يخرج من هذا الأمر بالإنباء تكليف ما لا يطاق لأنه علم أنهم لا يعلمون. وقال المحققون من أهل التأويل

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r1.claim: The clause may be syntactically independent or genitive by coordination with قال ربك.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r1.anchor: هذه الجملة يجوز إلا يكون لها محل من الإعراب لاستئنافها، وأن يكون محلها الجر لعطفها على " قال ربك

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r2.speaker: أبو علي الشلوبين
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r2.claim: عَلِم in its cognition sense takes one object before doubling and two after doubling; certainty sense instead takes extra objects with hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r2.anchor: ذكر ذلك أبو علي علي الشلوبين

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r3.claim: God is the subject of علّم, آدم its first object, and الأسماء its second, in the pattern of أعطى and كسا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r3.anchor: وفاعل " علم " يعود على الباري تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r4.claim: Adam is most plausibly a non-derived foreign proper name on the pattern فاعل, indeclinable for being a personal proper name and foreign.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r4.anchor: اسم أعجمي غير مشتق، ووزنه فاعل كنظائره نحو: آزر وشالح

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r5.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r5.claim: One proposed derivation takes Adam from أدمة, the reddish color that tends toward black.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r5.anchor: لا حذف. وقيل: لا بد من حذف واختلفوا

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r6.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r6.claim: Another proposed derivation takes Adam from أديم الأرض; the text calls this account stronger and links its declension rule to pattern and proper-name status.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r6.anchor: لا حذف. وقيل: لا بد من حذف واختلفوا

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r7.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r7.claim: A fourth account also derives Adam from أديم الأرض on فاعل; the author rejects this form because it should then be declinable.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r7.anchor: لا حذف. وقيل: لا بد من حذف واختلفوا

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r8.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r8.claim: A fifth account says Adam is Hebrew, from الإدام meaning soil.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r8.anchor: لا حذف. وقيل: لا بد من حذف واختلفوا

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r9.speaker: الطبري
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r9.claim: Al-Tabari says Adam was originally a four-letter verb like أكرم and was named to make a thing's direction recognizable.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r9.anchor: قال الطبري: " إنه في الأصل فعل رباعي مثل: أكرم، وسمي به لغرض إظهار الشيء

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r10.claim: Claims that Adam is derived are unlikely, since foreign names do not take derivation or inflection; formally passive آدم is semantically the agent.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r10.anchor: والحاصل أن ادعاء الاشتقاق فيه بعيد، لأن الأسماء الأعجمية لا يدخلها اشتقاق ولا تصريف، وآدم وإن كان مفعولا لفظا فهو

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r11.speaker: قرئ
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r11.claim: A passive reading of علّم makes آدم nominative as نائب الفاعل.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r11.anchor:
الله تعالى.
وقرئ: " علم " مبنيا للمفعول، و " آدم

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r12.claim: كلها is an emphatic qualifier of الأسماء and always follows it, though it may follow governing elements.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r12.anchor: تأكيد للأسماء تابع أبدا، وقد يلي العوامل

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r13.claim: No ellipsis is needed if all names were taught without specifying them: كلية signals comprehensiveness, and the lesson's purpose can be achieved without teaching referents; alternatively, names may mean referents.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r13.anchor: الظاهر أنه لا يحتاج إلى ادعاء حذف، لأن المعنى: وعلم آدم الأسماء، [ولم يبين لنا أسماء مخصوصة، بل دل كلها

SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says ال compensates for the omitted genitive in the proposed أسماء المسميات construction.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31/r14.anchor: فقيل: تقديره: أسماء المسميات، فحذف المضاف إليه للعلم. قال الزمخشري: " وعوض منه اللام

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r1.claim: The Zamakhshari deletion account takes the definite article to replace a genitive complement, as in Mary 19:4, and cites the contrast between naming the names and naming the referents in 2:31–33.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r1.anchor: في قوله: وعوض منه اللام " نظر، لأن الألف

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r2.claim: The author says the Basran school does not allow ال to stand in place of iḍāfa.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r2.anchor: لأن الألف واللام لا يقومان مقام الإضافة عند البصريين

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r3.claim: Another required ellipsis is مسميات الأسماء, with the first construct noun omitted and the genitive promoted; ثم عرضهم supports it because أسماء is not normally pluralized with a rational masculine pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: تقديره مسميات الأسماء، فحذف المضاف، وأقيم المضاف إليه مقامه، ورجح هذا القول بقوله تعالى: { ثم عرضهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r4.claim: In 24:40, أو كذي ظلمات is understood with ذي omitted; the pronoun of يغشاه refers back to that omitted word.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r4.anchor: تقديره: أو كذي ظلمات، فالهاء في " يغشاه " تعود على " ذي " المحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r5.claim: ثم expresses temporal delay; the pronoun in عرضهم refers to the supplied referents or names used for referents.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r5.anchor: ثم " حرف للتراخي كما تقدم، والضمير في " عرضهم " للمسميات المقدرة أو لإطلاق الأسماء وإرادة المسميات

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited for taking عرضهم to refer to the names themselves.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: يعود على الأسماء ونقل عن ابن عباس

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r7.claim: Readings عرضها and عرضهن support a names antecedent, but this treats non-rational plurals as rational; Ibn Abbas may instead have meant names standing for referents.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r7.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة من قرأ: " عرضها وعرضهن " إلا أن في هذا القول جعل ضمير غير العقلاء كضمير العقلاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r8.claim: على الملائكة is attached to عرضهم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#2/r8.anchor: واضح. و " على الملائكة " متعلق ب " عرضهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r1.claim: إنباء means informing and ordinarily governs two objects, the second with a preposition; the preposition may be omitted, as in 66:3.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r1.anchor: الإنباء: الإخبار، وأصل " أنبأ " أن يتعدى لاثنين ثانيهما بحرف الجر كهذه الآية

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r2.claim: أنبأ may also carry the certainty sense of أعلم and then govern three objects; نبأ, أخبر, خبر, and حدث have parallel usage.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r2.anchor: وقد يتضمن معنى " أعلم " اليقينية، فيتعدى تعديتها إلى ثلاثة مفاعيل، ومثل أنبأ: نبأ وأخبر

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r3.claim: هؤلاء is genitive in the construct and a demonstrative of low deixis, with long and short forms; the quoted poetry witnesses هؤلا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r3.anchor: في محل خفض بالإضافة, وهو اسم إشارة ورتبته دنيا، ويمد ويقصر

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r4.claim: هؤلاء is normally built on kasra but may take ḍamma or nunation; its hamza may become hāʾ or the form may be هولا, as in the cited poem.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r4.anchor: والمشهور بناؤه على الكسر، وقد يضم وقد ينون مكسورا، وقد تبدل همزته هاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r5.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r5.claim: Al-Farisi treats the demonstrative's last radical as hamza, so the first and last radicals share one root.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r5.anchor: ولامه عند الفارسي همزة فتكون فاؤه ولامه من مادة واحدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
