SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r6.speaker: المبرد
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the last radical was yāʾ, changed to hamza because it became final after the extra alif.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#3/r6.anchor: وعند المبرد أصلها ياء وإنما قلبت همزة لتطرفها بعد الألف الزائدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#4/r1.claim: The condition's جواب is elided and understood as فأنبئوني.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#4/r1.anchor: وجوابه محذوف أي: إن كنتم صادقين فأنبئوني

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#4/r2.speaker: الكوفيون والمبرد
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#4/r2.claim: The Kufans and al-Mubarrad say the preceding command is the conditional جواب; the author rejects this because a preceding جواب would need فاء, as in أنت ظالم إن فعلت.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#4/r2.anchor: والكوفيون والمبرد يرون أن الجواب هو المتقدم، وهو مردود بقولهم: " أنت ظالم إن فعلت

SAMIN-DURR:2:31#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#4/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#4/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya assigns the omitted جواب to al-Mubarrad and the fronted جواب to Sibawayh; the author says that attribution is mistaken.
SAMIN-DURR:2:31#4/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " إن كون الجواب محذوفا وهو رأي المبرد وكونه متقدما هو رأي سيبويه " وهو وهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r1.claim: Rāzī treats the challenge to name the things as evidence that the angels' preceding claim was false, while presenting the inference as a question.
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r1.anchor: أن قوله : { أنبئونى بأسماء هؤلاء إن كنتم صادقين } ( البقرة : 31 ) يدل على

RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r2.claim: He takes 2:33 to show that the angels had not known this before the episode and had doubted God's knowledge of all things.
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r2.anchor: ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم غيب السماوات والارض وأعلم ما تبدون وما كنتم تكتمون

RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r3.claim: Revelation of the corruption forecast is unlikely because repeating an inspired fact would be pointless; he infers conjecture, forbidden by 17:36 and 10:36.
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r3.anchor: فثبت أنهم قالوه عن الاستنباط والظن والقدح في الغير على سبيل الظن غير جائز

RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that God addressed the angels who had been Iblīs's troops in the war against the jinn; their question about a corrupting successor drew God's anger, and they repented by admitting their ignorance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r4.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : إن الله سبحانه وتعالى قال للملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r5.speaker: الجن وقتادة
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r5.claim: A report attributed to the jinn and Qatāda says the angels privately expected every new creature to be inferior to them; Adam's knowledge exposed that boast, so they repented and confessed ignorance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r5.anchor: وروي عن الجن وقتادة أن الله تعالى لما أخذ في خلق آدم همست الملائكة فيما بينهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r6.claim: Some narrations add that God sent fire to burn the angels after they asked whether He would place a corruptor on earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r6.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات أنهم لما قالوا أتجعل فيها ، أرسل الله عليهم نارا فأحرقتهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r7.speaker: من تمسكوا بقصة هاروت وماروت
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r7.claim: The account says Hārūt and Mārūt condemned human sins and prayed against people; God warned that human desires would make them disobey, but they claimed they would resist and were sent down for a test.
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r7.anchor: تمسكوا بقصة هاروت وماروت وزعموا أنهما كانا ملكين من الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r8.speaker: من تمسكوا بقصة هاروت وماروت
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r8.claim: In the story, Venus and her accompanying angel take human forms; the angels visit Venus, refuse sex unless they drink wine, then succumb to desire, and she imposes another condition.
RAZI-FULL:v2p153/r8.anchor: فأوحى الله تعالى إليهما إني لو ابتليتكما بما ابتليت به بني آدم من الشهوات لعصيتماني

RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r1.claim: After giving the angels a general answer about the wisdom of creating Adam, God clarified it by displaying Adam's knowledge, exposing their limits and reinforcing the general answer with a specific one.
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r1.anchor: أراد تعالى أن يزيدهم بيانا وأن يفصل لهم ذلك المجمل

RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r2.speaker: الأشعري والجبائي والكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r2.claim: Al-Ashʿarī, al-Jubbāʾī, and al-Kaʿbī hold that all languages are divinely instituted: God creates necessary knowledge of expressions, meanings, and their assignment.
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r2.anchor: قال الأشعري والجبائي والكعبي : اللغات كلها توقيفية . بمعنى أن الله تعالى خلق علما ضروريا

RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r3.speaker: الأشعري والجبائي والكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r3.claim: They argue that the construction of teaching Adam the names implies those names already existed before the teaching, so language preceded it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r3.anchor: وذلك يقتضي في تلك الأسماء أنها كانت أسماء قبل ذلك التعليم ، وإذا كان كذلك كانت اللغات حاصلة

RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r4.speaker: الأشعري والجبائي والكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r4.claim: They argue that the angels had to recognize Adam's naming as correct for his challenge to prove his truth, implying that name-to-thing assignments predated his instruction.
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r4.anchor: وذلك يقتضي أن يكون وضع تلك الأسماء لتلك المسميات متقدما على ذلك التعليم

RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r5.claim: Rāzī answers that God could create necessary knowledge that some assigner had assigned these names to these things without revealing whether the assigner was God or people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r5.anchor: بخلق العلم الضروري بأن واضعا وضع هذه الأسماء لهذه المسميات من غير تعيين

RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r6.claim: He answers another objection by allowing that God addressed the angels through another medium, such as writing.
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r6.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يقال خاطب الملائكة بطريق آخر بالكتابة وغيرها

RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r7.claim: He answers a third objection by saying God's prior will to assign words to meanings suffices for teaching to be attributed to the names.
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r7.anchor: إرادة الله تعالى وضع تلك الألفاظ لتلك المعاني سابقة على التعليم

RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r8.claim: Rāzī postpones his answer to the fourth argument for later discussion.
RAZI-FULL:v2p161/r8.anchor: وعن الرابع : ماسيأتي بيانه إن شاء الله تعالى والله تعالى أعلم .

RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r1.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r1.claim: Some interpret the names as the qualities, attributes, and properties of things, reasoning from the derivation of ism from sima, a mark that identifies an essence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r1.anchor: أي علمه صفات الأشياء ونعوتها وخواصها والدليل عليه أن الاسم اشتقاقه إما من السمة أو من السمو

RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r2.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r2.claim: They also derive ism from sumu, elevation: a thing's evidence stands above it, and knowledge of evidence comes before knowledge of what it proves.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r2.anchor: وإن كان من السمو فكذلك لأن دليل الشيء كالمرتفع على ذلك الشيء

RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r3.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r3.claim: They argue that grammarians' restriction of ism to particular word forms is a later convention and cannot rule out the broader meaning of qualities.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r3.anchor: ولكن ذلك عرف حادث لا اعتبار به

RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r4.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r4.claim: They prefer realities over labels because knowledge of things' realities is more meritorious, fitting a passage meant to display Adam's superiority.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r4.anchor: أن الفضيلة في معرفة حقائق الأشياء أكثر من الفضيلة في معرفة أسمائها

RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r5.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r5.claim: They argue that a challenge should test a capacity the audience can in principle share: language is learned only through instruction, whereas reason can attain knowledge of realities.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r5.anchor: وذلك لأن العقل لا طريق له إلى معرفة اللغات البتة : بل ذلك لا يحصل إلا بالتعليم

RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r6.speaker: الجمهور
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r6.claim: The majority understand the names as names for all created kinds, in all the different languages spoken by Adam's descendants, including Arabic, Persian, and Greek.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r6.anchor: القول الثاني : وهو الشمهور أن المراد أسماء كل ما خلق الله من أجناس المحدثات

RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r7.claim: In this account Adam's children spoke all these languages; after his death they spread out, each language prevailed in different groups, and generations forgot the others, explaining linguistic diversity.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r7.anchor: فلما مات آدم وتفرق ولده في نواحي العالم تكلم كل واحد منهم بلغة معينة

RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r8.speaker: أهل المعاني
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r8.claim: The grammarians of meaning posit an ellipsis: God taught Adam either names of the referents or the referents of the names; they prefer the former because 2:33 says to tell their names.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r8.anchor: قال أهل المعاني : قوله تعالى : { وعلم ءادم الاسماء } لا بد فيه من إضمار

RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r9.claim: Although the displayed set included non-rational things, the masculine plural pronoun is used because rational angels, humans, and jinn occur among them and the more complete category governs Arabic agreement.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162/r9.anchor: كان في جملتها الملائكة والإنس والجن وهم العقلاء ، فغلب الأكمل

RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r1.claim: The claim that God's request of the angels proves the permissibility of assigning an impossible task is weak: the request rebuked them while God knew they could not answer, as the challenge clause shows.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r1.anchor: لأنه تعالى إنما استنبأهم مع علمه تعالى بعجزهم على سبيل التبكيت

RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r2.claim: The Muʿtazilites say Adam's knowledge of the names was a miracle that proved his prophethood at that moment; Rāzī considers commissioning him to Eve most likely and does not rule out the angels as addressees.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r2.anchor: المسألة الرابعة : قالت المعتزلة : إن ما ظهر من آدم عليه السلام من علمه بالأسماء معجزة دالة على نبوته

RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r3.claim: Their proof is that the knowledge violated ordinary patterns, making it a miracle and therefore evidence that Adam was a messenger then.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r3.anchor: بأن حصول ذلك العلم له ناقض للعادة فوجب أن يكون معجزا

RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r4.claim: Rāzī objects that knowledge of a language is ordinary when God teaches it and its absence is ordinary when He does not, so Adam's knowledge need not violate custom.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r4.anchor: لأن حصول العلم باللغة لمن علمه الله تعالى وعدم حصوله لمن لم يعلمه الله ليس بناقض للعادة

RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r5.claim: Rāzī poses a dilemma: if the angels knew the name-to-thing mappings, they could name the objects too and Adam's distinction would disappear; if not, how could they verify his correctness?
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r5.anchor: فإن علموا ذلك فقد قدروا على أن يذكروا أسماء تلك المسميات

RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r6.claim: One proposed solution is that different angelic classes knew different languages; Adam recited them all, so each class verified its own language while all angels together could not produce the complete set, making it miraculous.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r6.anchor: ربما كان لكل صنف من أصناف الملائكة لغة من هذه اللغات

RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r7.claim: A second solution is that God gave the angels evidence of Adam's truth before they heard the names, so they recognized his correctness and the miracle when he spoke.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r7.anchor: إنه تعالى عرفهم قبل أن سمعوا من آدم عليه السلام تلك الأسماء ما استدلوا به على صدق آدم

RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r8.claim: Even if Adam performed an extraordinary act, Rāzī says it could have been a saintly wonder or a prophetic precursor, both allowed in his theological school, so the issue depends on those doctrines.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r8.anchor: فلم لا يجوز أن يكون ذلك من باب الكرامات أو من باب الإرهاص وهما عندنا جائزان

RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r9.speaker: من قطع بأنه عليه السلام ما كان نبيا في ذلك الوقت
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r9.claim: Those denying prophethood then argue that if Adam were already a prophet, his later agreed-upon lapse would be a major sin after prophethood, deserving disgrace and incompatible with prophets; therefore it preceded prophethood.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r9.anchor: واحتج من قطع بأنه عليه السلام ما كان نبيا في ذلك الوقت بوجوه : أحدها : أنه لو كان نبيا

RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r10.speaker: من قطع بأنه عليه السلام ما كان نبيا في ذلك الوقت
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r10.claim: They argue that a messenger must have an addressee, but none fits: under the Muʿtazilite ranking angels outrank humans, Eve alone existed and was addressed directly, no jinn were in heaven, and a messenger without a recipient serves no purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r10.anchor: لو كان رسولا في ذلك الوقت لكان إما أن يكون مبعوثا إلى أحد أو لا يكون

RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r11.claim: Rāzī says the argument that Adam had no possible recipient is not especially strong.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r11.anchor: وهذا الوجه ليس في غاية القوة

RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r12.speaker: من قطع بأنه عليه السلام ما كان نبيا في ذلك الوقت
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r12.claim: They infer from 2:37 that God chose Adam only after his lapse; since selection and messengership go together, he was not a messenger beforehand, citing 6:124.
RAZI-FULL:v2p162#2/r12.anchor: وثالثها : قوله تعالى : { ثم اجتباه ربه } فهذه الآية دل على أنه تعالى إنما اجتباه بعد الزلة

RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r1.claim: One reading asks the angels to name the objects if they know they can report truthfully.
RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r1.anchor: معناه أعلموني أسماء هؤلاء إن علمتم أنكم تكونون صادقين في ذلك الأعلام

RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r2.claim: Another reading commands them to report nothing but truth; it emphasizes their incapacity by making them recognize that they cannot truthfully answer or access the names.
RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r2.anchor: معناه أخبروني ولا تقولوا إلا حقا وصدقا

RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd take the condition to mean: if you are truthful that no creature is burdened with worship except one that you can perform.
RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r3.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود

RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r4.claim: A further reading challenges the angels to name the objects if their claim is true that God creates no creature more knowledgeable than them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p164/r4.anchor: إن كنتم صادقين في قولكم إني لم أخلق خلقا إلا كنتم أعلم منه

RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r1.claim: The verse proves knowledge's excellence: God displayed the wisdom of Adam's creation by displaying his knowledge, which would be the highest excellence if anything better existed He would have displayed that instead.
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r1.anchor: ما أظهر كمال حكمته في خلقه آدم عليه السلام إلا بأن أظهر علمه

RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r2.claim: Muqātil identifies four Qurʾānic meanings of wisdom: Qurʾānic admonitions, understanding and knowledge, prophethood, and the Qurʾān itself; Rāzī says all reduce to knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r2.anchor: ما يروى عن مقاتل : أنه قال : تفسر الحكمة في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r3.claim: The Qurʾān calls human knowledge little and worldly enjoyment little; since the world's finite extent, number, and duration contrast with knowledge and its rewards, the unnamed measure of knowledge must be vast.
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r3.anchor: وسمى الدنيا بأسرها قليلا { قل متاع الدنيا قليل } ( النساء : 77 ) فما سماه قليلا لا يمكننا أن ندرك كميته

RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r4.claim: The second proof is 39:9: scripture's contrasts between impure and pure, blind and seeing, darkness and light, Paradise and Fire, and shade and heat ultimately reflect the difference between learned and ignorant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r4.anchor: وإذا تأملت وجدت كل ذلك مأخوذا من الفرق بين العالم والجاهل

RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r5.claim: The third proof is 4:59: the strongest interpretation of those in authority identifies them as scholars, since rulers must obey scholars, not conversely.
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r5.anchor: والمراد من أولى الأمر العلماء في أصح الأقوال لأن الملوك يجب عليهم طاعة العلماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r6.claim: Scripture places scholars second beside God and the angels in 3:18 and beside God and the Messenger in 4:59, then gives them first place among humans in 3:7 and 13:43.
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r6.anchor: ثم انظر إلى هذه المرتبة فإنه تعالى ذكر العالم في موضعين من كتابه في المرتبة الثانية

RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r7.claim: The fourth proof is 58:11, which says God raises believers and those given knowledge in rank; this section begins the four groups by citing the ranks of the believers at Badr.
RAZI-FULL:v2p164#2/r7.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى ذكر الدرجات لأربعة أصناف . وألها : للمؤمنين من أهل بدر

RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r1.claim: Rāzī ranks four groups named in scripture: Badr believers, fighters, the righteous, and scholars; because scholars receive ranks above the other groups, he concludes they are the best people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r1.anchor: ثم فضل العلماء على جميع الأصناف بدرجات ، فوجب أن يكون العلماء أفضل الناس .

RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r2.claim: The fifth proof is that only scholars truly fear God; Rāzī lists their five scriptural traits as faith, monotheistic witness, weeping, humility, and reverent fear.
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r2.anchor: فإن الله تعالى وصف العلماء في كتابه بخمس مناقب ، أحدها : الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r3.speaker: ثابت عن أنس
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r3.claim: Anas reports from the Prophet that learners are among those freed from Hell: each step to a scholar earns worship and a city in Paradise, the earth seeks forgiveness for the learner, and angels attest their freedom.
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r3.anchor: أحدها : روى ثابت عن أنس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( من أحب أن ينظر إلى عتقاء الله من النار

RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r4.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r4.claim: Anas reports that a person seeking knowledge for other than God will ultimately be brought to God by it; knowledge sought for God is like day-long fasting and night-long prayer, and one learned chapter outweighs a mountain of gold spent in God's way.
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r4.anchor: وثانيها : عن أنس قال : قال عليه السلام : ( من طلب العلم لغير الله لم يخرج من الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r5.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports from the Prophet that one who dies seeking knowledge to revive Islam will stand one degree below the prophets in Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r5.anchor: وثالثها : عن الحسن مرفوعا ) من جاءه الموت وهو يطلب العلم ليحيى به الإسلام

RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r6.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r6.claim: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī reports that on Judgment Day God singles out scholars, saying He placed His light and knowledge among them because He knew them and not to punish them, and then forgives them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p165/r6.anchor: ورابعها : أبو موسى الأشعري مرفوعا ( يبعث الله العباد يوم القيامة ثم يميز العلماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r1.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that when a teacher of good dies, the birds of the sky, animals of the land, and fish of the sea mourn him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r1.anchor: وخامسها : قال عليه السلام : ( معلم الخير إذا مات بكى عليه طير السماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet that praying behind a scholar is like praying behind a prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r2.anchor: وسادسها : أبو هريرة مرفوعا ( من صلى خلف عالم من العلماء فكأنما صلى خلف نبي من الأنبياء )

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that a scholar outranks a worshipper by seventy degrees, each a seventy-year ride apart, because a scholar recognizes and removes innovations that a worshipper misses.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r3.anchor: وسابعها : ابن عمر مرفوعا ( فضل العالم على العابد بسبعين درجة

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r4.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports the Prophet's prayer for mercy upon his successors, identified as those who revive his Sunna and teach it to God's servants.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r4.anchor: وثامنها : الحسن مرفوعا قال عليه السلام : ( رحمة الله على خلفائي

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r5.claim: A prophetic report equates seeking knowledge to correct falsehood or guide people from misguidance with forty years of worship.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r5.anchor: من خرج يطلب بابا من العلم ليرد به باطلا إلى حق أو ضلالا إلى هدى

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r6.claim: When the Prophet sent ʿAlī to Yemen, he said that guiding one person is better than everything on which the sun rises or sets.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r6.anchor: وعاشرها : قال عليه السلام لعلي حين بعثه إلى اليمن ( لأن يهدي الله بك رجلا واحدا

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that one who seeks knowledge to teach people for God's sake receives the reward of seventy prophets.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r7.anchor: الحادي عشر : ابن مسعود مرفوعا ( من طلب العلم ليحدث به الناس ابتغاء وجه الله

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r8.speaker: عامر الجهني
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r8.claim: ʿĀmir al-Juhanī reports that the ink of a knowledge-seeker and a martyr's blood are weighed equally at Judgment Day; another version says scholars' ink outweighs the blood.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r8.anchor: الثاني عشر : عامر الجهني مرفوعا ( يؤتى بمداد طالب العلم ودم الشهيد يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r9.speaker: أبو وافد الليثي
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r9.claim: Abū Wāqid al-Laythī reports a Muslim narration about three men at the Prophet's gathering: God shelters the one who joins, is gracious to the shy one who stays behind, and turns away from the one who leaves.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r9.anchor: الثالث عشر : أبو وافد الليثي : أنه عليه السلام بينما هو جالس والناس معه إذ أقبل ثلاثة نفر

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r10.claim: An unnamed saying compares scholars' care for pupils with parental care: parents protect against worldly fire and harms, while scholars protect against Hell and the terrors of the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r10.anchor: العالم أرأف بالتلميذ من الأب والأم لأن الآباء والأمهات يحفظونه من نار الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r11.claim: Asked how he gained knowledge, Ibn Masʿūd says it came through a questioning tongue and an understanding heart.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r11.anchor: بم وجدت هذا العلم : قال بلسان سؤول ، وقلب عقول

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r12.claim: An unnamed maxim advises asking questions with a fool's boldness and retaining knowledge with the wise person's care.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r12.anchor: قال بعضهم سل مسألة الحمقى ، واحفظ حفظ الأكياس

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r13.speaker: مصعب بن الزبير
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r13.claim: Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr tells his son to learn: with wealth, knowledge adorns him; without wealth, knowledge itself becomes his wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r13.anchor: مصعب بن الزبير قال لابنه : يا بني تعلم العلم فإن كان لك مال كان العلم لك جمالا

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r14.claim: ʿAlī says there is no good in withholding knowledge, just as there is no good in speaking from ignorance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r14.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب : لا خير في الصمت عن العلم كما لا خير في الكلام عن الجهل

RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r15.speaker: بعض المحققين
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r15.claim: Some discerning scholars divide scholars into three: one knows God but not His commands, one knows His commands but not God, and one knows both God and His commands.
RAZI-FULL:v2p166/r15.anchor: قال بعض المحققين : العلماء ثلاثة عالم بالله غير عالم بأمر الله

RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r1.claim: The first scholar is so absorbed in witnessing divine majesty that he learns legal rulings only as necessary.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r1.anchor: فهو عبد قد استولت المعرفة الإلهية على قلبه فصار مستغرقا بمشاهدة نور الجلال

RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r2.claim: A second type knows God's commands and legal rulings but not the secrets of divine majesty.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r2.anchor: هو الذي يكون عالما بأمر الله وغير عالم بالله وهو الذي عرف الحلال والحرام

RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r3.claim: The complete scholar knows God and His law, moving between divine love and compassionate service to people; this is the way of messengers and the truthful.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r3.anchor: فهذا سبيل المرسلين والصديقين وهذا هو المراد بقوله عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r4.claim: Razi reads the saying to ask scholars, mix with sages, and sit with elders as three instructions matching scholars of law, knowers of God, and those who know both.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r4.anchor: سائل العلماء وخالط الحكماء وجالس الكبراء

RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r5.speaker: شقيق البلخي
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r5.claim: The scholar who knows God's commands remembers with the tongue, fears people rather than God, and is publicly modest but privately unashamed before God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r5.anchor: قال شقيق البلخي : لكل واحد من هؤلاء الثلاثة ثلاث علامات

RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r6.speaker: شقيق البلخي
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r6.claim: The knower of God remembers, fears, and feels shame inwardly: remembrance of the heart, fear of ostentation, and shame at inner thoughts.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r6.anchor: وأما العالم بالله فإنه يكون ذاكرا خائفا مستحييا . أما الذكر فذكر القلب

RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r7.speaker: شقيق البلخي
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r7.claim: The scholar who knows God and His law also bridges unseen and witnessed realms, teaches the first two classes, and is needed by them while needing neither.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r7.anchor: وأما العالم بالله وبأمر الله فله ستة أشياء الثلاثة التي ذكرناها

RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r8.speaker: شقيق البلخي
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r8.claim: The scholar who knows both God and His commands resembles the sun, steady without increase or decrease.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r8.anchor: مثل العالم بالله وبأمر الله كمثل الشمس لا يزيد ولا ينقص

RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r9.speaker: شقيق البلخي
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r9.claim: The scholar who knows God alone resembles the moon, sometimes full and sometimes waning.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r9.anchor: ومثل العالم بالله فقد كمثل القمر يكمل تارة وينقص تارة أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r10.speaker: شقيق البلخي
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r10.claim: The scholar who knows God's commands alone resembles a lamp that burns itself to illuminate others.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r10.anchor: ومثل العالم بأمر الله فقد كمثل السراج يحرق نفسه ويضيء لغيره

RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r11.speaker: فتح الموصلي
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r11.claim: Fath al-Mawsili asks whether a sick person deprived of food, drink, and medicine would die, introducing an analogy for the heart.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167/r11.anchor: قال فتح الموصلي : أليس المريض إذا امتنع عنه الطعام والشراب والدواء يموت ؟

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r1.claim: The heart likewise dies when deprived of knowledge, reflection, and wisdom, completing Fath al-Mawsili's analogy.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r1.anchor: فكذا القلب إذا امتنع عنه العلم والفكر والحكمة يموت

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r2.speaker: شقيق البليح
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r2.claim: Shafiq says hearers of his Quran lessons become pure disbelievers if they disbelieve him, hypocrites if constricted by his words, and pure believers if repentant and resolved against sin.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r2.anchor: قال شقيق البليح : الناس يقومون من مجلسي على ثلاثة أصناف : كافر محض ، ومنافق محض ، ومؤمن محض

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r3.speaker: شقيق البليح
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r3.claim: Shafiq lists sleeping after dawn or before night prayer, during prayer, or at a remembrance gathering, and laughing behind a funeral, in cemeteries, or at remembrance gatherings, as disliked by God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r3.anchor: وقال أيضا : ثلاثة من النوم يبغضها الله تعالى . وثلاثة من الضحك : النوم بعد صلاة الفجر

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r4.claim: An unnamed commentator compares knowledge to rainwater in the flood image of 13:17 and gives five correspondences.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم في قوله تعالى : { فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا } ( الرعد : 17 ) السيل ههنا العلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r5.claim: As rain descends from heaven, knowledge descends from heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r5.anchor: كما أن المطر ينزل من السماء كذلك العلم ينزل من السماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r6.claim: Rain repairs the earth, just as knowledge reforms people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r6.anchor: كما أن إصلاح الأرض بالمطر فإصلاح الخلق بالعلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r7.claim: Crops cannot grow without rain, just as deeds and worship cannot arise without knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r7.anchor: كما أن الزرع والنبات لا يخرج بغير المطر كذلك الأعمال والطاعات لا تخرج بغير العلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r8.claim: Rain follows thunder and lightning, while knowledge follows promise and warning.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r8.anchor: كما أن المطر فرع الرعد والبرق كذلك العلم فإنه فرغ الوعد والوعيد .

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r9.claim: Knowledge, like rain, can benefit or harm: it benefits those who act on it and harms those who do not.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r9.anchor: الخامس : كما أن المطر نافع وضار ، كذلك العلم نافع وضار : نافع لمن عمل به ضار لمن لم يعمل به

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r10.claim: Many people preach remembrance yet forget God, warn others yet defy Him, call others to God yet flee Him, or recite scripture while abandoning its verses.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r10.anchor: كم من مذكر بالله ناس لله ، وكم من مخوف بالله ، جريء على الله

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r11.claim: The world is adorned by scholars' knowledge, rulers' justice, worshipers' devotion, merchants' trust, and artisans' counsel, while Satan places envy, injustice, ostentation, betrayal, and fraud beside them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r11.anchor: الدنيا بستان زينت بخمسة أشياء : علم العلماء وعدل الأمراء وعبادة العباد

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r12.claim: Hasan al-Basri's five virtues were practicing before commanding, abstaining before forbidding, giving knowledge and wealth, self-sufficiency through knowledge, and matching private conduct to public conduct.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r12.anchor: فضل الحسن البصري على التابعين بخمسة أشياء : أولها : لم يأمر أحدا بشيء حتى عمله

RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r13.claim: To test whether knowledge benefits you, examine yourself for five qualities, which the next passage specifies.
RAZI-FULL:v2p167#2/r13.anchor: إذا أردت أن تعلم أن علمك ينفعك أم لا فاطلب من نفسك خمس خصال

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r1.claim: Beneficial knowledge is marked by loving modest means, obedience for reward, worldly renunciation for leisure, wisdom for a sound heart, and solitude for communion with God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r1.anchor: حب الفقر لقلة المؤنة ، وحب الطاعة طلبا للثواب ، وحب الزهد في الدنيا طلبا للفراغ

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r2.claim: Seek honor in humility rather than wealth or lineage.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r2.anchor: أطلب العز في التواضع لا في المال والعشيرة

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r3.claim: Seek riches in contentment rather than abundance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r3.anchor: أطلب الغنى في القناعة لا في الكثرة

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r4.claim: Seek security in paradise rather than worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r4.anchor: أطلب الأمن في الجنة لا في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r5.claim: Seek rest in having little rather than much.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r5.anchor: اطلب الراحة في القلة لا في الكثرة

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r6.claim: Seek knowledge's benefit in practice rather than abundant transmission.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r6.anchor: أطلب منفعة العلم في العمل لا في كثرة الرواية

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r7.speaker: ابن المبارك
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r7.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak says the community's corruption comes through five elite groups: scholars, warriors, ascetics, merchants, and rulers, whose failures deprive others of sound examples.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r7.anchor: قال ابن المبارك ما جاء فساد هذه الأمة إلا من قبل الخواص وهم خمسة

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r8.speaker: ابن المبارك
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r8.claim: Scholars inherit from prophets; if they serve religion poorly while pursuing wealth, ignorant people have no model to follow.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r8.anchor: فإذا كان العالم للدين واضعا وللمال رافعا فبمن يقتدي الجاهل

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r9.speaker: ابن المبارك
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r9.claim: Ascetics are the earth's supports; if they desire worldly life, repentant people lose their example.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r9.anchor: وإذا كان الزاهد في الدنيا راغبا فبمن يقتدي التائب

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r10.speaker: ابن المبارك
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r10.claim: Warriors are God's troops on earth; if they are greedy and ostentatious, they cannot prevail against the enemy.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r10.anchor: وإذا كان الغازي طامعا مرائيا فكيف يظفر بالعدو .

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r11.speaker: ابن المبارك
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r11.claim: Merchants are God's trustees on earth; if they betray, trust cannot be maintained.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r11.anchor: وإذا كان التاجر خائنا فكيف تحصل الأمانة

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r12.speaker: ابن المبارك
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r12.claim: Rulers are shepherds; if a shepherd becomes a wolf, governance fails.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r12.anchor: وإذا كان الراعي ذئبا فكيف تحصل الرعاية

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r13.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r13.claim: Ali says knowledge is the prophets' inheritance, whereas wealth is inherited from Pharaohs.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r13.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه : العلم أفضل من / المال

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r14.claim: Knowledge does not diminish when spent, whereas wealth does.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r14.anchor: الثاني : العلم لا ينقص بالنفقة والمال ينقص

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r15.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r15.claim: Wealth needs a guard, while knowledge protects its possessor.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r15.anchor: الثالث : يحتاج المال إلى الحافظ والعلم يحفظ صاحبه

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r16.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r16.claim: A dead person's wealth remains behind, while knowledge enters the grave with its owner.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r16.anchor: الرابع : إذا مات الرجل يبقى ماله والعلم يدخل مع صاحبه قبره

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r17.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r17.claim: Believers and unbelievers may obtain wealth, but only believers obtain knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r17.anchor: الخامس : المال يحصل للمؤمن والكافر والعلم لا يحصل إلا للمؤمن

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r18.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r18.claim: Everyone needs knowledgeable people for religion, while no one needs the wealthy for that purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r18.anchor: السادس : جميع الناس يحتاجون إلى صاحب العلم في أمر دينهم ولا يحتاجون إلى صاحب المال

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r19.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r19.claim: Knowledge helps a person cross the bridge, while wealth impedes him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r19.anchor: السابع : العلم يقوي الرجل على المرور على الصراط والمال يمنعه

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r20.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r20.claim: Abu al-Layth says even a person unable to retain a scholar's lesson receives seven honors by sitting with scholars.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r20.anchor: قال الفقيه أبو الليث : إن من يجلس عند العالم ولا يقدر أن يحفظ من ذلك العلم شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r21.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r21.claim: Such a listener gains the merit of learners.

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r22.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r22.claim: While seated with the scholar, the listener is restrained from sins.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r22.anchor: ما دام جالسا عنده كان محبوسا عن الذنوب

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r23.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r23.claim: Mercy descends on the person who leaves home seeking knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r23.anchor: إذا خرج من منزله طلبا للعلم نزلت الرحمة عليه

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r24.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r24.claim: A listener shares in the mercy that descends upon a study circle.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r24.anchor: إذا جلس في حلقة العلم فإذا نزلت الرحمة عليهم حصل له منها نصيب

RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r25.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r25.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r25.claim: Listening to the lesson is recorded as an act of obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168/r25.anchor: والخامس : ما دام يكون في الاستماع ، تكتب له طاعة

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r1.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r1.claim: The carried-over report says grief at failing to understand knowledge can lead a listener to God's presence, citing a saying about hearts broken for God.

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r2.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r2.claim: Seeing Muslims honor scholars and humiliate sinners turns a listener from sin and toward knowledge; hence the prophetic instruction to keep company with the righteous.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r2.anchor: يرى إعزاز المسلمين للعالم وإذلالهم للفساق فيرد قلبه عن الفسق

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r3.claim: An anonymous warning assigns seven levels of hell to scholars who hoard knowledge, resent correction, reserve learning for elites, scorn admonition, err in fatwas, mix falsehood with religion, or seek reputation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r3.anchor: قيل من العلماء من يضن بعلمه ولا يحب أن يوجد عند غيره فذاك في الدرك الأول من النار

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r4.claim: The second condemned scholar treats himself as a ruler and becomes angry when anyone challenges his right.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r4.anchor: ومن العلماء من يكون في علمه بمنزلة السلطان فإن رد عليه شيء من حقه غضب ، فذاك في الدرك الثاني من النار

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r5.claim: The third teaches rare knowledge only to wealthy and eminent people, deeming the poor unworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r5.anchor: ومن العلماء من يجعل حديثه وغرائب علمه لأهل الشرف واليسار ولا يرى الفقراء له أهلا

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r6.claim: The fourth is self-admiring, harsh when admonishing others and resentful when admonished.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r6.anchor: ومن العلماء من كان معجبا بنفسه إن وعظ عنف وإن وعظ أنف

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r7.claim: The fifth appoints himself to issue legal opinions and gives incorrect fatwas.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r7.anchor: ومن العلماء من ينصب نفسه للفتيا فيفتي خطأ

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r8.claim: The sixth learns the arguments of false teachers and mixes them into religion.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r8.anchor: ومن العلماء من يتعلم كلام المبطلين فيمزجه بالدين

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r9.claim: The seventh seeks knowledge to win people's regard.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r9.anchor: ومن العلماء من يطلب العلم لوجوه الناس فذاك في الدرك السابع من النار

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r10.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r10.claim: Abu al-Layth says company with eight groups increases eight traits, for good or ill.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r10.anchor: قال الفقيه أبو الليث : من جلس مع ثمانية أصناف من الناس زاده الله ثمانية أشياء

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r11.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r11.claim: Company with the rich increases love and desire for worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r11.anchor: من جلس مع الأغنياء زاده الله حب الدنيا والرغبة فيها

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r12.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r12.claim: Company with the poor fosters gratitude and contentment with God's allotment.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r12.anchor: ومن جلس مع الفقراء جعل الله له الشكر والرضا بقسمة الله

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r13.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r13.claim: Company with rulers increases hardness and pride.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r13.anchor: ومن جلس مع السلطان زاده الله القسوة والكبر

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r14.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r14.claim: Company with women increases ignorance and desire.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r14.anchor: ومن جلس مع النساء زاده الله الجهل والشهوة

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r15.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r15.claim: Company with children increases amusement and joking.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r15.anchor: ومن جلس مع الصبيان ازداد من اللهو والمزاح

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r16.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r16.claim: Company with sinners increases boldness in sin and postponement of repentance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r16.anchor: ومن جلس مع الفساق ازداد من الجرأة على الذنوب وتسويف التوبة

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r17.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r17.claim: Company with the righteous increases desire for obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r17.anchor: ومن جلس مع الصالحين ازداد رغبة في الطاعات

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r18.speaker: الفقيه أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r18.claim: Company with scholars increases knowledge and piety.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r18.anchor: ومن جلس مع العلماء ازداد العلم والورع

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r19.claim: God granted seven people distinct forms of knowledge, linking Adam with names, Khidr with divinely granted knowledge, Joseph with dream interpretation, David with armor-making, Solomon with birds' speech, Jesus with Torah and Gospel, and Muhammad with law and monotheism.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r19.anchor: إن الله علم سبعة نفر سبعة أشياء ( ا ) علم آدم الأسماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r20.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r20.claim: Adam's knowledge of names brought him the angels' prostration and greeting.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r20.anchor: فعلم آدم كان سببا له في حصول السجدة والتحية

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r21.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r21.claim: Khidr's knowledge led to Moses and Joshua becoming his students.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r21.anchor: وعلم الخضر كان سببا لأن وجد تلميذا مثل موسى ويوشع

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r22.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r22.claim: Joseph's knowledge led him to find his family and kingdom.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r22.anchor: وعلم يوسف كان سببا لوجدان الأهل والمملكة

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r23.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r23.claim: David's knowledge led him to leadership and rank.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r23.anchor: وعلم داود كان سببا لوجدان الرياسة والدرجة

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r24.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r24.claim: Solomon's knowledge led him to Bilqis and victory.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r24.anchor: وعلم سليمان كان سببا لوجدان بلقيس والغلبة

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r25.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r25.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r25.claim: Jesus' knowledge removed suspicion from his mother.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r25.anchor: وعلم عيسى كان سببا لزوال التهمة عن أمه

RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r26.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r26.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r26.claim: Muhammad's knowledge led to his intercession.
RAZI-FULL:v2p168#2/r26.anchor: وعلم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم كان سببا لوجود الشفاعة

RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r1.claim: If knowledge of created beings earns the angels' greeting, knowledge of the Creator and His attributes should earn the Lord's greeting, cited as 36:58.
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r1.anchor: بل يجد تحية الرب { سلام قولا من رب رحيم } ( يس : 58 ) والخضر وجد بعلم الفراسة

RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r2.claim: As Khidr's insight won Moses' company, the community's knowledge of spiritual reality should win the Prophet's company in the afterlife, citing 4:69.
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r2.anchor: والخضر وجد بعلم الفراسة صحبة موسى ، فيا أمة الحبيب بعلم الحقيقة كيف لا تجدون صحبة محمد

RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r3.claim: Joseph's dream interpretation saved him from worldly imprisonment; interpreters of God's book should likewise escape the prison of desires through divine guidance, citing 10:25.
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r3.anchor: ويوسف بتأويل الرؤيا نجا من حبس الدنيا ، فمن كان عالما بتأويل كتاب الله كيف لا ينجو من حبس الشهوات

RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r4.claim: As Joseph acknowledged God's gift of dream interpretation, scholars should acknowledge the gift of interpreting scripture and their roles as God's namesake, prophetic heir, caller, teacher, lamp, guide, and warner.
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r4.anchor: فأنت يا عالم أما تذكر منة الله على نفسك حيث علمك تفسير كتابه

RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r5.speaker: الحديث
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r5.claim: The passage cites a hadith saying scholars are leaders, jurists guides, and sitting with them increases one.
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r5.anchor: كما جاء في الحديث : العلماء سادة والفقهاء قادة ومجالستهم زيادة

RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r6.claim: A believer needs knowledge to perform obligatory duties.
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r6.anchor: إن الله أمرني بأداء الفرائض وأنا لا أقدر على أدائها إلا بالعلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r7.claim: A believer needs knowledge to avoid sins.
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r7.anchor: نهاني عن المعاصي وأنا لا أقدر على اجتنابها إلا بالعلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r8.claim: A believer needs knowledge to give thanks for God's blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r8.anchor: أوجب على شكر نعمه ولا أقدر عليه إلا بالعلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r9.claim: A believer needs knowledge to deal fairly with other people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r9.anchor: أمرني بإنصاف الخلق وأنا لا أقدر أن أنصفهم إلا بالعلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r10.claim: A believer needs knowledge to be patient under God's trials.
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r10.anchor: أمرني بالصبر على بلائه ولا أقدر عليه إلا بالعلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r11.claim: A believer needs knowledge to oppose Satan.
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r11.anchor: أمرني بالعداوة مع الشيطان ولا أقدر عليها إلا بالعلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r12.claim: The paths to paradise are in the hands of scholars, ascetics, worshipers, and fighters; each receives a distinct divine gift when sincere in that role.
RAZI-FULL:v2p169/r12.anchor: طريق الجنة في أيدي أربعة : العالم والزاهد والعابد والمجاهد ، فالزاهد إذا كان صادقا

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r1.claim: Religion without piety remains at risk, and speech without deeds is wasted.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r1.anchor: فالدين بلا تقوى على الخطر ، والقول بلا فعل كالهدر

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r2.claim: Manliness without humility is like a fruitless tree; knowledge without practice is like a rainless cloud.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r2.anchor: المروءة بلا تواضع كشجر بلا ثمر ، والعلم بلا عمل كغيث بلا مطر

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r3.claim: Religion is completed by piety, speech by action, manliness by humility, and knowledge by practice; without them each is deficient.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r3.anchor: لا يتم الدين إلا بالتقوى ، ولا يتم القول إلا بالفعل ،

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r4.claim: Ali tells Jabir that the world stands through a learned scholar who practices, an ignorant learner who is not too proud to learn, a generous rich person, and a poor person who does not sell the afterlife for this world.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r4.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه لجابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري : قوام الدنيا بأربعة بعالم يعمل بعلمه

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r5.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r5.claim: Al-Khalil says the person who knows and knows that he knows is a scholar to follow.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r5.anchor: قال الخليل : الرجال أربعة رجل يدري ويدري أنه يدري فهو عالم فاتبعوه

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r6.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r6.claim: The person who knows but does not realize he knows is asleep and should be awakened.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r6.anchor: ورجل يدري ولا يدري أنه يدري فهو نائم فأيقظوه

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r7.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r7.claim: The person who does not know but recognizes his ignorance seeks guidance and should be guided.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r7.anchor: ورجل لا يدري ويدري أنه لا يدري فهو مسترشد فأرشدوه

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r8.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r8.claim: The person who neither knows nor recognizes ignorance is a devil to avoid.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r8.anchor: ورجل لا يدري ولا يدري أنه لا يدري فهو شيطان فاجتنبوه

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r9.claim: Even a noble ruler should rise for his father, serve his guest, serve his teacher, and ask knowledgeable people about what he does not know.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r9.anchor: أربعة لا ينبغي للشريف أن يأنف منها وإن كان أميرا : قيامه من مجلسه لأبيه

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r10.claim: When scholars pursue dubious income, ordinary people eat doubtful food; when scholars eat doubtful food, ordinary people eat forbidden food; when scholars deem forbidden things lawful, ordinary people disbelieve.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r10.anchor: إذا اشتغل العلماء بجمع الحلال حار العوام آكلين للشبهات ، وإذا صال العالم آكلا للشبهات

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r11.claim: Reason and appetite sort things into four classes: rationally welcome but unwanted, desired but irrational, welcome to both, or rejected by both; these correspond to hardship, sin, knowledge, and ignorance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r11.anchor: قسم يرضاه العقل ولا ترضاه الشهوة

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r12.claim: Knowledge is a present paradise and ignorance a present hell: both reason and appetite welcome knowledge and reject ignorance, so each person's choice rehearses the corresponding final abode.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r12.anchor: فينزل العلم من الجهل منزلة الجنة من النار

RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r13.claim: Pleasure is perceiving what one loves and pain perceiving what one dislikes; wounds hurt by separating body parts, while fire hurts more because it separates all parts.
RAZI-FULL:v2p170/r13.anchor: كمال اللذة في إدراك المحبوب وكمال الألم في البعد عن المحبوب

RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r1.claim: The deeper and stronger the cognition, and the nobler, purer, and more lasting its object, the greater its pleasure.
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r1.anchor: كلما كان الإدراك أغوص وأشد والمدرك أشرف وأكمل ، والمدرك أنقى وأبقى

RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r2.claim: Knowledge belongs to the spirit, nobler than the body, and rational cognition is profound; its subject includes God, creation, and divine rulings.
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r2.anchor: ولا شك أن محل العلم هو الروح وهو أشرف من البدن ولا شك أن الإدراك العقلي أغوص

RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r3.claim: Because knowledge's objects include God, all creatures, and divine commands, nothing surpasses knowledge's perfection and pleasure or ignorance's misery and loss.
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r3.anchor: فثبت أنه لا كمال ولا لذة فوق كمال العلم ولذاته ولا شقاوة ولا نقصان فوق شقاوة الجهل

RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r4.claim: Experience confirms that answering a scholarly question correctly brings joy, while ignorance causes shame, showing knowledge's pleasure and ignorance's misery.
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r4.anchor: فإن علمها وقدر على الجواب والصواب فيها فرح بذلك وابتهج به ، وأن جهلها نكس رأسه حياء

RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r5.claim: Razi adds scriptural proofs of knowledge's excellence that he had omitted earlier.
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r5.anchor: واعلم أن ههنا وجوها أخر من النصوص تدل على فضيلة العلم نسينا إيرادها قبل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r6.claim: The first revelation links humanity's lowly origin as a clot with its highest station as a knower; the progression shows knowledge is the noblest rank.
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r6.anchor: كنت أنت في أول حالك في تلك الدرجة التي هي غاية الخساسة فصرت في آخر حالك

RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r7.claim: The ordering of God's generosity with His teaching by the pen suggests that teaching knowledge is why He is called most generous; knowledge therefore surpasses other gifts.
RAZI-FULL:v2p171/r7.anchor: وقد ثبت في أصول الفقه أن ترتيب الحكم على الوصف مشعر بكون الوصف علة

RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r1.claim: The verse that only God's servants who are scholars fear Him supports knowledge's excellence: scholars are people of fear, and the fearful are promised paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r1.anchor: الثالث : قوله سبحانه : { إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء } وهذه الآية فيها وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r2.claim: Reason also shows scholars fear God: true fear requires knowing the object's power, awareness, and wisdom, illustrated by subjects who do not fear a king unless they know he sees and can punish wrongdoing.
RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r2.anchor: لا بد له من العلم بأمور ثلاثة . منها : العلم بالقدرة ، لأن الملك عالم باطلاع رعيته

RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r3.claim: Fear of God follows knowledge that He knows everything, can do all things, and rejects wrongdoing and forbidden acts.
RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r3.anchor: فثبت أن خوف العبد من الله لا يحصل إلا إذا علم بكونه تعالى عالما بجميع المعلومات ، قادرا على كل المقدورات ، غير راض بالمنكرات والمحرمات

RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r4.claim: Fear leads to paradise because faith makes immediate pleasure seem trivial beside future pain, causing one to flee sin, fulfill duties, and earn reward.
RAZI-FULL:v2p171#2/r4.anchor: صار ذلك الإيمان سببا لفراره عن تلك اللذة العاجلة ، وذلك هو الخشية

RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r1.claim: Razi argues the two verses imply that paradise is reserved for scholars: only scholars fear God, and paradise belongs to those who fear their Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r1.anchor: أن ظاهر الآية يدل على أنه ليس للجنة أهل إلا العلماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r2.claim: The verse is a severe warning: knowledge of God necessarily produces fear, so arguments that do not produce fear are blameworthy knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r2.anchor: أن العلم الذي هو سبب القرب من الله تعالى هو الذي يورث الخشية

RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r3.claim: An alternate reading nominates the first word and accusates the second, making God the subject of fearing scholars; Razi says this would exalt scholars, since they distinguish what is possible for God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r3.anchor: وثالثها : قرىء { إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء } برفعه الأول ونصب الثاني

RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r4.claim: God's command to the Prophet to ask for increased knowledge alone proves knowledge's preciousness and God's special love for it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى : { وقل * ربى * زدنى علما } ( طه : 114 ) . وفيه أدل دليل

RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r5.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r5.claim: Qatada says even Moses did not consider himself satisfied with knowledge, asking to follow his teacher to learn guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة : لو اكتفى أحد من العلم لاكتفى نبي الله موسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r6.claim: Although Solomon possessed vast worldly dominion, he took pride in knowing birds' speech, so believers may more fittingly take pride in knowing the Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r6.anchor: ثم إنه لم يفتخر بالمملكة وافتخر بالعلم حيث قال : { وقال ياأيها الناس علمنا منطق الطير

RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r7.claim: Solomon mentions knowledge of birds before saying they were given everything, and the account of David and Solomon likewise presents judgment and knowledge before worldly matters, proving knowledge's higher rank.
RAZI-FULL:v2p172/r7.anchor: ولأنه قدم ذلك على قوله : { وأوتينا من كل شىء } وأيضا فإنه تعالى لما ذكر كمال حالهم قدم العلم أولا

RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r1.claim: The hoopoe's confident correction of Solomon despite its weakness shows knowledge's honor: even a lowly learner gains a forceful voice before rulers.
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r1.anchor: فلولا أن العلم أشرف الأشياء وإلا فمن أين للهدهد أن يتكلم في مجلس سليمان

RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r2.claim: The Prophet's comparison of an hour's reflection with sixty years of worship favors reflection because it brings one to God, while worship brings one to God's reward; alternatively, heart-work outranks bodily action.
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r2.anchor: تفكر ساعة خير من عبادة ستين سنة

RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r3.claim: Prayer serves inward remembrance, so its end is nobler than its means; this supports the superiority of knowledge and reflection.
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r3.anchor: جعل الصلاة وسيلة إلى ذكر القلب والمقصود أشرف من الوسيلة

RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r4.claim: The Qur'an calls knowledge great and wisdom abundant good; al-Razi identifies wisdom with knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r4.anchor: فسمى العلم عظيما وسمي الحكمة خيرا كثيرا فالحكمة هي العلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r5.claim: The ordering of Quranic teaching before the other blessings signals that knowledge is superior to them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r5.anchor: فجعل هذه النعمة مقدمة على جميع النعم

RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r6.claim: Al-Razi says all revealed scriptures speak of knowledge's merit.
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r6.anchor: أن سائر كتب الله ناطقة بفضل العلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r7.speaker: الله تعالى
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r7.claim: A saying attributed to God in the Torah tells Moses to magnify wisdom, learn it, practice it, and share it to gain divine honor in this life and the next.
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r7.anchor: عظم الحكمة فإني لا أجعل الحكمة في قلب عبد إلا وأردت أن أغفر له

RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r8.speaker: الله سبحانه وتعالى
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r8.claim: A saying in the Zabur tells David to seek the pious, or scholars, or the wise; God will not destroy a people while one of these is among them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r8.anchor: حادثوا من الناس الأتقاء فإن لم تجدوا فيهم تقيا فحادثوا العلماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r9.claim: Piety depends on knowledge, and scholars must be rational though rational people may lack learning; intellect is seed, knowledge its tree, and piety its fruit.
RAZI-FULL:v2p173/r9.anchor: لأن التقي لا يوجد بدون العلم كما بينا أن الخشية لا تحصل إلا مع العلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r1.claim: A Gospel passage warns hearers who neglect learning, urges them to seek and practice knowledge, and describes knowledge as an advocate for its possessor before God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r1.anchor: ويل لمن سمع بالعلم فلم يطلبه كيف يحشر مع الجهال إلى النار

RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r2.claim: In a Gospel resurrection dialogue, God assures scholars that their hope for mercy is fulfilled and admits them to Paradise among His righteous servants.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r2.anchor: فيقول : فأني قد فعلت ، إني قد استودعتكم حكمتي لا لشر أردته بكم

RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r3.claim: Muqatil says the Gospel records God telling Jesus to honor scholars, whom God preferred above all creation except prophets and messengers.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن سليمان وجدت في الإنجيل . أن الله تعالى قال لعيسى بن مريم

RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r4.claim: Ibn Umar transmits God's assurance that He placed knowledge in scholars without intending to punish them and will admit them to Paradise despite their deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر قال قال عليه الصلاة والسلام يقول الله تعالى للعلماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة وابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r5.claim: In the Prophet's final Medina sermon, learning humbly and teaching God's servants for God's sake earns the highest reward and rank in Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r5.anchor: قال أبو هريرة وابن عباس : خطبنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطبة بليغة

RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r6.claim: Ibn Umar reports that those who convey knowledge to Muhammad's community seeking God's face will sit on jeweled golden pulpits without fear until entering Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r6.anchor: ابن عمر مرفوعا إذا كان يوم القيامة صفت منابر من ذهب

RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r7.speaker: عيسى ابن مريم
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r7.claim: Jesus describes Muhammad's community as learned sages, almost prophets in understanding, content with little provision and work, and admitted to Paradise through the testimony of faith.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r7.anchor: عن عيسى ابن مريم عليهما السلام : أن أمة محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام علماء حكماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r8.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r8.claim: The Prophet promises protection from Hell for dust-covered feet seeking knowledge, angelic prayers, and martyr status for one who dies while seeking it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174/r8.anchor: قال عليه السلام ( من اغبرت قدماه في طلب العلم ، حرم الله جسد على النار

RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r1.claim: The knowledge-seeker's grave is expanded and illuminated, while a scholar's sleep, study, breath, and tears are credited with worship, charity, and spiritual merit.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r1.anchor: وأربعين قبرا عن يساره ، وأربعين عن خلفه

RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r2.claim: The Prophet warns that insulting a scholar amounts successively to insulting knowledge, the Prophet, Gabriel, and God, who will humiliate the offender.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r2.anchor: فمن أهان العالم فقد أهان العلم ، ومن أهان العلم فقد أهان النبي

RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r3.claim: The most generous after Adam is a learned person who spreads knowledge for God and a fighter who dies in God's path; the scholar is raised alone as a community.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r3.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( ألا أخبركم بأجود الأجواد

RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r4.claim: The Prophet promises a path to Paradise for seeking knowledge and says Quran study in a mosque brings tranquility, mercy, angelic presence, and God's remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا ( من نفس عن مؤمن كربة من كرب الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r5.claim: The Prophet says prophets, scholars, and martyrs intercede on Judgment Day.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r5.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام ( يشفع يوم القيامة ثلاثة : الأنبياء ثم العلماء ثم الشهداء )

RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r6.speaker: الراوي
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r6.claim: The narrator places scholars at the highest rank between prophethood and martyrdom.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r6.anchor: قال الراوي : فأعظم مرتبة هي واسطة بين النبوة والشهادة

RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r7.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r7.claim: Muadh's report portrays learning as fear of God, worship, struggle, charity, guidance, and life for hearts; angels and creatures pray for scholars, whom God raises as leaders.
RAZI-FULL:v2p174#2/r7.anchor: معاذ بن جبل قال عليه الصلاة والسلام ( تعلموا العلم فإن تعلمه لله خشية

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r1.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r1.claim: After death, a person's work continues through ongoing charity, useful knowledge, or a righteous child praying for them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r1.anchor: إذا مات ابن آدم انقطع عمله إلا من ثلاث صدقة جارية ؛ أو علم ينتفع به

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r2.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r2.claim: When asked whom to approach for needs, the Prophet names Quran people, then scholars, then bright-faced people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r2.anchor: إذا سألتم الحوائج فاسألوها الناس قيل يا رسول الله ومن الناس

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r3.speaker: الراوي
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r3.claim: The narrator explains that 'people of the Quran' means those who memorize its meanings.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r3.anchor: قال الراوي والمراد بأهل القرآن من يحفظ معانيه

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r4.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r4.claim: The Prophet calls one who enjoins right and forbids wrong God's, His Book's, and His Messenger's deputy, and likens worldly life to poison taken in medicinal doses.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r4.anchor: من أمر بالمعروف ونهى عن المنكر فهو خليفة الله في أرضه وخليفة كتابه

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r5.speaker: الراوي
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r5.claim: The narrator includes scholars among those deputies because they explain what is forbidden and lawful.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r5.anchor: قال الراوي والعلماء داخلون فيه لأنهم يقولون هذا حرام فاجتنبوه وهذا حلال فخذوه

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r6.speaker: الخبر
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r6.claim: An unnamed report calls the scholar a prophet who has received no revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r6.anchor: في الخبر : العالم نبي لم يوح إليه

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r7.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r7.claim: The Prophet says one should be a scholar, learner, listener, or lover of learning, never a fifth kind who perishes.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r7.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام ( كن عالما ، أو متعلما ، أو مستمعا ، أو محبا

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r8.speaker: الراوي
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r8.claim: The narrator reconciles the two-people report by treating listeners and lovers as learners, so only the learned and those learning escape the category of worthless rabble.

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r9.speaker: أعراب
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r9.claim: An Arab advises his son to be a stealthy lion, a lurking wolf, or a vigilant dog, never an incomplete human being.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r9.anchor: كن سبعا خالسا أو ذئبا خانسا أو كلبا حارسا

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r10.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r10.claim: The Prophet promises emancipation for every step when someone leans on a scholar's hand and a good deed for every hair when kissing a scholar's head.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r10.anchor: من اتكأ على يده عالم كتب الله له بكل خطوة عتق رقبة

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r11.claim: The heavens and earth grieve when an honored person is humiliated, a rich person impoverished, or a scholar made a plaything by the ignorant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r11.anchor: برواية أبي هريرة ( بكت السموات / السبع ومن فيهن

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r12.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r12.claim: Quran bearers lead the people of Paradise, martyrs command them, and prophets are their masters.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r12.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : ( حملة القرآن عرفاء أهل الجنة والشهداء قواد أهل الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r13.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r13.claim: The Prophet calls scholars keys to Paradise and deputies of the prophets.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r13.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : ( العلماء مفاتيح الجنة وخلفاء الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r14.speaker: الراوي
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r14.claim: The narrator says scholars are metaphorical keys because their knowledge opens Paradise; dreaming of holding Paradise's keys signifies religious knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r14.anchor: قال الراوي الإنسان لا يكون مفتاحا إنما المعنى أن عندهم من العلم مفتاح الجنان

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r15.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r15.claim: A report assigns 999 of every 1,000 daily mercies to scholars, knowledge-seekers, and Muslims, leaving one for everyone else.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r15.anchor: إن لله تعالى في كل يوم وليلة ألف رحمة على جميع خلقه الغافلين

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r16.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r16.claim: In a dialogue with Gabriel, the Prophet ranks knowledge first, then looking at and visiting a scholar; knowledge sought for God and communal good guarantees Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r16.anchor: قلت يا جبريل أي الأعمال أفضل لأمتي ؟ قال : العلم ، قلت ثم أي ؟

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r17.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r17.claim: The Prophet names scholars and learners among ten people whose prayers are answered, alongside the virtuous, vulnerable, pilgrims, fighters, and others.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r17.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام ( عشرة تستجاب لهم الدعوة العالم والمتعلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r18.speaker: رسول الله
