RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r18.claim: The Prophet defines knowledge as a guide for action, intellect as a leader to good, desire as sin's mount, wealth as the arrogant's cloak, and the world as the afterlife's market.
RAZI-FULL:v2p175/r18.anchor: سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما العلم ؟ فقال : دليل العمل قيل : فما العقل

RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r1.claim: A man told that he had one hour left asks the Prophet for the best use of it, studies, and dies before sunset; al-Razi infers that learning must be the best deed.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r1.anchor: قال اشتغل بالتعلم فاشتغل بالتعلم ، وقبض قبل المغرب

RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r2.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r2.claim: A famous report says all people are dead except the learned.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r2.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( الناس كلهم موتى إلا العالمون

RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r3.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r3.claim: Anas reports seven continuing benefits after death, beginning with imparting knowledge; al-Razi says teaching leads because spiritual benefit outlasts bodily benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r3.anchor: عن أنس قال عليه الصلاة والسلام ( سبعة للعبد تجري بعد موته : من علم علما

RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r4.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r4.claim: A report says to sit with scholars when they move people from doubt to certainty, pride to humility, enmity to counsel, ostentation to sincerity, and desire to renunciation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r4.anchor: لا تجالسوا العلماء إلا إذا دعوكم من خمس إلى خمس

RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r5.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r5.claim: In counsel to Ali, the Prophet calls monotheism his capital, work his craft, prayer the delight of his eyes, remembrance his heart's vision, and knowledge his inheritance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r5.anchor: يا علي احفظ التوحيد فأنه رأس مالي والزم العمل فإنه حرفتي

RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r6.speaker: أبو كبشة الأنصاري
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r6.claim: In a four-person parable, the knowledgeable person who uses wealth rightly and the one who wishes to do likewise share reward; the ignorant rich and poor who wish to misuse wealth share blame.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176/r6.anchor: أبو كبشة الأنصاري قال ضرب لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مثل الدنيا مثل أربعة رهط

RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r1.speaker: كميل بن زياد
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r1.claim: Ali divides people into a Godly scholar, a learner on the path to salvation, and ignorant rabble; knowledge protects and grows when shared, while wealth dwindles, and knowledge remains a person's adornment and judge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r1.anchor: كميل بن زياد قال أخذ علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه بيدي فأخرجني إلى الجبانة

RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r2.claim: Umar says a sinner may leave a scholar's gathering repentant and sinless, and that no soil is more honored than scholars' gatherings.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r2.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه : إن الرجل ليخرج من منزله وعليه من الذنوب مثل جبل تهامة

RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Solomon chose knowledge over kingship and wealth, yet received knowledge and the kingdom together.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r3.anchor: عنم ابن عباس خير سليمان بين الملك والمال وبين العلم فاختار العلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r4.claim: Asked why Solomon used the hoopoe to find water, Ibn Abbas says it could see beneath the earth like glass; when challenged about covered traps, he answers that fate blinds sight.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r4.anchor: عن نافع بن الأرزق قال لابن عباس كيف اختار سليمان الهدهد لطلب الماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r5.claim: Abu Sa'id says 9,999 of Paradise's 10,000 portions belong to those who understood God's command through their intellect, and one to righteous poor believers.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخدري تقسم الجنة على عشرة آلاف جزء تسعة آلاف وتسعمائة وتسعة وتسعون

RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas advises his son to pursue good manners, which aid dignity and companionship, provide comfort and standing, and elevate the lowly.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس لولده يا بني عليك بالأدب فإنه دليل على المروءة

RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r7.speaker: الحسن البصري
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r7.claim: Hasan al-Basri says scholars' pen-scratching is glorification, writing and reading are worship, their ink resembles martyrs' blood, and they will be honored with the prophets.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r7.anchor: عن الحسن البصري : صرير قلم العلماء تسبيح وكتابة العلم والنظر فيه عبادة

RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r8.speaker: كتاب كليلة ودمنة
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r8.claim: Kalila wa-Dimna says scholars, rulers, and brothers must not be slighted: disrespecting each damages religion, worldly life, or personal honor respectively.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r8.anchor: في ( كتاب كليلة ) ودمنة : أحق من لا يستخف بحقوقهم ثلاثة : العالم والسلطان والإخوان

RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r9.speaker: سقراط
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r9.claim: Socrates says knowledge is superior because no one can serve it to you as they can other things, and nobody can take it from you.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r9.anchor: قال سقراط من فضيلة العلم أنك لا تقدر على أن يخدمك فيه أحد

RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r10.speaker: بعض الحكماء
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r10.claim: A wise man's retort says one may close the eyes, ears, or mouth, but cannot stop oneself from learning.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r10.anchor: قيل لبعض الحكماء لا تنظر فأغمض عينيه

RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r11.claim: A humorous legal anecdote says a learned thief, drinker, or adulterer could evade punishment by offering a legal-sounding excuse for the act.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r11.anchor: إذا كان السارق عالما لا تقطع يده لأنه يقول كان المال وديعة لي

RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r12.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r12.claim: One speaker urges reviving brothers' hearts with explanatory insight as vegetation revives dead land, since a soul distanced from desires and doubts is better than fertile soil.
RAZI-FULL:v2p176#2/r12.anchor: أحيوا قلوب إخوانكم ببصائر بيانكم كما تحيون الموات بالنبات والنواة

RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r1.speaker: الشاعر
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r1.claim: An unnamed poet equates ignorance with death before burial and says one not revived by knowledge has no resurrection; al-Razi uses the poem to praise learning.
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r1.anchor: وإن امرأ لم يحيى بالعلم ميت … وليس له حتى النشور نشور

RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r2.claim: Sin committed in ignorance seems unlikely to cease, while knowledge makes repentance possible: Adam sought forgiveness, whereas Satan persisted in error through ignorance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r2.anchor: انظر إلى زلة آدم فإنه بعلمه استغفر والشيطان غوى وبقي في غيه أبدا

RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r3.claim: Joseph's minister defended him with a Quranic argument and thereby deserved a share in his kingdom; by analogy, defending true religion with proof merits God's favor.
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r3.anchor: إن كان قميصه قد من * دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين

RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r4.claim: A would-be royal servant is told to learn; once knowledge opens his eyes, he chooses service to God, realizing the true master is the Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r4.anchor: كنت أهلا لخدمتك حين لم ترني أهلا لخدمتك

RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r5.claim: Love of worldly life obstructs learning: a tiny object over the eye's dark surface blocks physical sight, so the whole world covering the heart's pupil blocks inward sight.
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r5.anchor: إذا وضعت على سواد عينك جزءا من الدنيا لا ترى شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r6.speaker: حكيم
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r6.claim: A sage traces knowledge from heart and seeking through study and debate, but debate alone is barren; knowledge joined to action bears an everlasting kingdom.
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r6.anchor: وإذا ظهر بالمناظرة فهو عقيم ونتاجه بالعمل

RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r7.claim: Al-Razi reads the ant's warning in 27:18 as exonerating Solomon: prophets are protected from sin, and any crushing would be inadvertent; the ant's knowledge wins leadership, so fuller knowledge merits leadership.
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r7.anchor: فقوله تعالى : { وهم لا يشعرون } إشارة إلى تنزيه الأنبياء عليهم السلام عن المعصية

RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r8.claim: As training makes a dog's impure catch pure, knowledge of God may purify souls naturally pure but stained by sin, turning the rejected into the accepted through divine mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r8.anchor: فههنا النفس والروح طاهرتان في أصل الفطرة إلا أنهما تلوثتا بأقذار المعصية

RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r9.claim: The heart rules the limbs because of knowledge, not strength, size, or sharpness; therefore knowledge is the noblest attribute.
RAZI-FULL:v2p177/r9.anchor: وإنما تلك الرياسة بسبب العلم فدل على أن العلم أشرف الصفات

RAZI-FULL:v2p178/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p178/r1.speaker: أبو يوسف
RAZI-FULL:v2p178/r1.claim: Abu Yusuf rejects amputation in a theft case: admitting to taking property proves liability but not theft, and a later theft admission cannot cancel that established liability.
RAZI-FULL:v2p178/r1.anchor: فقال أبو يوسف : لا قطع عليه

RAZI-FULL:v2p178/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p178/r2.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
RAZI-FULL:v2p178/r2.claim: Under threat from al-Hajjaj, Yahya ibn Ya'mar proves Hasan and Husayn descend from the Prophet: Jesus is counted among Noah's descendants despite having no human father, so maternal descent counts; al-Hajjaj releases him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p178/r2.anchor: وهو قوله : { ونوحا هدينا من قبل ومن ذريته * داوود * وسليمان }

RAZI-FULL:v2p178/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p178/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v2p178/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa argues that when a group accepts its chosen representative as imam, that imam's Quran recitation counts as theirs; his Medina interlocutors accept the logic.
RAZI-FULL:v2p178/r3.anchor: قالوا : لأنا رضينا به إماما فكان قوله قولا لنا

RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r1.claim: Al-Farazdaq escaped punishment by changing ضاع to ضاء, recasting a complaint that his poetry was lost at Khalisa’s door as praise of its radiance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r1.anchor: وإنما قلت : وخالصة من وراء الستر تسمع : فلقد ضاء شعري على بابكم … كما ضاء در على خالصة

RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r2.claim: Khalisa rewarded the poet with more than a million dirhams in jewelry; Sulayman bought the jewelry back and returned it to her.
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r2.anchor: فأتبعه سليمان بن عبد الملك حاجبه لما خرج من عنده حتى اشترى الحلي من الفرزدق بما ألف ورده على خالصة

RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r3.speaker: الربيع
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r3.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says Abu Hanifa rejects the separate exception that the caliph’s grandfather permitted.
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r3.anchor: هذا يعني أبا حنيفة يخالف جدك حيث يقول : الاستثناء المنفصل جائز وأبو حنيفة ينكره

RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r4.claim: Abu Hanifa answers the charge by arguing that if people could privately except themselves from a pledge, they could cancel allegiance after returning home.
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r4.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة هذا الربيع يقول ليس لك بيعة في رقبة الناس

RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r5.claim: Abu Yusuf conditionally upheld retaliation for a Muslim who killed a protected non-Muslim, requiring proof that the victim was paying jizya; without proof, the claim failed.
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r5.anchor: حتى تقوم البينة العادلة أن الذمي يوم قتله المسلم كان ممن يؤدي الجزية فلم يقدروا عليه فبطل دمه

RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r6.claim: Al-Ghadban’s reply وعليك السلام secured him safety from al-Hajjaj, illustrating the practical benefit of knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p179/r6.anchor: فقال له ما جواب السلام عليك ؟ فقال وعليك السلام ثم فطن الحجاح ، وقال : قاتلك الله يا غضبان

RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r1.claim: A poet escaped danger by parsing the final ر of أمير as accusative, making Shabib the caliph he was addressing rather than the caliph being named.
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r1.anchor: فقال : إنما قلت ومنا أمير المؤمنين شبيب ، بنصب الراء فناديتك واستغثت بك

RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r2.claim: Sulayman b. Kathir explained that his curse against Abu Muslim was spoken while looking at unripe grapes; Abu Muslim appreciated the excuse and forgave him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r2.anchor: ولكن في كرم كذا لما نظرت إلى الحصرم

RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa rules that the spouses can speak without breaking their mutual oaths, since the initial exchange about the oaths had already dissolved them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r3.anchor: أعاد أبو حنيفة الفتوى ، فقال من أين قلت ؟ قال : لما شافهته باليمين بعدما حلف كانت مكلمة

RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r4.speaker: سفيان
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r4.claim: Sufyan praises Abu Hanifa’s analysis as revealing a point of knowledge that everyone else had missed.
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r4.anchor: قال سفيان : إنه ليكشف لك من العلم عن شيء كلنا عنه غافل

RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa helps a man recover stolen goods despite his oath of silence by having neighbors identify suspects individually; the thief’s silence identifies him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r5.anchor: فقال لهم أبو حنيفة . هل تحبون أن يرد الله على هذا متاعه ؟ قالوا : نعم

RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa lends a young man the unaffordable bride-price and advises him to claim he will move away after the marriage, prompting the in-laws to seek a settlement.
RAZI-FULL:v2p180/r6.anchor: ثم قال له : بعد الدخول أظهر أنك تريد الخروج من هذا البلد إلى بلد بعيد

RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r1.claim: Abu Hanifa resolves the marriage dispute by suggesting the husband threaten to travel with his wife until her family repays the bride-price; a debt would then prevent her travel, so he accepts a settlement.
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r1.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة : الطريق أن ترضوه بأن تردوا عليه ما أخذتموه منه

RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r2.claim: Abu Hanifa advises a father to buy the slave girl himself and marry her to his son, so a divorce returns her to the father and the son’s attempted emancipation is ineffective.
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r2.anchor: فقال له أبو حنيفة : إذهب به معك إلى سوق النخاسين فإذا وقعت عينه على جارية فابتعها لنفسك

RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r3.speaker: الليث بن سعد
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r3.claim: Al-Layth says he admired Abu Hanifa’s quick response even more than its substance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r3.anchor: قال الليث : فوالله ما أعجبني جوابه كما أعجبني سرعة جوابه

RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r4.claim: Abu Hanifa answers a vow to have intercourse with one’s wife during Ramadan by advising the couple to travel, making daytime intercourse permissible for the traveler.
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r4.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة : يسافر مع امرأته فيطؤها نهارا / في رمضان

RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r5.claim: Al-Hajjaj tracks the thief of four thousand dirhams through a distinctive perfume and recovers the money for the victim.
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r5.anchor: من وجد منه ريح هذا الطيب فخذوه فإذا رجل له وفرة فأخذوه

RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r6.speaker: أبو يوسف
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r6.claim: Abu Yusuf resolves Harun al-Rashid’s problem with an oath not to sell, give away, or free a beloved slave by gifting half and selling half.
RAZI-FULL:v2p180#2/r6.anchor: فقال : يهب النصف ويبيع النصف ولايحنث

RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r1.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r1.claim: Muhammad b. al-Hasan tells Harun al-Rashid that his fear of God after sin entitles him to two gardens, citing the promise to whoever fears standing before his Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r1.anchor: فقلت له يا أمير المؤمنين إذاوقعت في معصية هل تخاف الله في تلك الحالة أو بعدها

RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r2.speaker: أبو يوسف
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r2.claim: Abu Yusuf frees a slave girl from the caliph’s coercive oath by instructing her to confess when asked whether she stole the jewelry, then deny stealing it when asked to produce it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r2.anchor: قال أبو يوسف : قد صدقت يا أمير المؤمنين في الإقرار أو الإنكار

RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r3.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r3.claim: Shafiʿi defeats Bishr al-Muraysi’s objection that universal consensus cannot be known by asking whether he recognizes consensus on the caliph’s rule; Bishr concedes and falls silent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r3.anchor: فقال الشافعي : هل تعرف إجماع الناس على خلافة هذا الجالس ؟ فأقر به خوفا وانقطع

RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r4.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that whoever wishes to see him should look at al-Hasan and al-Husayn.
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r4.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : إذا أردتم أن تنظروا إلي فانظروا إلى الحسن والحسين

RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r5.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r5.claim: Ali says a person’s worth is measured by what he excels at.
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r5.anchor: فقال الحسين سمعت أبي عليا يقول قيمة كل امرىء ما يحسنه

RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r6.claim: Husayn attributes to his grandfather the maxim that generosity should be proportionate to the recipient’s knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r6.anchor: وسمعت جدي يقول : المعروف بقدر المعرفة

RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r7.claim: In Husayn’s test, the Bedouin names faith as the best deed, trust in God as rescue from ruin, and knowledge with forbearance as adornment; generosity, patience, or a lightning strike follow if those are absent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p181/r7.anchor: قال الأعرابي : الإيمان بالله . قال : فما نجاة العبد من الهلكة قال : الثقة بالله

RAZI-FULL:v2p182/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p182/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p182/r1.claim: Knowledge is intrinsically noble and beloved, while ignorance is intrinsically deficient: the learned are hurt by being called ignorant, and the ignorant pleased by false praise as learned.
RAZI-FULL:v2p182/r1.anchor: وكل ذلك دليل على أن العلم شريف لذاته ومحبوب لذاته والجهل نقصان لذاته

RAZI-FULL:v2p182/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p182/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p182/r2.claim: Knowledge naturally commands deference: animals check themselves before humans, ordinary people follow the more capable, and even the Prophet’s enemies were awed into submission; the cited poem says his bearing itself told his story.
RAZI-FULL:v2p182/r2.anchor: فلو لم تكن فيه آيات مبينة … كانت بداهتة تنبيك عن خبر

RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r1.claim: Human superiority over other animals comes from a divine, luminous faculty that enables grasping truths and worship, not from strength; humanity’s purpose is worship.
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r1.anchor: واللطيفة الربانية التي لأجلها صار مستعدا لإدراك حقائق الأشياء

RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r2.claim: The learned mind ranges across all categories and relations of being, and a knowledgeable soul can bring ignorant souls to knowledge, becoming complete and then perfecting others as an intermediary between God and people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r2.anchor: فإنها كانت كاملة ثم صارت مكملة وتصير واسطة بين الله وبين عباده

RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r3.claim: Exegetes interpret the Spirit sent with the angels and the Spirit revealed to Muhammad as knowledge or the Qur’an; just as a body without spirit is dead, spirit without knowledge is dead.
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r3.anchor: والمفسرون فسروا هذا الروح بالعلم والقرآن وكما أن البدن بلا روح ميت فاسد

RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r4.claim: Knowledge is the spirit of spirit and enduring happiness because universal conceptions do not decay or change.
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r4.anchor: فالعلم روح الروح ونور النور ولب اللب ومن خواص هذه السعادة أنها تكون باقية

RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r5.claim: Prophets were sent to call people to truth, using wisdom and clear insight as the Qur’an commands.
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r5.anchor: فالأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم ما بعثوا إلا للدعوة إلى الحق

RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r6.claim: In the exchange with the angels, God answers their concern about human corruption by saying He knows what they do not, setting knowledge itself as the relevant answer.
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r6.anchor: لما قال : { إني جاعل فى الارض خليفة } ( البقرة : 30 ) قالت الملائكة : { أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها }

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r1.claim: God answers the angels through knowledge rather than power, will, hearing, sight, or other attributes, showing knowledge’s superior rank among divine perfections.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r1.anchor: وإنما جعل صفة العلم جوابا لهم وذلك يدل على أن صفات الجلال والكمال

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r2.claim: God displayed Adam’s superiority by knowledge, then made him the object of the angels’ prostration and the deputy of the lower world; knowledge earned that distinction.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r2.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه إنما أظهر فضل آدم عليه السلام بالعلم وذلك يدل أيضا على أن العلم أشرف

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r3.claim: The angels’ glorification is praiseworthy only when joined with knowledge; without it, worship would be hypocrisy or blameworthy imitation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r3.anchor: فإنهما إن حصلا بدون العلم كان ذلك نفاقا والنفاق أخس المراتب

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r4.claim: Adam’s single ijtihadi error had grave consequences, which Razi treats as evidence of the great stakes and exalted rank of knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r4.anchor: إنما وقع عليه اسم المعصية لأنه أخطأ / في مسألة واحدة اجتهادية على ما سيأتي بيانه

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r5.claim: Through knowledge Adam repented, abandoned persistence and pride, and received the honor of divine election.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r5.anchor: ثم إنه ببركة جلالة العلم لما تاب وأناب وترك الإصرار والاستكبار وجد خلعة الاجتباء

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r6.claim: Abraham reasoned from the star to the moon and sun, reached the Creator through proof, and received God’s praise for his insight and argument.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r6.anchor: ولم يزل ينتقل بفكره من شيء إلى شيء إلى أن وصل بالدليل الزاهر والبرهان الباهر

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r7.claim: After learning about the Creator, Abraham sought knowledge of resurrection, then taught and argued with his father, his people, and the ruler of his time.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r7.anchor: ثم إنه عليه السلام بعد الفراغ من معرفة المبدأ اشتغل بمعرفة المعاد

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r8.claim: The careers of Salih, Hud, Shuʿayb, and Moses likewise show prophets learning, teaching, and directing people to examine evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r8.anchor: كيف كان اشتغالهم في أوائل أمورهم وأواخرها بالتعلم والتعليم وإرشاد الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r9.claim: God’s gifts to Muhammad include guidance and knowledge before material wealth; the sequence and the references to what he did not know exalt knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r9.anchor: فقدم الامتنان بالعلم على الامتنان بالمال

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r10.claim: Muhammad’s first revelation began with the command to read, and God then taught him what he had not known.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r10.anchor: ثم إنه أول ما أوحى إليه قال : { اقرأ باسم ربك } ( العلق : 1 ) ثم قال : { وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم }

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r11.claim: The Prophet would pray to be shown things as they truly are.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r11.anchor: وهو عليه الصلاة والسلام كان أبدا يقول : أرنا الأشياء كما هي

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r12.claim: The Qur’an dignifies knowledge by naming it life, spirit, and light.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r12.anchor: سمى العلم في كتابه بالأسماء الشريفة . فمنها : الحياة

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r13.claim: Talut’s selection over the people is supported by his greater knowledge and physical capacity, with knowledge named first.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r13.anchor: إن الله اصطفاه عليكم وزاده بسطة في العلم والجسم

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r14.claim: Joseph asks to manage the land’s storehouses on the basis of being trustworthy and knowledgeable, rather than lineage, eloquence, or beauty.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r14.anchor: وقال يوسف { اجعلنى على خزائن الارض إنى حفيظ عليم } ( يوسف : 55 ) ولم يقل إني حسيب نسيب فصيح مليح

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r15.claim: A reported saying locates a person’s distinction in the heart and tongue: speech uses the tongue, while combat uses the heart.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r15.anchor: جاء في الخبر ( المرء بأصغريه قلبه ولسانه ) إن تكلم تكلم بلسانه

RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r1.claim: The poet says a young man is half tongue and half heart, leaving only flesh and blood as the remainder.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r1.anchor: لسان الفتى نصف ونصف فؤاده … فلم يبق إلا صورة اللحم والدم

RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r2.claim: The Qur’an presents being veiled from God as a punishment before the punishment of Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r2.anchor: فقال : { كلا إنهم عن ربهم يومئذ لمحجوبون * ثم إنهم لصالوا الجحيم } ( المطففين : 15 ، 16 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r3.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r3.claim: Some say knowledge has three points of origin: a thinking heart, an expressive tongue, and an illustrative explanation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : العلوم مطالعها من ثلاثة أوجه ، قلب متفكر ، ولسان معبر

RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r4.claim: Ali offers a wordplay defining the letters of العلم through elevation, subtlety, and magnanimity.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r4.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه : ( عين العلم من العلو ، ولامه من اللطف

RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r5.claim: A list presented as ten sciences assigns practical purposes to theology, esoteric knowledge, social conduct, law, astronomy, combat, politics, dream interpretation, physiognomy, medicine, and divine reality.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r5.anchor: وأيضا قيل العلوم عشرة : علم التوحيد للأديان ، وعلم السر لرد الشيطان

RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r6.claim: A four-water analogy links kinds of knowledge to the Qur’anic water from heaven: theology to spring water, jurisprudence to a canal, asceticism to rain, and innovations to destructive floodwater.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r6.anchor: وأيضا قيل ضرب المثل في العلم بالماء قوله تعالى : { أنزل من السماء مآء }

RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r7.claim: Theology resembles spring water that should not be disturbed; seeking to know God’s manner risks unbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r7.anchor: علم التوحيد كماء العين لا يجوز تحريكه لئلا يتكدر

RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r8.claim: Jurisprudence resembles canal water that increases through digging, as legal understanding grows through inference.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r8.anchor: وعلم الفقه يزداد بالاستنباط كماء القناة يزداد بالحفر

RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r9.claim: Ascetic knowledge resembles clear rainwater that becomes clouded by air, as asceticism is clouded by greed.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r9.anchor: وعلم الزهد كماء المطر ينزل صافيا ويتكدر بغبار الهواء

RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r10.claim: Innovation resembles a flood that kills living things and destroys people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184/r10.anchor: وعلم البدع كماء السيل يميت الأحياء ويهلك الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r1.claim: Al-Ashʿari defines knowledge as that by which one knows, or that which makes an essence knowing.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الأشعري العلم ما يعلم به وربما قال ما يصير الذات به عالما

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r2.claim: Razi reports the objection that al-Ashʿari’s definition is circular because knower and known are understood only through knowledge, then gives al-Ashʿari’s reply from immediate self-knowledge of knowing, pain, and pleasure.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r2.anchor: واعترضوا عليه بأن العالم والمعلوم لا يعرفان إلا بالعلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r3.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr defines knowledge as knowing an object as it is, or simply as maʿrifa.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r3.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر العلم معرفة المعلوم على ما هو عليه وربما قال العلم هو المعرفة

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r4.claim: Razi objects that defining knowledge as knowing the known is circular, and that “as it is” adds nothing after saying knowledge conforms to the object.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r4.anchor: والاعتراض على الأول أن قوله معرفة المعلوم تعريف العلم بالمعلوم فيعود الدور أيضا

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r5.claim: Razi rejects identifying knowledge with maʿrifa as tautological; maʿrifa follows ambiguity and cannot describe God because it presupposes prior ignorance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r5.anchor: وثالثها : أن الله تعالى يوصف بأنه عالم ولا يوصف بأنه عارف لأن المعرفة تستدعي سبق الجهل

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r6.speaker: الأستاذ أبو إسحاق الإسفرايني
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r6.claim: Al-Isfarayini defines knowledge as disclosing the known, making realities manifest, or simply clarification.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r6.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو إسحاق الإسفرايني : العلم تبيين المعلوم وربما قال إنه استبانة الحقائق

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r7.claim: Razi says clarification is merely a harder word substituted for knowledge, and disclosure after obscurity does not apply to God; the fuller definition inherits al-Qadi’s objections.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r7.anchor: وهو أيضا ضعيف أما قول العلم هو التبيين فليس فيه إلا تبديل لفظ بلفظ أخفى منه

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r8.speaker: الأستاذ أبو بكر بن فورك
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r8.claim: Ibn Furak defines knowledge as that which enables its possessor to perform and perfect an act.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r8.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو بكر بن فورك : العلم ما يصح من المتصف به / إحكام الفعل وإتقانه

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r9.claim: Razi objects that this account cannot cover knowledge of necessary truths or impossibilities, which do not produce perfected action.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r9.anchor: لأن العلم بوجوب الواجبات وامتناع الممتنعات لا يفيد الأحكام

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r10.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r10.claim: Al-Qaffal defines knowledge as affirming the known as it is, or conceiving the known as it is.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r10.anchor: وقال القفال : العلم إثبات المعلوم على ما هو به وربما قيل العلم تصور المعلوم

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r11.claim: Razi says the objections already given apply to al-Qaffal’s formulations as well.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r11.anchor: والوجوه السالفة متوجهة على هذه العبارة

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r12.speaker: إمام الحرمين
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r12.claim: Al-Juwayni sorts belief into certain or uncertain: matching certainty is immediate, theoretical, or unsupported imitation; false certainty is ignorance; equal uncertainty is doubt, while its stronger and weaker sides are expectation and illusion.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r12.anchor: وقال إمام الحرمين : الطريق إلى تصور ماهية العلم وتميزها عن غيرها أن نقول إنا نجد من أنفسنا

RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r13.claim: Razi says al-Juwayni’s account is flawed in several respects, with the specific objections deferred beyond this excerpt.
RAZI-FULL:v2p184#2/r13.anchor: واعلم أن هذا التعريف مختل من وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r1.claim: Rāzī rejects a definition that presupposes intuitive knowledge of belief: if belief’s essence is self-evident, the same could be said of knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r1.anchor: أن هذا التعريف لا يتم إلا إذا ادعينا أن علمنا بماهية الإعتقاد علم بديهي

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r2.claim: Defining knowledge as absence of its opposites fails because those opposites are no clearer than knowledge, making the account circular or more obscure.
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r2.anchor: أن هذا تعريف العلم بانتفاء أضداده وليست معرفة هذه الأضداد أقوى من معرفة العلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r3.claim: Knowledge includes conception as well as assent, but conception admits no certainty, doubt, strength, or weakness, so this definition excludes it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r3.anchor: أن العلم قد يكون تصورا وقد يكون تصديقا والتصور لا يتطرق إليه الجزم ولا التردد ولا القوة ولا الضعف

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r4.claim: The Muʿtazila define knowledge as belief that produces tranquility of the soul, or simply whatever produces that tranquility; they treat “tranquility” as an intelligible metaphor.
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r4.anchor: العلم هو الإعتقاد المقتضى سكون النفس وربما قالوا العلم ما يقتضي سكون النفس

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r5.speaker: الأصحاب
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r5.claim: Rāzī’s associates object that belief is a genus distinct from knowledge, so knowledge cannot be defined as a kind of belief.
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r5.anchor: الإعتقاد جنس مخالف للعلم فلا يجوز جعل العلم منه

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r6.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r6.claim: The Muʿtazila can answer that belief and knowledge share a common element, which is what their definition means by belief.
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r6.anchor: لا شك أن بين العلم واعتقاد المقلد قدرا مشتركا فنحن نعني بالاعتقاد ذلك القدر

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r7.speaker: الأصحاب
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r7.claim: Rāzī’s associates say the tranquility definition also excludes God’s knowledge, since it cannot be described as producing tranquility of a soul.
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r7.anchor: وهذا التعريف يخرج عنه أيضا علم الله تعالى فإنه لا يجوز أن يقال فيه إنه يقتضي سكون النفس

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r8.speaker: الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r8.claim: The philosophers define knowledge as a form present in the soul that corresponds to the known object.
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r8.anchor: العلم صورة حاصلة في النفس مطابقة للمعلوم

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r9.claim: Calling knowledge a “form” is metaphorical and needs clarification: if a mountain itself exists in the mind, that is impossible; if only its image exists, the image rather than the mountain is known.
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r9.anchor: إذا عقلنا الجبل والبحر فإن حصلا في الذهن ففي الذهن جبل وبحر وهذا محال

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r10.claim: The claim that a mental form corresponds to the known is circular.

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r11.claim: Correspondence cannot explain their abstract objects, such as second intelligibles and mental considerations, which may have no external existence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r11.anchor: المعلومات قد تكون موجودة في الخارج وقد لا تكون وهي التي يسمونها بالأمور الاعتبارية والصور الذهنية والمعقولات الثانية

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r12.claim: People know non-existent things, but correspondence requires two positive entities and therefore cannot relate an image to sheer non-being.
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r12.anchor: أنا قد نعقل المعدوم ولا يمكن أن يقال الصورة العقلية مطابقة للمعدوم

RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r13.speaker: الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r13.claim: Al-Ghazālī explains the philosophers’ account by comparing inner perception with sight: an image of the object enters the faculty, while its essence, not its physical body, is meant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p185/r13.anchor: حاول الغزالي إيضاح كلام الفلاسفة في تعريف العلم فقال إدراك البصيرة الباطنة نفهمه بالمقايسة بالبصر الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r1.speaker: الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r1.claim: In al-Ghazālī’s analogy, the human substance is like iron, intellect like a polished mirror, and the known object like the reflected image.
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r1.anchor: جوهر الآدمي كالحديد وعقله كالصقالة والمعلوم كالصورة

RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r2.claim: Rāzī rejects defining sight as an image impressed in the visual faculty because the definition invokes both the one who sees and the object seen.
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r2.anchor: أنه ذكر في تعريف الأبصار المبصر والباصر وهو دور

RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r3.claim: If sight were the imprint itself, a tiny faculty could not contain an image as large as what is seen; even if a small image is only a condition, that condition differs from seeing.
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r3.anchor: لما أبصرنا إلا بمقدار نقطة الناظر لاستحالة انطباع العظيم في الصغير

RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r4.claim: We see an object where it is; if we saw only its impressed image, we would see it at the image’s location instead.
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r4.anchor: أنا نرى المرئي حيث هو ، ولو كان المرئي هو الصورة المنطبعة لما رأيته في حيزه ومكانه

RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r5.claim: If the mental image of heat has heat’s essence, the intellect becomes hot when thinking of heat; if it does not, the mind has not grasped heat’s essence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r5.anchor: إما أن تكون مساوية للحرارة في الماهية أو لا تكون

RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r6.claim: Rāzī says leading philosophers agree that an object’s image is not imprinted in a mirror, so al-Ghazālī’s explanation fits neither their position nor their principles.
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r6.anchor: اتفق المحققون من الفلاسفة على أن صورة المرئي لا تنطبع في المرآة

RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r7.claim: Failure to define knowledge can result either from the subject being too obscure or from its being so evident that nothing clearer can define it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r7.anchor: العجز عن التعريف قد يكون لخفاء المطلوب جدا وقد يكون لبلوغه في الجلاء

RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r8.claim: Knowledge’s essence is self-evident: everyone necessarily knows that they exist and that they are neither in the sky nor in the depths of the sea.
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r8.anchor: كل أحد يعلم بالضرورة أنه يعلم وجود نفسه وأنه يعلم أنه ليس على السماء ولا في لجة البحر

RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r9.claim: Knowing a relation entails knowing both its terms; necessary knowledge of such relations therefore makes knowledge’s essence immediately known and impossible to define.
RAZI-FULL:v2p186/r9.anchor: فلما كان العلم الضروري بهذه المنسوبية حاصلا كان العلم الضروري بماهية العلم حاصلا

RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r1.claim: Rāzī begins a discussion of thirty words thought to be synonyms for knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r1.anchor: في البحث عن ألفاظ يظن بها أنها مرادفة للعلم وهي ثلاثون

RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r2.claim: Idrāk literally means meeting or reaching; when the intellect reaches and grasps an intelligible essence, this is perception.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r2.anchor: القوة العاقلة إذا وصلت إلى ماهية المعقول وحصلتها كان ذلك إدراكا

RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r3.claim: Shuʿūr is perception without firm establishment, the first wavering arrival of knowledge in the intellect; God may be described as both perceiving and knowing.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r3.anchor: الشعور وهو إدراك بغير استثبات وهو أول مراتب وصول المعلوم إلى القوة العاقلة

RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r4.claim: Taṣawwur is the intellect’s complete grasp of a meaning; the term derives from bodily “form,” by analogy with the mistaken idea that essences inhere in intellect as shapes in matter.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r4.anchor: التصور لفظ مشتق من الصورة ولفظ الصورة حيث وضع فإنما وضع للهيئة الجسمانية

RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r5.claim: Ḥifẓ is an acquired mental image made firm enough to recover if lost; God’s knowledge is not called preservation because it cannot weaken or be lost.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r5.anchor: إذا حصلت الصورة في العقل وتأكدت واستحكمت وصارت بحيث لو زالت لتمكنت القوة العاقلة

RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r6.claim: Tadhakkur is the mind’s attempt to retrieve a stored image after it has vanished; this seems paradoxical because a present image needs no recovery, while an unnoticed one cannot be sought.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187/r6.anchor: إذا حاول الذهن استرجاعها فتلك المحاولة هي التذكر

RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r1.claim: Dhikr is the return of an image after its disappearance; an unnamed poet’s line makes prior forgetting a condition, and speech is called remembrance because it brings meaning to mind.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r1.anchor: فالله يعلم أني لست أذكره … وكيف أذكره إذ لست أنساه

RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r2.claim: The command “remember Me” raises a dilemma: if addressed during forgetfulness the servant is unaware of it, but if after forgetfulness remembrance already exists and cannot be newly produced.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r2.anchor: فهذا الأمر هل يتوجه على العبد حال حصول النسيان أو بعد زواله

RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r3.claim: The analogous command to know that none is a deity but God concerns assent to monotheism, not conception, so the paradox does not apply as strongly as it does to remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r3.anchor: فاعلم أن المأمور به إنما هو معرفة للتوحيد وهذا من باب التصديقات

RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r4.claim: Rāzī answers that introspection confirms people can remember; knowing that capacity suffices for disciplined effort even though the process itself remains unknown.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r4.anchor: نجد من أنفسنا أنه يمكننا التذكر وإذا كان ذلك ممكنا كان ما ذكرته تشكيكا في الضروريات

RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r5.claim: Failing to grasp how one remembers reveals human limitation; God makes the most evident things mysterious so servants recognize their incapacity and glimpse divine secrets.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r5.anchor: سبحان من جعل أظهر الأشياء أخفاها ليتوصل العبد به إلى كنه عجزه ونهاية قصوره

RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r6.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r6.claim: One group distinguishes maʿrifa as knowledge of particulars from ʿilm as knowledge of universals.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r6.anchor: المعرفة إدراك الجزئيات والعلم إدراك الكليات

RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r7.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r7.claim: Another group calls maʿrifa conception and ʿilm assent, making maʿrifa higher because human assent to a Necessary Being is certain while grasping God’s essence exceeds human capacity.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r7.anchor: المعرفة التصور والعلم هو التصديق وهؤلاء جعلوا العرفان أعظم درجة من العلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r8.claim: On that account every gnostic is learned, but not every learned person is a gnostic; no human truly knows God because grasping His essence is impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r8.anchor: فإن أحدا من البشر لا يعرف الله تعالى لأن الاطلاع على كنه هويته وسر ألوهيته محال

RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r9.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r9.claim: A further account defines maʿrifa as recognizing a second apprehension of something as the same thing previously perceived.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r9.anchor: ثم أدرك ذلك الشيء ثانيا وعرف أن هذا المدرك الذي أدركه ثانيا هو الذي أدركه أولا

RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r10.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r10.claim: Some who hold souls pre-existed bodies say souls were drawn from Adam, confessed God’s lordship, then forgot Him through bodily darkness and recognize Him again upon release.
RAZI-FULL:v2p187#2/r10.anchor: إنها هي الذر المستخرج من صلب آدم عليه السلام وإنها أقرت بالإلهية واعترفت بالربوبية

RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r1.claim: Fahm is conceiving something from an interlocutor’s words; ifhām is the conveyance of meaning through wording to the listener’s understanding.
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r1.anchor: الفهم وهو تصور الشيء من لفظ المخاطب والإفهام هو اتصال المعنى باللفظ إلى فهم السامع

RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r2.claim: Fiqh is knowing a speaker’s purpose; Qur’an 18:93 describes Quraysh as barely understanding because their doubts and desires kept them from seeing the true benefits and aims of divine duties.
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r2.anchor: فقهت كلامك أي وقفت على غرضك من هذا الخطاب

RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r3.claim: ʿAql is knowledge of qualities such as good, evil, perfection, and deficiency: perceived benefits prompt action, harms prompt restraint, like a camel’s tether.
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r3.anchor: العقل وهو العلم بصفات الأشياء من حسنها وقبحها وكمالها ونقصانها

RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r4.speaker: بعض الصالحين
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r4.claim: When asked what intellect is, one righteous person answered that it is knowing which of two goods is better and which of two evils is worse; the rational person obeys God’s commands.
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r4.anchor: هو العلم بخير الخيرين وشر الشرين

RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r5.claim: Dirāya is knowledge reached through a kind of contrivance: arranging premises and using deliberation; its derivation evokes training with a hunting spear and a tool for grooming hair.
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r5.anchor: المعرفة الحاصلة بضرب من الحيل وهو تقديم المقدمات واستعمال الروية

RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r6.claim: Dirāya cannot be attributed to God because thought and contrivance are impossible for Him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r6.anchor: وهذا لا يصح إطلاقه على الله تعالى لامتناع الفكر والحيل عليه تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r7.claim: Ḥikma can mean sound knowledge or righteous action, but is more specific to practical than theoretical knowledge and more commonly used for action; God’s wisdom creates benefits and welfare.
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r7.anchor: وهي اسم لكل علم حسن ، وعمل صالح وهو بالعلم العملي أخص منه بالعلم النظري

RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r8.claim: One definition of wisdom is knowing things as they truly are; it implies knowledge of essences is superior because particulars change while essences endure.
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r8.anchor: هي معرفة الأشياء بحقائقها ، وهذا إشارة إلى أن إدراك الجزئيات لا كمال فيه

RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r9.claim: Another definition calls wisdom performing an act whose outcome is praiseworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r9.anchor: هي الإتيان بالفعل الذي عاقبته محمودة

RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r10.claim: A further definition is imitating the Creator in governance as far as humanly possible: removing ignorance, injustice, stinginess, and foolishness from one’s knowledge, action, generosity, and forbearance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p188/r10.anchor: هي الاقتداء بالخالق سبحانه وتعالى في السياسة بقدر الطاقة البشرية

RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r1.speaker: قالوا
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r1.claim: Certainty requires believing something is so and that its opposite is impossible, based on either intuitive necessity or rational proof.
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r1.anchor: إن اليقين لا يحصل إلا إذا اعتقد أن الشيء كذا وأنه يمتنع كون الأمر بخلاف معتقده

RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r2.claim: The mind is the soul’s capacity to acquire knowledge not yet possessed; God creates the spirit ignorant, but for worship, which requires knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r2.anchor: استعداد النفس لتحصيل هذه المعارف هو الذهن

RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r3.claim: God provides the senses and thought to acquire knowledge: the text links hearing, sight, and reflection to Qur’anic signs and says their cooperation makes the ignorant spirit learned.
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r3.anchor: فإذا تطابقت هذه القوى صار الروح الجاهل عالما

RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r4.claim: Thought is the soul’s movement from present assents toward assents not yet brought to mind; one investigator likens it to supplication for knowledge from God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r4.anchor: إن الفكر يجري مجرى التضرع إلى الله تعالى في استنزال العلوم من عنده

RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r5.claim: Intuition is the soul’s readiness to find the middle term linking the two sides of an unknown; that term supplies two premises, like legal witnesses, from which the conclusion follows.
RAZI-FULL:v2p189/r5.anchor: فاستعداد النفس لوجدان ذلك المتوسط هو الحدس

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r1.claim: Dhakāʾ is exceptionally strong, perfected intuition reaching its highest degree: quick, penetrating arrival at truth; its etymology evokes fire, wind, and sharp slaughter.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r1.anchor: الذكاء وهو شدة الحدس وكماله وبلوغه الغاية القصوى

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r2.claim: Fiṭna is noticing something deliberately hinted at and is most often used for solving riddles and symbols.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r2.anchor: الفطنة وهي عبارة عن التنبه لشيء قصد تعريضه

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r3.claim: A khāṭir is the soul’s movement toward obtaining proof; strictly it is the content present in the mind, while the mind is called the thought by naming a container for what it holds.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r3.anchor: الخاطر وهو حركة النفس نحو تحصيل الدليل

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r4.claim: Wahm is a weaker belief, or judgment about particular non-sensible matters involving particular embodied beings, such as a lamb’s bond with its mother.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r4.anchor: الوهم وهو الإعتقاد المرجوح وقد يقال إنه عبارة عن الحكم بأمور جزئية غير محسوسية

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r5.claim: Ẓann is a preponderant belief that still allows its alternative; because belief’s strength is hard to measure, degrees of conjecture are likewise indistinct.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r5.anchor: ترجيح أحد طرفي المعتقد في القلب على الآخر مع تجويز الطرف الآخر

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r6.claim: Some commentators read “they think they will meet their Lord” as knowledge: worldly knowledge compared with the afterlife is conjecture, or true worldly knowledge is nearly confined to prophets and the truthful.

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r7.claim: Conjecture based on strong evidence is accepted and praiseworthy and underlies most practical judgments; weakly grounded conjecture is blameworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r7.anchor: وعليه مدار أكثر أحوال هذا العلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r8.claim: Khayāl is the image that remains from a sensed object after it is absent; it can appear in sleep or waking, while ṭayf is only used for sleep.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r8.anchor: الصورة الباقية عن المحسوس بعد غيبته

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r9.claim: Badīha is knowledge arising immediately in the soul without thought, such as knowing that one is half of two.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r9.anchor: المعرفة الحاصلة ابتداء في النفس لا بسبب الفكر كعلمك بأن الواحد نصف الاثنين

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r10.claim: Awwaliyyāt are the same as self-evident first principles: the intellect initially joins predicate to subject without an intermediary; with mediation, the middle term is primary.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r10.anchor: الذهن يلحق محمول القضية بموضوعها أولا لا بتوسط شيء آخر

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r11.claim: Rawiyya is knowledge reached after extensive thought.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r11.anchor: ما كان من المعرفة بعد فكر كثير

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r12.claim: Kiyāsa is the soul’s ability to infer what benefits it; the Prophet calls the discerning person one who reckons with himself and works for the afterlife, the greatest good.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r12.anchor: الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r13.claim: Khibra is knowledge acquired through experience; Abū al-Dardāʾ says he found people “akhbar taqillahu,” and another derivation compares it to a milk-rich she-camel.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r13.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء : وجدت الناس أخبر تقله

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r14.claim: Raʾy is the mind’s encompassing of premises expected to yield a conclusion, or the conclusion itself; opinion is to thought as a tool is to a maker.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r14.anchor: الرأي ، وهو إحاطة الخاطر في المقدمات التي يرجى منها إنتاج المطلوب

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r15.claim: Two proverbs warn against immature opinion and recommend setting opinion aside to reach the right result.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r15.anchor: إياك والرأي الفطير ، وقيل : دع الرأي تصب

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r16.claim: Firāsa infers inward character from outward signs; Qur’anic references validate the method, and its etymology suggests knowledge seized like a predator taking prey.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r16.anchor: الاستدلال بالحق الظاهر على الخلق الباطن ، وقد نبه الله تعالى على صدق هذا الطريق

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r17.claim: One kind of physiognomy arrives spontaneously without a known cause, as inspiration or revelation; the Prophet says there are inspired people in his community, including ʿUmar.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r17.anchor: إن في أمتي لمحدثين وإن عمر لمنهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r18.claim: A second kind is a learned craft that infers inward traits from visible forms; exegetes apply the two types to the “witness” in Qur’an 11:17.
RAZI-FULL:v2p190/r18.anchor: الاستدلال بالأشكال الظاهرة على الأخلاق الباطنة

STUDYQURAN:2:31/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r1.claim: Adam may derive from adīm, the earth's surface; a hadith links this to Adam's earthly origin and humanity's varied colors, temperaments, and fortunes.
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r1.anchor: Some derive Adam from adīm, meaning the surface of the earth, in keeping with the ḥadīth,

STUDYQURAN:2:31/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r2.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r2.claim: The names taught to Adam are ordinary words people use with one another, including man, sea, mountain, and kettle.
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r2.anchor: such as Ibn ʿAbbās, to be those that people use in discourse with one another, such as “man,” “sea,”“mountain,” and even “kettle.”

STUDYQURAN:2:31/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r3.speaker: Mujāhid
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r3.claim: Adam was taught the names of everything.
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r3.anchor: To others, such as Mujāhid, they are “the names of everything.”

STUDYQURAN:2:31/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r4.claim: Adam was taught the names of the angels.
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r4.anchor: Still others say he was taught the names of angels;

STUDYQURAN:2:31/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r5.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r5.claim: Adam was taught the names of all his progeny; al-Ṭabarī favors this because the pronoun hum suggests named humans or angels.
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r5.anchor: or that he was taught the names of all his progeny, which the commentator al-Ṭabarī prefers, in part because the pronoun hum is used rather than hāʾ,

STUDYQURAN:2:31/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r6.claim: The masculine plural pronoun usually refers to human or angelic persons, while nonpersons usually take a feminine singular pronoun, though 24:45 is an exception.
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r6.anchor: The plural of persons (human beings and angels) is the masculine plural, but the plural of other things (animals, inanimate objects) is usually expressed by the feminine singular pronoun, though this rule does not always hold

STUDYQURAN:2:31/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r7.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r7.claim: Adam learned all earthly languages, and his descendants gradually came to prefer one language over the others.
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r7.anchor: For al-Rāzī, this means that Adam indeed was taught all the languages of the earth, and his descendants came to prefer one over the others in the course of time.

STUDYQURAN:2:31/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r8.speaker: al-Ṭabrisī
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r8.claim: A comparable process of linguistic differentiation would have followed the flood.
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r8.anchor: The commentator al-ṭabrisī adds that a similar process would have taken place after the flood.

STUDYQURAN:2:31/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r9.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r9.claim: “Laid them before” can refer either to the names themselves or to the objects those names designate.
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r9.anchor: Laid them before refers either to the names themselves or to the objects named.

STUDYQURAN:2:31/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r10.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r10.claim: Being taught the names of things can mean being granted knowledge of all things.
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r10.anchor: For some, to be taught the names of things means to be given knowledge of all things.

STUDYQURAN:2:31/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r11.speaker: Ibn ʿArabī
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r11.claim: Ibn ʿArabī analogizes the angels' diverse functions and hierarchy to human spiritual and sensory faculties, each limited and unable to perceive what is above itself.
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r11.anchor: Ibn ʿArabī’s interpretation of this passage begins by pointing out that in relation to the world angels “are like the spiritual and sensory faculties” in human beings.

STUDYQURAN:2:31/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r12.speaker: Ibn ʿArabī
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r12.claim: Adam's synthetic reality let him know all the Divine Names; the angels lacked that synthesis and could not glorify God through Names they did not know, so Adam knew God in ways they could not.
STUDYQURAN:2:31/r12.anchor: Adam was capable of knowing all the Divine Names, unlike the angels who “did not possess the synthesis possessed by Adam, and were not aware of the Divine Names

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r16.claim: By focusing only on material origin, Iblis overlooks Adam’s ennoblement through God’s Hands, His Spirit, and exceptional knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r16.anchor: Iblīs’s argument, based purely on the original substance from which Adam was created, makes Iblīs blind to other ways in which God had ennobled Adam

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.claim: Eve enters without an account of her origin; although primordial Adam represents all humanity, male and female, the Quran does not explain how this Adam becomes the first couple.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.anchor: the Quran does not explicitly discuss the process by which this primordial Adam is differentiated into the first male and female

TAB-FULL:v1p511/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Angel of Death gathered sweet and salty earth to make Adam, explaining the name Adam as derived from the earth's surface.
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «بعث رب العزة ملك الموت، فأخذ من أديم الأرض من عذبها ومالحها، فخلق منه آدم

TAB-FULL:v1p511/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r2.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r2.claim: Ali says Adam was made from earth containing good and bad qualities, which are reflected among his good and bad descendants.
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r2.anchor: عن علي، قال: «إن آدم خلق من أديم الأرض فيه الطيب والصالح والرديء، فكل ذلك أنت راء في ولده الصالح والرديء

TAB-FULL:v1p511/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Adam was named for being created from the earth's surface.
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: «خلق آدم من أديم الأرض فسمي آدم

TAB-FULL:v1p511/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r4.speaker: أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r4.claim: Al-Suddi transmits a report from some Companions that the Angel of Death gathered soil of varied colors for Adam, explaining the diversity of his descendants and the name Adam.
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r4.anchor: عن ناس، من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن ملك الموت لما بعث ليأخذ من الأرض تربة آدم

TAB-FULL:v1p511/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r5.speaker: رسول الله
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r5.claim: The Prophet says Adam was created from a handful taken from all the earth, so his descendants vary in color, terrain, and good or bad qualities.
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r5.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن الله خلق آدم من قبضة قبضها من جميع الأرض

TAB-FULL:v1p511/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r6.claim: If Adam derives from أديم الأرض, al-Tabari treats Adam as a verbal proper name and says this formation explains why the name is indeclinable, like Ahmad and Asʿad.
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r6.anchor: يجب أن يكون أصل آدم فعلا سمي به أبو البشر، كما سمي أحمد بالفعل من الإحماد، وأسعد من الإسعاد

TAB-FULL:v1p511/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r7.claim: Al-Tabari explains Adam as reaching the earth's visible surface; أديم means its visible skin, and إدام is named for resembling the upper skin of its source.
TAB-FULL:v1p511/r7.anchor: وآدمتها وجهها الظاهر لرأي العين، كما أن جلدة كل ذي جلدة له آدمة، ومن ذلك سمي الإدام إداما

TAB-FULL:v1p515/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p515/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p515/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Adam learned familiar names used by people, including human, animal, land, plain, sea, mountain, and donkey.
TAB-FULL:v1p515/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " علم الله آدم الأسماء كلها، وهي هذه الأسماء التي يتعارف بها الناس: إنسان ودابة، وأرض، وسهل، وبحر، وجبل، وحمار

TAB-FULL:v1p515/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p515/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p515/r2.claim: Mujahid says Adam learned the name of every thing, with another report specifying the crow and pigeon.
TAB-FULL:v1p515/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: " في قول الله: {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} [البقرة: 31] قال: علمه اسم كل شيء

TAB-FULL:v1p515/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p515/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v1p515/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Adam learned the name of every thing, down to camels, cows, and sheep.
TAB-FULL:v1p515/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: «علمه اسم كل شيء، حتى البعير والبقرة والشاة»

TAB-FULL:v1p515/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p515/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p515/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the comprehensive teaching included a bowl, its diminutive form, and even terms for bodily functions.
TAB-FULL:v1p515/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: «علمه القصعة من القصيعة، والفسوة من الفسية»

TAB-FULL:v1p517/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r1.claim: Qatada says Adam named each class of creation and was guided to identify each thing with its own kind.
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r1.anchor: فأنبأ كل صنف من الخلق باسمه وألجأه إلى جنسه

TAB-FULL:v1p517/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r2.claim: Qatada says Adam learned every thing's name, such as mountain and sea, and God then presented those named things to the angels.
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: " في قوله: {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} [البقرة: 31] قال علمه اسم كل شيء: هذا جبل، وهذا بحر

TAB-FULL:v1p517/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say Adam named every thing, including horses, mules, camels, jinn, and wild animals.
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، وقتادة، قالا: " علمه اسم كل شيء: هذه الخيل، وهذه البغال، والإبل، والجن، والوحش

TAB-FULL:v1p517/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r4.claim: Al-Rabiʿ gives the concise interpretation that Adam learned the name of every thing.

TAB-FULL:v1p517/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r5.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r5.claim: Al-Rabiʿ also transmits the alternative view that Adam was taught the names of the angels.
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r5.anchor: عن الربيع: قوله: " {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} [البقرة: 31] قال: أسماء الملائكة

TAB-FULL:v1p517/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says Adam was taught the names of all his descendants.
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " في قوله: {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} [البقرة: 31] قال: أسماء ذريته أجمعين

TAB-FULL:v1p517/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r7.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that the names were of Adam's descendants and the angels, rather than all other kinds of creation.
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r7.anchor: قول من قال في قوله: {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها} [البقرة: 31] إنها أسماء ذريته وأسماء الملائكة

TAB-FULL:v1p517/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r8.claim: Al-Tabari argues that the masculine plural pronoun in عرضهم usually refers to human beings and angels; animals and other creation usually take feminine pronouns.
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r8.anchor: ولا تكاد العرب تكني بالهاء والميم إلا عن أسماء بني آدم والملائكة

TAB-FULL:v1p517/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r9.claim: Al-Tabari notes Arabic can use the masculine plural for mixed creatures, citing 24:45, so the broader interpretation remains possible.
TAB-FULL:v1p517/r9.anchor: فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين ومنهم من يمشي على أربع

TAB-FULL:v1p519/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p519/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p519/r1.claim: Al-Tabari maintains that prevalent Arabic usage supports names of humans and angels, while acknowledging that referring to all species with the masculine plural is valid.
TAB-FULL:v1p519/r1.anchor: الغالب المستفيض في كلام العرب ما وصفنا من إخراجهم كناية أسماء أجناس الأمم إذا اختلطت بالهاء والألف، أو الهاء والنون

TAB-FULL:v1p519/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p519/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p519/r2.claim: Al-Tabari notes variant recitations of the pronoun: Ibn Masʿud has feminine plural عرضهن, while Ubayy has feminine singular عرضها.
TAB-FULL:v1p519/r2.anchor: وقد ذكر أنها في حرف ابن مسعود: «ثم عرضهن» ، وأنها في حرف أبي: «ثم عرضها» .

TAB-FULL:v1p519/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p519/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p519/r3.claim: Al-Tabari suggests Ibn Abbas's interpretation of all names may reflect Ubayy's reading, which he says Ibn Abbas recited; that reading makes the interpretation linguistically sound.
TAB-FULL:v1p519/r3.anchor: ولعل ابن عباس تأول ما تأول من قوله: علمه اسم كل شيء حتى الفسوة والفسية على قراءة أبي فإنه فيما بلغنا كان يقرأ قراءة أبي

TAB-FULL:v1p520/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r1.claim: Al-Tabari explains عرضهم as presenting those bearing the names to the angels; on the received reading, the pronoun most strongly points to Adam's descendants and the angels, though the all-creatures reading remains possible.
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r1.anchor: ويعني جل ثناؤه بقوله: {ثم عرضهم} [البقرة: 31] ثم عرض أهل الأسماء على الملائكة

TAB-FULL:v1p520/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r2.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak reports from Ibn Abbas that God presented the names of all kinds of creation Adam had been taught.
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: " {ثم عرضهم على الملائكة} [البقرة: 31] ثم عرض هذه الأسماء

TAB-FULL:v1p520/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r3.speaker: أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r3.claim: Al-Suddi transmits from some Companions the view that God presented the created beings to the angels.
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r3.anchor: عن ناس، من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " {ثم عرضهم} [البقرة: 31] ثم عرض الخلق على الملائكة

TAB-FULL:v1p520/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says Adam's descendants were taken from his back and then presented to the angels.
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " أسماء ذريته كلها أخذهم من ظهره. قال: ثم عرضهم على الملائكة

TAB-FULL:v1p520/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r5.claim: Qatada says Adam learned each thing's name and God presented those names to the angels.
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: " {ثم عرضهم} [البقرة: 31] قال: علمه اسم كل شيء ثم عرض تلك الأسماء على الملائكة

TAB-FULL:v1p520/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r6.claim: Mujahid says God presented the bearers of the names to the angels.
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد: " {ثم عرضهم} [البقرة: 31] عرض أصحاب الأسماء على الملائكة

TAB-FULL:v1p520/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r7.claim: Mujahid also explains the presentation as showing the names of the pigeon and crow to the angels.
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {ثم عرضهم على الملائكة} [البقرة: 31] يعني عرض الأسماء الحمامة والغراب

TAB-FULL:v1p520/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r8.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r8.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say Adam named every thing, and the peoples were presented one group at a time.
TAB-FULL:v1p520/r8.anchor: عن الحسن، وأبي بكر عن الحسن، وقتادة، قالا: «علمه اسم كل شيء هذه الخيل وهذه البغال وما أشبه ذلك، وجعل يسمي كل شيء باسمه، وعرضت عليه أمة أمة»

TAB-FULL:v1p522/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p522/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p522/r1.claim: Al-Tabari defines أنبئوني as “inform me” or “tell me.”

TAB-FULL:v1p522/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p522/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p522/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses أنبئوني as asking the angels to tell him the names.
TAB-FULL:v1p522/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {أنبئوني} [البقرة: 31] يقول: أخبروني بأسماء، هؤلاء

TAB-FULL:v1p522/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p522/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p522/r3.claim: Al-Tabari cites al-Nabigha's use of أنبأه to mean that someone informed or made another know something.
TAB-FULL:v1p522/r3.anchor: وأنبأه المنبئ أن حيا … حلول من حرام أو جذام

TAB-FULL:v1p522#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p522#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p522#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says “these” refers to the named things Adam had just been told about.
TAB-FULL:v1p522#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج عن مجاهد: " {أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء إن كنتم صادقين} [البقرة: 31] يقول: بأسماء هؤلاء التي حدثت بها آدم

TABATABAI:2:30-32/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r6.speaker: author
